question: In what priestly town in the territory of Benjamin was Jeremiah born as the son of Hilkiah?
option1: Anathoth
option2: Shiloh
option3: Nob
option4: Gibeon
correct: Anathoth
explanation: Jeremiah originated from the priestly lineage of Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, a city assigned to the descendants of Aaron. Jeremiah 1:1 (KJV) - "The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin:"

question: In which regnal year of King Josiah did the word of the LORD first come to Jeremiah?
option1: The eighteenth year of his reign
option2: The thirteenth year of his reign
option3: The fifth year of his reign
option4: The twenty-first year of his reign
correct: The thirteenth year of his reign
explanation: Jeremiah received his prophetic calling in 627 BC, during the thirteenth year of the righteous Judean king Josiah. Jeremiah 1:2 (KJV) - "To whom the word of the LORD came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign."

question: What divine declaration establishes Jeremiah's prenatal consecration and universal prophetic appointment in Jeremiah 1:5?
option1: Behold, from the foundation of the world thy name was written in the book of life to preach repentance
option2: According to the covenant of thy fathers I have chosen thee to be a royal priest unto the house of Israel
option3: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations
option4: I have called thee by thy name from the womb of thy mother to declare my glory among the Gentiles
correct: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations
explanation: God revealed that Jeremiah's divine commission preceded biological conception, ordaining him not merely to Judah but as an emissary to the nations. Jeremiah 1:5 (KJV) - "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations."

question: What initial objection did Jeremiah raise when commissioned by the LORD in Jeremiah 1:6?
option1: O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send
option2: Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips
option3: Lord, I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue from my youth
option4: Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child
correct: Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child
explanation: Feeling overwhelmed by youthfulness and rhetorical inadequacy, Jeremiah pleaded his inability to speak before God touched his mouth. Jeremiah 1:6 (KJV) - "Then said I, Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child."

question: What sixfold mandate over nations and kingdoms was entrusted to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 1:10?
option1: To root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant
option2: To rebuke, and to judge, and to scatter, and to exile, to restore, and to bless
option3: To bind, and to loose, and to condemn, and to forgive, to establish, and to preserve
option4: To smite, and to break, and to burn, and to overthrow, to gather, and to sanctify
correct: To root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant
explanation: Jeremiah's prophetic task comprised four destructive verbs of judgment followed by two constructive verbs of restoration. Jeremiah 1:10 (KJV) - "See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant."

question: What Hebrew wordplay and theological meaning is conveyed by the vision of the rod of an almond tree (shaqed) in Jeremiah 1:11-12?
option1: The priesthood of Aaron is being renewed with flowering buds and sweet fruit
option2: God is diligently watching over (shoqed) His word to perform and hasten it without delay
option3: The northern kingdoms are blossoming into an empire that will crush Damascus
option4: The winter of divine judgment has passed and spring redemption has begun
correct: God is diligently watching over (shoqed) His word to perform and hasten it without delay
explanation: The almond tree ('shaqed', the 'awake/hastening tree' that blooms first in spring) serves as an auditory pun denoting that Yahweh watches over ('shoqed') His word to perform it. Jeremiah 1:11-12 (KJV) - "Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Jeremiah, what seest thou? And I said, I see a rod of an almond tree. Then said the LORD unto me, Thou hast well seen: for I will hasten my word to perform it."

question: What did the vision of the seething pot facing toward the north symbolize in Jeremiah 1:13-14?
option1: The famine and boiling thirst that would consume Samaria during a three-year siege
option2: The burning wrath of the false prophets stirring up rebellion against Babylon
option3: Calamity and scalding military invasion boiling over from northern kingdoms upon all inhabitants of the land
option4: The sacrificial offerings of Jerusalem being overturned by Egyptian cavalry
correct: Calamity and scalding military invasion boiling over from northern kingdoms upon all inhabitants of the land
explanation: A boiling cauldron tilted toward the south depicted Babylonian and allied armies erupting through the northern invasion corridor. Jeremiah 1:13-14 (KJV) - "And the word of the LORD came unto me the second time, saying, What seest thou? And I said, I see a seething pot; and the face thereof is toward the north. Then the LORD said unto me, Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land."

question: Where will the invading kings of the north set their thrones when they besiege Judah according to Jeremiah 1:15?
option1: Upon the summit of the Mount of Olives
option2: Within the holy courts of Solomon's temple
option3: Beside the pool of Siloam in the King's Dale
option4: At the entering of the gates of Jerusalem
correct: At the entering of the gates of Jerusalem
explanation: Invading monarchs would establish their judicial and command pavilions directly at the gateway portals of Jerusalem. Jeremiah 1:15 (KJV) - "For, lo, I will call all the families of the kingdoms of the north, saith the LORD; and they shall come, and they shall set every one his throne at the entering of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all the walls thereof round about, and against all the cities of Judah."

question: What three architectural and military metaphors describe the supernatural resilience God granted Jeremiah against his adversaries in Jeremiah 1:18?
option1: A defenced city, an iron pillar, and brasen walls
option2: A shield of gold, a flaming sword, and an unshakeable rock
option3: A royal fortress, a horned altar, and an ivory palace
option4: A tall cedar, an armored chariot, and a watchman's tower
correct: A defenced city, an iron pillar, and brasen walls
explanation: God fortified His young prophet into an invincible defensive redoubt: a fortified city, an iron support pillar, and bronze battlements against the entire social order. Jeremiah 1:18 (KJV) - "For, behold, I have made thee this day a defenced city, and an iron pillar, and brasen walls against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against the princes thereof, against the priests thereof, and against the people of the land."

question: What divine promise closes Jeremiah's call narrative in Jeremiah 1:19?
option1: Behold, thy enemies shall be scattered as chaff, and thou shalt see their downfall in peace
option2: And they shall fight against thee; but they shall not prevail against thee; for I am with thee, saith the LORD, to deliver thee
option3: Thou shalt dwell securely under the shadow of the Almighty until all these words be fulfilled
option4: No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper, and every tongue that riseth against thee thou shalt condemn
correct: And they shall fight against thee; but they shall not prevail against thee; for I am with thee, saith the LORD, to deliver thee
explanation: God guarantees not the absence of intense conflict, but absolute preservation through His sovereign presence. Jeremiah 1:19 (KJV) - "And they shall fight against thee; but they shall not prevail against thee; for I am with thee, saith the LORD, to deliver thee."

question: How does God fondly characterize Israel's youthful devotion and covenant honeymoon in Jeremiah 2:2?
option1: I recall the purity of thy heart when Moses led thee forth with timbrels and dancing
option2: I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown
option3: Thou wast my peculiar treasure, walking uprightly in the paths of righteousness across the desert
option4: Thy faith was like the morning star when thou didst receive my holy law at Mount Sinai
correct: I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown
explanation: Yahweh poignantly recalls the pristine loyalty of Israel during the wilderness wanderings, when she followed Him like a devoted young bride into unsown wastes. Jeremiah 2:2 (KJV) - "Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, Thus saith the LORD; I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown."

question: How was Israel consecrated to Yahweh, and what consequence befell any foreign power that dared devour her in Jeremiah 2:3?
option1: Israel was an anointed king; any who touched him were smitten with plague and barrenness
option2: Israel was a walled vineyard; whoever trespassed was pierced by the arrows of the Almighty
option3: Israel was holiness unto the LORD, and the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them
option4: Israel was the seal upon God's heart; those who oppressed him were drowned in deep waters
correct: Israel was holiness unto the LORD, and the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them
explanation: As sacred 'firstfruits' belonging exclusively to God, any predatory nation that consumed Israel incurred sacrilegious guilt and divine retribution. Jeremiah 2:3 (KJV) - "Israel was holiness unto the LORD, and the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them, saith the LORD."

question: What two monumental evils did God charge against His apostate people in Jeremiah 2:13?
option1: They have profaned the holy sabbaths, and offered their firstborn sons in sacrifice to Molech
option2: They have forgotten the law of Moses, and bowed before the golden calves of Dan and Bethel
option3: They have despised the house of prayer, and made pacts of blood with the kings of Egypt and Babylon
option4: They have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water
correct: They have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water
explanation: Israel committed irrational apostasy by abandoning an inexhaustible spring of living artesian water to dig fractured, leaking underground reservoirs. Jeremiah 2:13 (KJV) - "For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water."

question: Which two Egyptian cities are singled out in Jeremiah 2:16 as having broken or shaved the crown of Judah's head?
option1: Noph and Tahapanes
option2: Zoan and On
option3: Migdol and Pithom
option4: Thebes and Alexandria
correct: Noph and Tahapanes
explanation: Noph (Memphis) and Tahapanes (Daphnae) represent Egyptian military oppression that humiliated Judah's dignity. Jeremiah 2:16 (KJV) - "Also the children of Noph and Tahapanes have broken the crown of thy head."

question: What two foreign watercourses does Jeremiah rebuke Judah for drinking from in Jeremiah 2:18?
option1: The pools of Gihon and the brook of Cherith
option2: The waters of Sihor (Nile) and the waters of the river (Euphrates)
option3: The springs of Jericho and the waters of Merom
option4: The rivers of Damascus (Abana and Pharpar)
correct: The waters of Sihor (Nile) and the waters of the river (Euphrates)
explanation: Drinking the waters of Sihor (Egypt's Nile) and the River (Assyria's Euphrates) signified spiritual adultery through foreign political alliances. Jeremiah 2:18 (KJV) - "And now what hast thou to do in the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of Sihor? or what hast thou to do in the way of Assyria, to drink the waters of the river?"

question: What agricultural metaphor highlights the tragic moral transformation of Israel in Jeremiah 2:21?
option1: I planted thee as a green olive tree: how art thou become a barren thorn in the desert?
option2: I sowed thee as the finest wheat of Bashan: how art thou become bitter tares fit for the fire?
option3: Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?
option4: I nurtured thee as a royal fig tree: how art thou withered without budding or leaf?
correct: Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?
explanation: God planted Israel as choice Sorek stock, yet she incomprehensibly degenerated into a wild, alien vine bearing poisonous fruit. Jeremiah 2:21 (KJV) - "Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?"

question: What chemical cleansing agents are declared powerless to purge Judah's ingrained moral guilt in Jeremiah 2:22?
option1: Hyssop and running water
option2: Oil of myrrh and frankincense
option3: Brimstone and cedar ash
option4: Nitre and much soap
correct: Nitre and much soap
explanation: Even mineral natron (nitre) and vegetable alkali soap cannot erase the deep-seated stain of Judah's idolatrous corruption before God. Jeremiah 2:22 (KJV) - "For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord GOD."

question: What two untamable animal metaphors depict Judah's compulsive, uninhibited pursuit of pagan idolatry in Jeremiah 2:23-24?
option1: A swift dromedary traversing her ways and a wild ass in heat snuffing up the wind
option2: A ravenous wolf prowling by night and a roaring lion seeking prey
option3: A wandering sheep without a shepherd and an ox refusing the yoke
option4: A wild horse galloping toward the battle and a viper lurking in the rocks
correct: A swift dromedary traversing her ways and a wild ass in heat snuffing up the wind
explanation: Judah's frenzied craving for false gods resembled a young female camel crisscrossing tracks or a wild donkey in heat sniffing the desert breeze. Jeremiah 2:23-24 (KJV) - " ... thou art a swift dromedary traversing her ways; A wild ass used to the wilderness, that snuffeth up the wind at her pleasure; in her occasion who can turn her away? all they that seek her will not weary themselves; in her month they shall find her."

question: What absurd paternity do the idolaters of Judah ascribe to wooden idols and carved stones in Jeremiah 2:27?
option1: Saying to Baal, Thou art our creator; and to Ashtoreth, Thou hast nourished our children
option2: Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth
option3: Saying to the sun, Rule over our harvest; and to the moon, Protect our borders
option4: Saying to the molten calf, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up from Egypt
correct: Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth
explanation: The prophet mocks the insanity of pagans addressing inanimate blocks of wood as their biological father and rocks as their maternal womb. Jeremiah 2:27 (KJV) - "Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth: for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us."

question: According to what measure does Jeremiah quantify the shocking multitude of Judah's manufactured deities in Jeremiah 2:28?
option1: According to the sand of the seashore
option2: According to the thousands of the clans of Benjamin
option3: According to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah
option4: According to the days of the solar year
correct: According to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah
explanation: Judah had multiplied local deities to match the geographic census of every single town and village in the realm. Jeremiah 2:28 (KJV) - "But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah."

question: What Mosaic legal principle from Deuteronomy 24:1-4 does Jeremiah invoke to contrast God's astonishing grace toward adulterous Judah in Jeremiah 3:1?
option1: An adulteress caught in the act must be stoned outside the gate without mercy
option2: A treacherous priest who profanes the sanctuary must be stripped of his vestments forever
option3: A divorced wife who marries another man cannot lawfully return to her first husband, yet God invites scandalous Judah to return to Him
option4: A barren woman cannot inherit her husband's land after his death
correct: A divorced wife who marries another man cannot lawfully return to her first husband, yet God invites scandalous Judah to return to Him
explanation: Under the Torah, an adulterously remarried divorcee could never return to her first husband; yet Yahweh's radical covenant love supersedes legal precedent, pleading for her return. Jeremiah 3:1 (KJV) - "They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the LORD."

question: What anatomical idiom in Jeremiah 3:3 describes Judah's shameless obstinacy and refusal to blush over her sins?
option1: Thy heart was hardened like an adamant stone
option2: Thy neck was an iron sinew and thy brow brass
option3: Thy ears were uncircumcised and closed to correction
option4: Thou hadst a whore's forehead, thou refusedst to be ashamed
correct: Thou hadst a whore's forehead, thou refusedst to be ashamed
explanation: A 'whore's forehead' denotes brazen, unrepentant impudence that refuses moral embarrassment even when severe drought strikes the land. Jeremiah 3:3 (KJV) - "Therefore the showers have been withholden, and there hath been no latter rain; and thou hadst a whore's forehead, thou refusedst to be ashamed."

question: What did God give to northern Israel when He put her away for her persistent adultery in Jeremiah 3:8?
option1: A bill of divorce
option2: A cup of trembling
option3: A yoke of iron
option4: A scroll of lamentations
correct: A bill of divorce
explanation: God formally issued northern Israel a legal certificate of divorce (culminating in the 722 BC Assyrian deportation), yet treacherous Judah failed to take warning. Jeremiah 3:8 (KJV) - "And I saw, when for all the causes whereby backsliding Israel committed adultery I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce; yet her treacherous sister Judah feared not, but went and played the harlot also."

question: How did backsliding Israel compare with treacherous sister Judah in the divine evaluation of Jeremiah 3:11?
option1: Both sisters were equally condemned without distinction
option2: The backsliding Israel hath justified herself more than treacherous Judah
option3: Judah was found holy because of the temple of Solomon
option4: Israel was twice as corrupt because of the golden calves of Jeroboam
correct: The backsliding Israel hath justified herself more than treacherous Judah
explanation: Judah's sin was far more heinous because she possessed the temple and witnessed Israel's fall, yet repented only hypocritically and feignedly. Jeremiah 3:11 (KJV) - "And the LORD said unto me, The backsliding Israel hath justified herself more than treacherous Judah."

question: What marital declaration does God proclaim to call back His wandering people in Jeremiah 3:14?
option1: Return, O house of Jacob; for I have purchased thee with an everlasting price
option2: Awake, O virgin of Israel; for I am thy sovereign king and protector
option3: Turn, O backsliding children, saith the LORD; for I am married unto you
option4: Hearken, O seed of Abraham; for my covenant cannot be broken
correct: Turn, O backsliding children, saith the LORD; for I am married unto you
explanation: God grounds His passionate summons in irrevocable covenant matrimony: 'for I am married unto you' (ki anokhi ba'alti vakhem). Jeremiah 3:14 (KJV) - "Turn, O backsliding children, saith the LORD; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion:"

question: What leadership gift does God promise to bestow upon His gathered remnant in Jeremiah 3:15?
option1: Kings armed with iron sceptres to subdue the heathen nations
option2: Priests clothed in fine linen offering sweet incense upon golden altars
option3: Judges endowed with the wisdom of Solomon to govern the gates
option4: Pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding
correct: Pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding
explanation: In place of self-serving corrupt rulers, God promises godly spiritual shepherds who will nurture the flock with true divine wisdom. Jeremiah 3:15 (KJV) - "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding."

question: What astonishing prophecy concerning the Ark of the Covenant is unveiled in Jeremiah 3:16?
option1: They shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of the LORD: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more
option2: It shall be hidden in the caves of Mount Nebo until the Messiah appears
option3: It shall be overlaid with pure diamonds and placed upon Mount Zion for all nations to worship
option4: It shall be taken into heaven with the sound of a great trumpet before the temple falls
correct: They shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of the LORD: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more
explanation: In the new covenant era, the physical Ark of the Covenant will be completely superseded and rendered obsolete by God's immediate enthronement across the whole city. Jeremiah 3:16 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass, when ye be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days, saith the LORD, they shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of the LORD: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more."

question: What title will be given to Jerusalem when all nations gather unto it in Jeremiah 3:17?
option1: The city of righteousness
option2: The throne of the LORD
option3: The mountain of holiness
option4: The valley of vision
correct: The throne of the LORD
explanation: Jerusalem will no longer merely house a golden chest in the Holy of Holies, but the entire city itself will be designated 'The Throne of the LORD'. Jeremiah 3:17 (KJV) - "At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD; and all the nations shall be gathered unto it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem: neither shall they walk any more after the imagination of their evil heart."

question: What sound of mourning echoes from the high places in Jeremiah 3:21?
option1: Lamentations of the false prophets mourning their burned idols and crushed altars
option2: Cries of the watchmen reporting the galloping chariots of the northern invaders
option3: Weeping and supplications of the children of Israel: for they have perverted their way, and they have forgotten the LORD their God
option4: Groaning of the elders fasting in sackcloth for the departure of the glory
correct: Weeping and supplications of the children of Israel: for they have perverted their way, and they have forgotten the LORD their God
explanation: The high places - previously sites of licentious pagan revelry - now resound with the tearful contrition of Israelites acknowledging their spiritual ruin. Jeremiah 3:21 (KJV) - "A voice was heard upon the high places, weeping and supplications of the children of Israel: for they have perverted their way, and they have forgotten the LORD their God."

question: Where alone is authentic salvation to be found according to the penitent confession in Jeremiah 3:23?
option1: In the fortified strongholds of the kings of Judah
option2: In the multitude of burnt offerings sacrificed upon Mount Moriah
option3: In the mutual covenants formed with the princes of Egypt
option4: Truly in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel
correct: Truly in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel
explanation: The people repudiate pagan hill cults, confessing that human hills and mountain shrines offer no rescue: salvation belongs solely to Yahweh. Jeremiah 3:23 (KJV) - "Truly in vain is salvation hoped for from the hills, and from the multitude of mountains: truly in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel."

question: What agrarian command does God issue to the men of Judah and Jerusalem in Jeremiah 4:3?
option1: Prune your wild olive branches, and water the roots of the vine
option2: Plow deep furrows in the desert, and gather the early harvest
option3: Thresh the wheat with an iron wheel, and burn the useless chaff
option4: Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns
correct: Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns
explanation: Borrowing from Hosea 10:12, Jeremiah demands radical internal preparation: hard, unplowed hearts must be broken up so God's word is not choked by thorns. Jeremiah 4:3 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD to the men of Judah and Jerusalem, Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns."

question: What spiritual surgery is commanded in Jeremiah 4:4 to avert the unquenchable fire of God's fury?
option1: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart
option2: Wash your hands in innocence, and pour out libations at the threshold
option3: Shave your heads in sackcloth, and fast forty days in the wilderness
option4: Offer unblemished rams upon the altar, and consecrate your priests
correct: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart
explanation: Physical circumcision without inward consecration is meaningless; God demands radical circumcision of the heart to remove sinful obstinacy. Jeremiah 4:4 (KJV) - "Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings."

question: What predatory beast has arisen from his thicket to make the land desolate in Jeremiah 4:7?
option1: The fierce leopard waiting by the gate of the kings
option2: The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way
option3: The ravenous wolf of the evenings prowling through the vineyards
option4: The great dragon that lieth in the midst of his rivers
correct: The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army are depicted as an unstoppable apex predator breaking out of the Jordan thickets to ravage nations. Jeremiah 4:7 (KJV) - "The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant."

question: What meteorological metaphor describes the northern judgment that comes not to cleanse or fan grain in Jeremiah 4:11-12?
option1: A torrential hailstorm sweeping away the refuge of lies
option2: A dense cloud of darkness blotting out the sun at noon
option3: A dry wind of the high places in the wilderness ... not to fan, nor to cleanse, even a full wind
option4: A burning sirocco scorching the blossoming almond trees
correct: A dry wind of the high places in the wilderness ... not to fan, nor to cleanse, even a full wind
explanation: Unlike the gentle agricultural breeze used for winnowing chaff, this scorching desert gale (the sirocco) comes with devastating destructive force to execute sentence. Jeremiah 4:11-12 (KJV) - "At that time shall it be said to this people and to Jerusalem, A dry wind of the high places in the wilderness toward the daughter of my people, not to fan, nor to cleanse, Even a full wind from those places shall come unto me: now also will I give sentence against them."

question: From which two northern locations is the voice declaring affliction and approaching calamity in Jeremiah 4:15?
option1: Damascus and Mount Hermon
option2: Hazor and Mount Gilboa
option3: Megiddo and Mount Carmel
option4: Dan and Mount Ephraim
correct: Dan and Mount Ephraim
explanation: Dan marks the northernmost border of Israel, and Mount Ephraim represents the northern approaches to Jerusalem, charting the enemy's swift advance. Jeremiah 4:15 (KJV) - "For a voice declareth from Dan, and publisheth affliction from mount Ephraim."

question: What personal anguish causes Jeremiah to cry out in physical visceral pain in Jeremiah 4:19?
option1: My bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart; my heart maketh a noise in me; I cannot hold my peace, because thou hast heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war
option2: My eyes are dim with weeping; my skin is black like an oven because of the terrible famine
option3: My bones are pierced within me, and my sinews take no rest by reason of the rod of his wrath
option4: Woe is me for my hurt! my wound is grievous: but I said, Truly this is a grief, and I must bear it
correct: My bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart; my heart maketh a noise in me; I cannot hold my peace, because thou hast heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war
explanation: Jeremiah experiences acute physical torment in his inner organs ('bowels' / me'ay) as the trumpet alarm of incoming war reverberates in his soul. Jeremiah 4:19 (KJV) - "My bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart; my heart maketh a noise in me; I cannot hold my peace, because thou hast heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war."

question: How does God describe the moral paradox and spiritual tragedy of His people in Jeremiah 4:22?
option1: They boast in the wisdom of Egypt, yet walk blindly into destruction
option2: They are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge
option3: They discern the signs of the sky, but know not the time of their visitation
option4: They have built palaces of cedar, but their foundation is laid upon sand
correct: They are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge
explanation: Judah displayed perverse intellectual ingenuity in devising wicked schemes, while remaining utterly ignorant of moral good. Jeremiah 4:22 (KJV) - "For my people is foolish, they have not known me; they are sottish children, and they have none understanding: they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge."

question: What primordial Genesis terminology does Jeremiah evoke to describe the cosmic de-creation of the land in Jeremiah 4:23?
option1: I saw the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven pouring down fiery rain
option2: The stars of heaven fell unto the earth, and the moon was turned into blood
option3: I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light
option4: The sea and the waves were roaring, and the foundations of the mountains were dissolved
correct: I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light
explanation: Jeremiah employs the exact Genesis 1:2 phrase 'tohu va-bohu' ('without form and void'), depicting judgment as the cosmic unmaking of creation back into primeval chaos. Jeremiah 4:23 (KJV) - "I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light."

question: What reassuring divine caveat tempers the total devastation pronounced in Jeremiah 4:27?
option1: I will leave a thousand in the city and a hundred in the field
option2: My holy hill of Zion shall never be moved for David's sake
option3: The temple shall stand as an everlasting beacon amidst the ruins
option4: The whole land shall be desolate; yet will I not make a full end
correct: The whole land shall be desolate; yet will I not make a full end
explanation: Even amidst absolute territorial desolation, God preserves a faithful remnant covenant: He will not make a 'full end' (kalah). Jeremiah 4:27 (KJV) - "For thus hath the LORD said, The whole land shall be desolate; yet will I not make a full end."

question: How does Jeremiah portray the futile cosmetic attempts of Jerusalem to seduce her former foreign allies in Jeremiah 4:30?
option1: Though thou clothest thyself with crimson, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou rentest thy face with painting, in vain shalt thou make thyself fair; thy lovers will despise thee, they will seek thy life
option2: Though thou sendest ambassadors with silver vessels, and camels loaded with choice spices, they will betray thee
option3: Though thou buildest high walls and hirest archers from Cush, thy towers shall crumble into dust
option4: Though thou swear allegiance to Pharaoh on the altar of Osiris, the Chaldeans shall burn thy gates
correct: Though thou clothest thyself with crimson, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou rentest thy face with painting, in vain shalt thou make thyself fair; thy lovers will despise thee, they will seek thy life
explanation: Judah is personified as a desperate aging courtesan applying lavish scarlet robes, gold jewels, and eye-paint (antimony), yet her former paramours now seek her murder. Jeremiah 4:30 (KJV) - "And when thou art spoiled, what wilt thou do? Though thou clothest thyself with crimson, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou rentest thy face with painting, in vain shalt thou make thyself fair; thy lovers will despise thee, they will seek thy life."

question: What challenging search through the streets of Jerusalem is commanded to see if God would pardon the city in Jeremiah 5:1?
option1: Seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it
option2: Count the righteous elders who fast twice in the week and tithe their herbs
option3: Search out fifty blameless priests who have not bowed the knee to Baal
option4: Find ten upright scribes who preserve the book of the covenant without alteration
correct: Seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it
explanation: Echoing Abraham's intercession for Sodom (Genesis 18), God promises to spare Jerusalem if even a single person who executes justice and seeks truth can be found. Jeremiah 5:1 (KJV) - "Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it."

question: How does Jeremiah characterize the spiritual obstinacy of the people when divine discipline struck them in Jeremiah 5:3?
option1: They have stopped their ears like the deaf adder that will not hearken
option2: They have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return
option3: They have turned their backs like stubborn heifers refusing the goad
option4: They have hardened their hearts like Pharaoh in the day of plagues
correct: They have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return
explanation: Divine affliction produced neither grief nor repentance, but calcified their defiance into petrified obstinacy ('harder than a rock'). Jeremiah 5:3 (KJV) - "O LORD, are not thine eyes upon the truth? thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return."

question: What three predatory animals are unleashed to destroy those who have broken the yoke and burst the bonds in Jeremiah 5:6?
option1: A bear robbed of her whelps, a roaring lion, and a venomous asp
option2: A wild boar out of the wood, an eagle from the crag, and a stalking tiger
option3: A lion out of the forest, a wolf of the evenings, and a leopard watching over their cities
option4: A desert jackal, a fierce mastiff, and a horned viper in the sand
correct: A lion out of the forest, a wolf of the evenings, and a leopard watching over their cities
explanation: Three deadly carnivores symbolize the ferocious, stealthy, and swift Babylonian forces stalking the apostate cities. Jeremiah 5:6 (KJV) - "Wherefore a lion out of the forest shall slay them, and a wolf of the evenings shall spoil them, a leopard shall watch over their cities: every one that goeth out thence shall be torn in pieces: because their transgressions are many, and their backslidings are increased."

question: What animal lust metaphor exposes the rampant marital infidelity of Judah's wealthy elite in Jeremiah 5:8?
option1: They were as wild bulls goring one another in the lush pastures of Bashan
option2: They were as rutting stags clashing horns upon the rocky hillsides
option3: They were as greedy dogs barking in the marketplace after discarded meat
option4: They were as fed horses in the morning: every one neighed after his neighbour's wife
correct: They were as fed horses in the morning: every one neighed after his neighbour's wife
explanation: Prosperity without holiness degenerated into unrestrained sexual covetousness, compared to well-fed stallions neighing lustfully after neighboring mares. Jeremiah 5:8 (KJV) - "They were as fed horses in the morning: every one neighed after his neighbour's wife."

question: What dismissive falsehood did the people utter against the warnings of Yahweh's prophets in Jeremiah 5:12?
option1: It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine
option2: The temple of the LORD shall protect us, and our walls cannot be breached
option3: Pharaoh is marching to our aid, and the Babylonians shall flee in terror
option4: The visions of Jeremiah are for a distant time, and his words are vain wind
correct: It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine
explanation: Judah adopted practical atheism and false security, denying God's agency ('It is not He') and claiming disaster would never touch them. Jeremiah 5:12 (KJV) - "They have belied the LORD, and said, It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine:"

question: What transformative effect will God give to His words in Jeremiah's mouth in Jeremiah 5:14?
option1: Behold, my words shall be a sharp twoedged sword piercing between soul and spirit
option2: Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them
option3: Behold, my words shall be an iron hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces
option4: Behold, my words shall be a consuming plague wasting the fatness of their flesh
correct: Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them
explanation: While false prophets dismissed divine speech as empty wind, God made Jeremiah's prophetic message an incinerating fire that consumes the rebellious people like dry tinder. Jeremiah 5:14 (KJV) - "Wherefore thus saith the LORD God of hosts, Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them."

question: How is the invading Babylonian military described in Jeremiah 5:15-16?
option1: A nomadic horde from the desert whose tents cover the hills like grasshoppers
option2: A savage race armed with iron chariots and bronze scythes
option3: A mighty nation, an ancient nation, whose language thou knowest not ... their quiver is as an open sepulchre, they are all mighty men
option4: A confederacy of uncircumcised seafaring warriors from the isles of Chittim
correct: A mighty nation, an ancient nation, whose language thou knowest not ... their quiver is as an open sepulchre, they are all mighty men
explanation: Babylon was an ancient, formidable superpower whose foreign tongue heightened terror, whose archers struck with lethal cemetery-filling accuracy. Jeremiah 5:15-16 (KJV) - "Lo, I will bring a nation upon you from far, O house of Israel, saith the LORD: it is a mighty nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language thou knowest not, neither understandest what they say. Their quiver is as an open sepulchre, they are all mighty men."

question: What natural boundary established by divine decree proves God's sovereign majesty in contrast to Judah's rebellion in Jeremiah 5:22?
option1: The rocky foundations of the mountains set deep in the earth
option2: The appointed orbits of the sun and stars across the celestial vault
option3: The courses of the underground springs flowing through desert valleys
option4: The sand placed for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it
correct: The sand placed for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it
explanation: Even the raging, roaring ocean respects the fragile sand barrier established by divine fiat; yet human hearts shamelessly transgress God's moral boundaries. Jeremiah 5:22 (KJV) - "Fear ye not me? saith the LORD: will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?"

question: What trapping metaphor illustrates the predatory deceit of the wealthy oppressors in Jeremiah 5:26-27?
option1: They lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men. As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit
option2: They dig deep pits in the dark, and drag the helpless into their underground dungeons
option3: They spread fishing nets upon the waters, and gather the innocent for market
option4: They hunt like desert leopards stalking the poor in the narrow alleys
correct: They lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men. As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit
explanation: Wicked elites trapped fellow citizens through fraud and legal entrapment, filling their mansions with ill-gotten wealth like fowlers' cages packed with captive birds. Jeremiah 5:26-27 (KJV) - "For among my people are found wicked men: they lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men. As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: therefore they are become great, and waxen rich."

question: What 'wonderful and horrible thing' committed in the land climaxes Chapter 5 in Jeremiah 5:30-31?
option1: The king sacrifices his royal sons to Chemosh, and the elders offer libations upon the roofs
option2: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means; and my people love to have it so
option3: The temple gates are shut, and foreign idols are set up in the Holy of Holies
option4: The judges sell the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes
correct: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means; and my people love to have it so
explanation: A corrupt collusion between deceptive prophets and authoritarian priests was enthusiastically embraced by an unthinking populace: 'and my people love to have it so'. Jeremiah 5:30-31 (KJV) - "A wonderful and horrible thing is committed in the land; The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means; and my people love to have it so: and what will ye do in the end thereof?"

question: In which two southern locations are the children of Benjamin commanded to sound the trumpet and kindle a fire signal in Jeremiah 6:1?
option1: Blow the trumpet in Hebron, and set up a sign of fire in Bethlehem
option2: Blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Bethhaccerem
option3: Blow the trumpet in Beersheba, and set up a sign of fire in En-gedi
option4: Blow the trumpet in Kirjath-jearim, and set up a sign of fire in Mizpah
correct: Blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Bethhaccerem
explanation: Tekoa (south of Bethlehem) and Beth-haccerem ('house of the vineyard') were strategic southern high-altitude beacons to sound the alarm as invaders marched from the north. Jeremiah 6:1 (KJV) - "O ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Bethhaccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction."

question: How does Jerusalem emit moral corruption according to the natural metaphor in Jeremiah 6:7?
option1: As a volcano speweth out fire and ash, so she burneth with abominations
option2: As a stagnant marsh breedeth pestilence, so she corrupteth the nations
option3: As a fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her wickedness
option4: As a furnace poureth out dross, so she consumeth her innocent children
correct: As a fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her wickedness
explanation: Just as a natural artesian spring continually bubbles forth fresh water, Jerusalem effortlessly and perpetually gushed out violence, oppression, and moral filth. Jeremiah 6:7 (KJV) - "As a fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her wickedness: violence and spoil is heard in her; before me continually is grief and wounds."

question: What viticultural metaphor describes the thoroughness of the impending judgment upon the remnant in Jeremiah 6:9?
option1: They shall cut down the branches with an axe, and burn the root in the fire
option2: They shall tread the winepress outside the city until blood flows to the bridles
option3: They shall uproot the vineyard, and sow the fertile terraces with salt
option4: They shall throughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine: turn back thine hand as a grapegatherer into the baskets
correct: They shall throughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine: turn back thine hand as a grapegatherer into the baskets
explanation: Like a meticulous grape-harvester re-checking every leaf and cluster to ensure no stray grape escapes, the conquerors will thoroughly glean survivors into exile baskets. Jeremiah 6:9 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall throughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine: turn back thine hand as a grapegatherer into the baskets."

question: What anatomical defect prevents the people from listening to Jeremiah's prophetic warnings in Jeremiah 6:10?
option1: Their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken: behold, the word of the LORD is unto them a reproach
option2: Their eyes are blinded by the glitter of Egyptian gold
option3: Their tongue is paralyzed by the deceit of false diviners
option4: Their heart is covered with a veil of thick darkness
correct: Their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken: behold, the word of the LORD is unto them a reproach
explanation: An 'uncircumcised ear' signifies spiritual insensitivity and moral blockage that regards God's solemn word not with reverence, but as an intolerable offense and reproach. Jeremiah 6:10 (KJV) - "To whom shall I speak, and give warning, that they may hear? behold, their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken: behold, the word of the LORD is unto them a reproach; they have no delight in it."

question: How did the false prophets and corrupt priests superficialize the fatal spiritual wound of the nation in Jeremiah 6:14?
option1: They covered the bleeding wound with cosmetic ointment and sweet perfumes
option2: They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace
option3: They promised deliverance within seventy days by the hand of an angel
option4: They declared that temple sacrifices washed away all iniquity without repentance
correct: They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace
explanation: Corrupt religious leaders applied superficial band-aids to a mortal terminal cancer, chanting tranquilizing mantras of 'Shalom, shalom' when impending doom was at the gates. Jeremiah 6:14 (KJV) - "They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace."

question: What divine directive commands travelers to seek the ancient covenant ways to find soul rest in Jeremiah 6:16?
option1: Seek out the new wisdom of the nations, and follow the counsel of the kings of the earth
option2: Tread the narrow path of the Nazarites, and abstain from wine and strong drink
option3: Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein
option4: Depart from the cities of wickedness, and dwell in tents in the wilderness like the Rechabites
correct: Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein
explanation: God directs the nation to stand at life's crossroads and inquire for the time-tested ancient paths of Mosaic covenant obedience to obtain rest (echoed by Jesus in Matthew 11:29). Jeremiah 6:16 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein."

question: What costly foreign luxuries offered in ritual worship are rejected as unacceptable to God in Jeremiah 6:20?
option1: Gold of Ophir and dyed garments from Tyre
option2: Myrrh from Arabia and cedar timber from Lebanon
option3: Fine linen from Egypt and ivory from the islands of Chittim
option4: Incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country
correct: Incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country
explanation: Expensive imported frankincense from South Arabian Sheba and sweet aromatic calamus from distant lands cannot substitute for genuine moral obedience. Jeremiah 6:20 (KJV) - "To what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices sweet unto me."

question: How are the cruel northern invaders armed and described in Jeremiah 6:23?
option1: They shall lay hold on bow and spear; they are cruel, and have no mercy; their voice roareth like the sea; and they ride upon horses, set in array as men for war
option2: They march with shields of bronze and iron battering rams, executing slaughter without sparing
option3: They carry poisoned darts and flaming torches, shouting with the voice of roaring lions
option4: They wear heavy coats of mail and wield twoedged battleaxes, trampling the vineyards like locusts
correct: They shall lay hold on bow and spear; they are cruel, and have no mercy; their voice roareth like the sea; and they ride upon horses, set in array as men for war
explanation: The invading Babylonian cavalry and archers were renowned for ruthless mercilessness, their battle cry deafening like ocean breakers. Jeremiah 6:23 (KJV) - "They shall lay hold on bow and spear; they are cruel, and have no mercy; their voice roareth like the sea; and they ride upon horses, set in array as men for war against thee, O daughter of Zion."

question: What metallurgical role was Jeremiah appointed to fulfill among God's people in Jeremiah 6:27?
option1: A hammer to shatter the dross and an anvil to forge new vessels
option2: A tower and a fortress among my people, that thou mayest know and try their way
option3: A silversmith to refine the holy vessels of the sanctuary
option4: A watchman upon the walls to sound the silver trumpet
correct: A tower and a fortress among my people, that thou mayest know and try their way
explanation: Jeremiah was appointed as an assayer ('an assayer and a fortress' / bachon) to test and evaluate the moral purity of the nation's spiritual metal. Jeremiah 6:27 (KJV) - "I have set thee for a tower and a fortress among my people, that thou mayest know and try their way."

question: What metallurgical verdict concludes Chapter 6 when the smelting process utterly fails to extract silver in Jeremiah 6:29-30?
option1: The crucible is cracked, the gold is turned to ashes ... A destroyed heritage shall they be named
option2: The furnace is quenched, the coals are scattered ... Worthless dross fit only for the dungheap
option3: The bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire; the founder melteth in vain ... Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them
option4: The molten metal is spilled upon the ground ... Broken vessels that cannot be repaired
correct: The bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire; the founder melteth in vain ... Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them
explanation: In ancient cupellation, lead was oxidized by bellows heat to separate precious metal from dross; here the bellows are scorched and lead vaporized in vain because the wicked cannot be separated: they are discarded as 'reprobate silver' (refuse dross). Jeremiah 6:29-30 (KJV) - "The bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire; the founder melteth in vain: for the wicked are not plucked away. Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them."

question: What threefold superstitious chant did the Judeans repeat, treating the temple as an unconditional magical talisman in Jeremiah 7:4?
option1: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts, the whole earth is full of his glory
option2: Zion shall stand forever, the city of our God cannot be moved
option3: The temple of the LORD, The temple of the LORD, The temple of the LORD, are these
option4: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the mountain of his holiness
correct: The temple of the LORD, The temple of the LORD, The temple of the LORD, are these
explanation: Judah substituted external ritualism and building superstition for moral obedience, chanting 'The temple of the LORD' as if God's presence guaranteed inviolability regardless of their sins. Jeremiah 7:4 (KJV) - "Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of the LORD, The temple of the LORD, The temple of the LORD, are these."

question: What indictment from Jeremiah 7:11 did Jesus famously quote when cleansing the Jerusalem temple in Matthew 21:13?
option1: My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer; but ye have made it an house of merchandise
option2: Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise
option3: Ye have profaned my sanctuary with the blood of innocent sacrifices and unjust gain
option4: Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes?
correct: Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes?
explanation: Jesus cited Jeremiah 7:11 to condemn religious hypocrites who turned God's house into a bandits' lair ('den of robbers' / me'arat paritsim) where criminals took refuge between their crimes. Jeremiah 7:11 (KJV) - "Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the LORD."

question: What historical sanctuary does God point to as tangible historical proof that He will abandon an unfaithful sanctuary in Jeremiah 7:12-14?
option1: Shiloh
option2: Bethel
option3: Gilgal
option4: Nob
correct: Shiloh
explanation: God reminded Judah that Shiloh - the original site of the Tabernacle during Joshua and Eli's era - was completely destroyed by the Philistines because of Israel's wickedness. Jeremiah 7:12 (KJV) - "But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel."

question: What startling prohibition did God lay upon Jeremiah concerning intercessory prayer for Judah in Jeremiah 7:16?
option1: Fast not forty days for their sins, neither pour out ashes upon thy head, for their judgment is fixed
option2: Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee
option3: Offer no blood of bullocks or rams on their behalf, for my soul delighteth not in their oblations
option4: Enter not into the house of mourning to comfort them, for I have taken away my peace from this people
correct: Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee
explanation: Because Judah's moral corruption was irrevocable, God commanded Jeremiah to cease all intercessory prayer: judicial judgment was now inevitable. Jeremiah 7:16 (KJV) - "Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee."

question: How did whole families actively participate in manufacturing idolatrous baked offerings in the streets in Jeremiah 7:18?
option1: The sons slaughter the lambs, the fathers pour the wine, and the mothers weave tapestries for Baal
option2: The young men fashion idols, the elders blow trumpets, and the maidens dance around Ashtoreth
option3: The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven
option4: The fathers build high altars, the mothers brew spiced wine, and the children sprinkle blood upon the stones
correct: The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven
explanation: Apostasy was an entrenched family project: children gathered fuel, fathers stoked flames, and mothers baked sacrificial crescent cakes to the Mesopotamian astral goddess Ishtar ('queen of heaven'). Jeremiah 7:18 (KJV) - "The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto other gods, that they may provoke me to anger."

question: What foundational covenant demand took precedence over external ritual sacrifices at the Exodus according to Jeremiah 7:22-23?
option1: Offer daily morning and evening lambs upon the bronze altar without blemish
option2: Keep the seven feasts of the Lord throughout your generations as an everlasting ordinance
option3: Circumcise every male child on the eighth day and bring the firstfruits of thy cattle
option4: Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you
correct: Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you
explanation: At Sinai, God's primary requirement was not ceremonial ritualism, but moral obedience and personal covenant allegiance. Jeremiah 7:23 (KJV) - "But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you."

question: What expression describes God's persistent, tireless prophetic outreach to His stubborn people throughout their history in Jeremiah 7:25?
option1: Daily rising up early and sending them
option2: Pleading with them in visions of the night season
option3: Stretching out my hands all the day long unto a disobedient people
option4: Sending angels of light to rebuke their transgressions
correct: Daily rising up early and sending them
explanation: The anthropomorphic idiom 'rising up early and sending' (hashkem veshaloach) portrays God's diligent, eager, and unwavering paternal compassion in sending prophet after prophet. Jeremiah 7:25 (KJV) - "Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them:"

question: What barbaric child-sacrifice ritual was conducted at Tophet in the Valley of the son of Hinnom in Jeremiah 7:31?
option1: To bury their infants alive beneath the foundation stones of foreign altars
option2: To burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart
option3: To pass their youth through fire unto Molech to divine the fortune of kings
option4: To sacrifice the firstborn of every virgin upon the blood-stained rocks of Chemosh
correct: To burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart
explanation: Judah practiced heinous infant cremations to Molech at Tophet, an abomination so contrary to God's holy nature that 'neither came it into my heart'. Jeremiah 7:31 (KJV) - "And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart."

question: What ominous new name is assigned to the Valley of the son of Hinnom (Tophet) in Jeremiah 7:32?
option1: The field of blood
option2: The valley of Jehoshaphat
option3: The valley of slaughter
option4: The place of weeping
correct: The valley of slaughter
explanation: Because of unburied heaps of slaughtered Judeans during the Babylonian assault, Gehenna (Valley of Hinnom) was renamed 'The Valley of Slaughter'. Jeremiah 7:32 (KJV) - "Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place."

question: What four joyful sounds will completely vanish from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 7:34?
option1: The song of the harpers, the shout of the harvesters, the melody of the tabret, and the laughter of children
option2: The sound of the flute, the chanting of the Levites, the blessing of the priests, and the prayer of the upright
option3: The cry of the watchmen, the roar of the warriors, the counsel of the wise, and the rejoicing of the princes
option4: The voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride
correct: The voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride
explanation: Impending devastation extinguishes all civic and marital celebration: joy, gladness, and wedding songs are silenced forever in the desolate land. Jeremiah 7:34 (KJV) - "Then will I cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride: for the land shall be desolate."

question: What posthumous desecration will conquerors inflict upon the tombs of Judah's royalty, priests, and prophets in Jeremiah 8:1-2?
option1: They shall burn their bones into lime to plaster the palaces of Babylon
option2: They shall cast their royal sepulchres into the brook Kidron to be washed away
option3: They shall grind their skeletons to powder and scatter them on the four winds
option4: They shall bring out the bones ... and spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served
correct: They shall bring out the bones ... and spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served
explanation: The bones of apostate rulers and false prophets will be exhumed and strewn like dung before the very astral bodies (sun, moon, stars) they illicitly worshiped. Jeremiah 8:1-2 (KJV) - "At that time, saith the LORD, they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of their graves: And they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served ... they shall be for dung upon the face of the earth."

question: What tragic preference will the miserable survivors of Judah choose in all the places of their dispersion in Jeremiah 8:3?
option1: Death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue of them that remain of this evil family
option2: They shall choose to serve idols in foreign lands rather than return to Zion
option3: They shall choose eternal silence in the wilderness rather than singing songs of joy
option4: They shall choose poverty and sackcloth rather than royal riches in Babylon
correct: Death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue of them that remain of this evil family
explanation: The horrors of exile, famine, and humiliation will be so excruciating that survivors will long for death as a merciful relief. Jeremiah 8:3 (KJV) - "And death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue of them that remain of this evil family, which remain in all the places whither I have driven them, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What natural instinct of migratory birds shames the irrational spiritual ignorance of God's people in Jeremiah 8:7?
option1: The eagle soareth toward the sun and the falcon returneth to the nest; but my people have forgotten the rock of their salvation
option2: The stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the LORD
option3: The owl watcheth through the night and the raven provideth for her young; but my people rebel against my holy law
option4: The sparrow findeth an house and the swallow a nest for her brood; but my people have forsaken my altars
correct: The stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the LORD
explanation: Migratory birds instinctively follow the seasonal ordinances God embedded into creation, while human beings endowed with revelation defy divine order. Jeremiah 8:7 (KJV) - "Yea, the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the LORD."

question: How does Jeremiah rebuke the corrupt scribes who claimed intellectual and legal superiority in Jeremiah 8:8?
option1: They have added lies to the scroll of Moses, and their parchment shall be consumed by fire
option2: Their ink is mixed with gall, and they have perverted the judgment of the widow and orphan
option3: How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain
option4: They seal up the law among their disciples, yet walk after the stubbornness of their own heart
correct: How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain
explanation: Jeremiah unmasks the professional scribal guild for using their 'lying pen' (et sheqer) to falsify the true intent of the Torah and justify corruption. Jeremiah 8:8 (KJV) - "How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain."

question: What rhetorical question exposes the intellectual bankruptcy of the 'wise men' who rejected God's word in Jeremiah 8:9?
option1: Can a corrupt tree bring forth pleasant fruit, or a bitter fountain sweet water?
option2: Have they not leaned upon the broken reed of Egypt, which pierceth the hand of him that leaneth?
option3: Will their astrological charts save them when the King of Babylon breaketh down their gates?
option4: Lo, they have rejected the word of the LORD; and what wisdom is in them?
correct: Lo, they have rejected the word of the LORD; and what wisdom is in them?
explanation: Any intellectual system or philosophy that dismisses divine revelation is fundamentally devoid of authentic wisdom. Jeremiah 8:9 (KJV) - "The wise men are ashamed, they are dismayed and taken: lo, they have rejected the word of the LORD; and what wisdom is in them?"

question: What venomous, uncharmable plague will God release among His obstinate people in Jeremiah 8:17?
option1: Serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you
option2: Fiery scorpions from the desert that sting with torment five months
option3: Horned vipers hiding beneath the threshold of every palace
option4: Swarming locusts and cankerworms that devour every green leaf
correct: Serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you
explanation: Babylonian conquerors are likened to lethal, deaf vipers that no serpent charmer can soothe or divert from their fatal strike. Jeremiah 8:17 (KJV) - "For, behold, I will send serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you, saith the LORD."

question: What proverb of tragic missed opportunity and expired grace is uttered in Jeremiah 8:20?
option1: The sun is gone down while it was yet day, and we are left in darkness
option2: The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved
option3: The fountain of living waters is dried up, and our cisterns are broken
option4: The watchman hath blown the trumpet in vain, and the sword hath overtaken us
correct: The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved
explanation: The agrarian cycle from spring barley harvest to late summer fruit harvest passed without military relief from Egyptian allies, leaving Judah facing hopeless doom. Jeremiah 8:20 (KJV) - "The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved."

question: What famous double medical question laments the unhealed spiritual condition of the daughter of my people in Jeremiah 8:22?
option1: Can nitre cleanse the guilty soul, or much soap wash away iniquity?
option2: Is there no oil of olive in Samaria; is there no medicine in Damascus?
option3: Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
option4: Why will ye die, O house of Israel; why do ye refuse the cup of healing?
correct: Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
explanation: Gilead was world-renowned for its restorative aromatic resin (balm); the prophet poignantly asks why the nation's spiritual wound remains unhealed when the divine Great Physician is near. Jeremiah 8:22 (KJV) - "Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?"

question: What physical posture and color does Jeremiah assume in his profound identification with the grief of his people in Jeremiah 8:21?
option1: I sit in ashes in the dust; I am clothed with mourning garments of goat hair
option2: My knees smite together with trembling; my heart is melted like wax
option3: I go mourning without the sun; I stand up and cry in the assembly of the elders
option4: For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me
correct: For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me
explanation: Jeremiah's intense emotional agony manifested physically: 'I am black' (qadarti), wearing dark mourning garb and darkened by overwhelming sorrow. Jeremiah 8:21 (KJV) - "For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me."

question: From where was the terrifying snorting of the invading cavalry horses heard in Jeremiah 8:16?
option1: Dan
option2: Damascus
option3: Megiddo
option4: Samaria
correct: Dan
explanation: The thunderous vibrations and neighing of the Babylonian war horses echoed from the northern frontier post of Dan, shaking the entire countryside. Jeremiah 8:16 (KJV) - "The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan: the whole land trembled at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones; for they are come, and have devoured the land, and all that is in it; the city, and those that dwell therein."

question: What heartfelt yearning for inexhaustible weeping opens Chapter 9, cementing Jeremiah's reputation as the weeping prophet?
option1: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
option2: Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not thy holy law day and night
option3: Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people
option4: Woe is me that I dwell in Meshech, that I wander in the wilderness among tears
correct: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
explanation: Jeremiah desires his head to become a reservoir and his eyes an unceasing spring of tears to adequately mourn the catastrophic slaughter of his people. Jeremiah 9:1 (KJV) - "Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!"

question: What solitary shelter did Jeremiah wish for to escape the treacherous and adulterous company of his countrymen in Jeremiah 9:2?
option1: A cave in the rocks of Engedi
option2: A lodging place of wayfaring men in the wilderness
option3: A watchtower upon Mount Hermon
option4: A quiet booth in the desert of Sinai
correct: A lodging place of wayfaring men in the wilderness
explanation: Exhausted by pervasive hypocrisy and betrayal, Jeremiah longed for a lonely caravan shelter (khan) in the desert rather than living among treacherous citizens. Jeremiah 9:2 (KJV) - "Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men."

question: What lethal weapon metaphor describes the slanderous, deceptive tongue of the Judeans in Jeremiah 9:3, 8?
option1: Their tongue is a sharp twoedged sword devouring the innocent
option2: Their tongue is a flaming torch setting the forest on fire
option3: They bend their tongues like their bow for lies ... their tongue is as an arrow shot out; it speaketh deceit
option4: Their tongue is a poison dart dipped in the venom of asps
correct: They bend their tongues like their bow for lies ... their tongue is as an arrow shot out; it speaketh deceit
explanation: Speech was weaponized into military instruments: bent bows launching deadly arrows of falsehood and treacherous deceit against neighbors. Jeremiah 9:3, 8 (KJV) - "And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies: but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth ... Their tongue is as an arrow shot out; it speaketh deceit: one speaketh peaceably to his neighbour with his mouth, but in heart he layeth his wait."

question: What patriarchal name-pun warns that even closest family members would utterly defraud and supplant each other in Jeremiah 9:4?
option1: For every brother will sell his kinsman like Joseph into Egyptian bondage
option2: For every brother will rise up against his companion like Cain in the field
option3: For every brother will build a high place like Absalom against his father
option4: For every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders
correct: For every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders
explanation: The Hebrew verb 'aqov ya'qov' ('utterly supplant') invokes the name of Jacob (Ya'aqov, the supplanter), warning that universal treachery had infected the closest kin. Jeremiah 9:4 (KJV) - "Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders."

question: What two desolate transformations will reduce Jerusalem and the cities of Judah in Jeremiah 9:11?
option1: I will make Jerusalem heaps, and a den of dragons; and I will make the cities of Judah desolate, without an inhabitant
option2: A burning pit of pitch, and an habitation of desert owls and scorpions
option3: A field sown with salt, and a pasture for the flocks of the Nomads
option4: A fortress of dust, and a refuge for wild beasts of the islands
correct: I will make Jerusalem heaps, and a den of dragons; and I will make the cities of Judah desolate, without an inhabitant
explanation: Jerusalem's glorious stone palaces will be reduced to rubble heaps and colonized by jackals ('dragons' / tannim). Jeremiah 9:11 (KJV) - "And I will make Jerusalem heaps, and a den of dragons; and I will make the cities of Judah desolate, without an inhabitant."

question: What bitter food and toxic beverage will God feed this apostate nation in Jeremiah 9:15?
option1: Ashes and vinegar
option2: Wormwood and water of gall
option3: Bitter herbs and dross
option4: Wild gourds and hemlock
correct: Wormwood and water of gall
explanation: Wormwood (bitter artemisia) and poisonous hemlock/gall (rosh) symbolize the intolerable bitterness of divine chastisement and siege starvation. Jeremiah 9:15 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will feed them, even this people, with wormwood, and give them water of gall to drink."

question: Who are summoned in Jeremiah 9:17 to take up professional lamentation for the catastrophic fall of Zion?
option1: The priests of the sons of Aaron and the Levite cantors
option2: The watchmen upon the walls and the elders of the gate
option3: The mourning women and cunning women
option4: The daughters of the kings and the maidens of Shiloh
correct: The mourning women and cunning women
explanation: Professional female keening-singers (meqonenot, skilled wailing women) were summoned to orchestrate mass dirges for the ruined nation. Jeremiah 9:17 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Consider ye, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; and send for cunning women, that they may come:"

question: How does Jeremiah personify Death invading the homes and extinguishing life in Jeremiah 9:21?
option1: Death hath broken down the iron gates, and hath marched through the broad avenues with a sword
option2: Death hath poisoned the water springs, and hath breathed pestilence upon the sucklings
