option4: Then will I cause this sanctuary to be plowed with salt like the ruins of Sodom
correct: Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth
explanation: Threatening that the magnificent Solomonic temple would suffer the same total destruction as ancient Shiloh was viewed by the religious hierarchy as capital blasphemy. Jeremiah 26:6, 9 (KJV) - "Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth ... Why hast thou prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant? And all the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the LORD."

question: What formal capital indictment did the corrupt priests and false prophets bring against Jeremiah before the civil magistrates in Jeremiah 26:11?
option1: This man hath spoken blasphemy against the Holy of Holies and must be stoned
option2: This man is an Egyptian spy seeking to deliver our king into the hands of Pharaoh
option3: This man hath profaned the sabbath and stirred up sedition among the people
option4: This man is worthy to die; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard with your ears
correct: This man is worthy to die; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard with your ears
explanation: The priests and court prophets demanded the death penalty ('worthy to die' / mishpat mavet), charging Jeremiah with treason for prophesying doom against Jerusalem. Jeremiah 26:11 (KJV) - "Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard with your ears."

question: What heroic, unyielding legal defense did Jeremiah present to the assembled princes and people in Jeremiah 26:14-15?
option1: As for me, behold, I am in your hand: do with me as seemeth good and meet unto you. But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves
option2: I appeal unto King Jehoiakim, and demand to be judged before the council of the seventy elders
option3: The temple cannot protect you, and my blood will be required of your children for forty generations
option4: Behold, twelve legions of angels surround me, and no man can lay a hand upon my life
correct: As for me, behold, I am in your hand: do with me as seemeth good and meet unto you. But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves
explanation: With extraordinary serenity, Jeremiah yielded his physical life to their custody while solemnly warning that executing him would incur the guilt of shedding innocent blood. Jeremiah 26:14-15 (KJV) - "As for me, behold, I am in your hand: do with me as seemeth good and meet unto you. But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof: for of a truth the LORD hath sent me unto you to speak all these words in your ears."

question: What eighth-century prophet was cited by the elders as a legal precedent to save Jeremiah's life in Jeremiah 26:18?
option1: Amos of Tekoa
option2: Micah the Morasthite
option3: Hosea the son of Beeri
option4: Isaiah the son of Amoz
correct: Micah the Morasthite
explanation: Senior elders intervened, quoting Micah 3:12 verbatim to prove that true prophets had historically pronounced Jerusalem's ruin without being executed. Jeremiah 26:18 (KJV) - "Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and spake to all the people of Judah, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest."

question: How did righteous King Hezekiah respond to Micah's prophecy of doom, contrasting sharply with Jehoiakim's murderous wrath in Jeremiah 26:19?
option1: He tore down the high places and offered a thousand bullocks upon the bronze altar
option2: He imprisoned Micah in the palace until the Assyrian siege was lifted
option3: Did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD, and the LORD repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them?
option4: He sent messengers to the prophetess Huldah to inquire whether the word was true
correct: Did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD, and the LORD repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them?
explanation: Hezekiah responded with godly fear, humble repentance, and fervent intercession, moving God to spare Jerusalem from destruction. Jeremiah 26:19 (KJV) - "Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death? did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD, and the LORD repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them? Thus might we procure great evil against our souls."

question: Which contemporary prophet prophesied identical words against Jerusalem, fled to Egypt for his life, but was extradited and executed by King Jehoiakim in Jeremiah 26:20-23?
option1: Zephaniah the son of Cushi
option2: Habakkuk the Levite
option3: Hananiah the son of Azur
option4: Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim
correct: Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim
explanation: Prophet Urijah ben Shemaiah echoed Jeremiah's exact warnings, but when Jehoiakim sought his life, he fled to Egypt, was extradited by royal agents, murdered, and thrown into a common grave. Jeremiah 26:20-23 (KJV) - "And there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the LORD, Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah ... And they fetched forth Urijah out of Egypt, and brought him unto Jehoiakim the king; who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people."

question: Which high-ranking royal official was dispatched to Egypt by King Jehoiakim to extradite the fugitive prophet Urijah in Jeremiah 26:22?
option1: Elnathan the son of Achbor
option2: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
option3: Gedaliah the son of Pashur
option4: Gemariah the son of Hilkiah
correct: Elnathan the son of Achbor
explanation: Elnathan ben Achbor (who later urged Jehoiakim not to burn Jeremiah's scroll, Jeremiah 36:25) was sent with an armed extradition squad to seize Urijah. Jeremiah 26:22 (KJV) - "And Jehoiakim the king sent men into Egypt, namely, Elnathan the son of Achbor, and certain men with him into Egypt."

question: What disgraceful burial was inflicted upon the executed prophet Urijah by King Jehoiakim in Jeremiah 26:23?
option1: Burned his corpse in the valley of Tophet with unclean carcases
option2: Cast his dead body into the graves of the common people
option3: Hanged his body upon the city walls of Jerusalem before the gates
option4: Cast his bones into the brook Kidron to be washed into the Dead Sea
correct: Cast his dead body into the graves of the common people
explanation: Jehoiakim denied Urijah an honorable family sepulchre, tossing his corpse into the public pauper cemetery ('graves of the common people'). Jeremiah 26:23 (KJV) - " ... who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people."

question: Which influential nobleman protected Jeremiah from the murderous mob and prevented him from being put to death in Jeremiah 26:24?
option1: Baruch the son of Neriah
option2: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
option3: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
option4: Hilkiah the high priest
correct: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
explanation: Ahikam ben Shaphan - a member of the prestigious reforming scribal family that discovered the law under Josiah, and father of future governor Gedaliah - used his aristocratic influence to rescue Jeremiah. Jeremiah 26:24 (KJV) - "Nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death."

question: What symbolic physical implements was Jeremiah commanded to manufacture and strap onto his own neck in Jeremiah 27:2?
option1: Make thee iron chains and fetters, and bind thy hands and feet
option2: Make thee a wooden collar and a bronze crown, and wear them in the gate
option3: Make thee bonds and yokes, and put them upon thy neck
option4: Make thee a sackcloth harness and an ox bridle, and lead a heifer through Zion
correct: Make thee bonds and yokes, and put them upon thy neck
explanation: Jeremiah constructed a wooden ox yoke and leather thongs ('bonds and yokes'), wearing it upon his neck as an enacted sign of imperial servitude to Babylon. Jeremiah 27:2 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD to me; Make thee bonds and yokes, and put them upon thy neck,"

question: To the ambassadors of which five foreign kingdoms was Jeremiah instructed to send replica yokes via their envoys visiting Jerusalem in Jeremiah 27:3?
option1: Egypt, Philistia, Damascus, Assyria, and Cush
option2: Media, Elam, Persia, Sheba, and Dedan
option3: Syria, Hamath, Arpad, Carchemish, and Calno
option4: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon
correct: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon
explanation: Diplomats from five regional kingdoms gathered in Jerusalem to plot an anti-Babylonian coalition; Jeremiah gave each envoy a yoke to take back to their monarchs. Jeremiah 27:3 (KJV) - "And send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the Ammonites, and to the king of Tyrus, and to the king of Zidon, by the hand of the messengers which come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah;"

question: On what theological foundation of creation does Yahweh assert His right to bestow global governance upon Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 27:5-6?
option1: I have made the earth, the man and the beast ... by my great power and by my outstretched arm, and have given it unto whom it seemed meet unto me
option2: Because the kingdoms of the world are full of idolatry and blood, I have chosen a fierce king to punish them
option3: According to the covenant of Noah, the northern empires shall rule over the tents of Shem
option4: I have raised up the Chaldeans as a mighty hammer to establish the borders of the nations
correct: I have made the earth, the man and the beast ... by my great power and by my outstretched arm, and have given it unto whom it seemed meet unto me
explanation: As the supreme Creator of the planet, humanity, and animal kingdom, God possesses absolute proprietary authority to transfer geopolitical dominion to whomsoever He pleases. Jeremiah 27:5-6 (KJV) - "I have made the earth, the man and the beast that are upon the ground, by my great power and by my outstretched arm, and have given it unto whom it seemed meet unto me. And now have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant; and the beasts of the field have I given him also to serve him."

question: For how many generations of Babylonian royal succession will all nations serve Nebuchadnezzar according to Jeremiah 27:7?
option1: Unto ten generations of his seed
option2: Him, and his son, and his son's son, until the very time of his land come
option3: Until his dynasty is cut off after seventy weeks
option4: Throughout all generations forever
correct: Him, and his son, and his son's son, until the very time of his land come
explanation: Babylonian hegemony was strictly generational, spanning Nebuchadnezzar, his son Evil-Merodach (Amel-Marduk), and his grandson Belshazzar (Nabonidus's co-regent), after which Babylon would be conquered. Jeremiah 27:7 (KJV) - "And all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son's son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him."

question: What practical advice did Jeremiah deliver to King Zedekiah to ensure survival and avoid military catastrophe in Jeremiah 27:12?
option1: Send ambassadors to Egypt with gold and silver to hire ten thousand horsemen
option2: Strengthen the towers of Zion and fast forty days before the Ark of the Covenant
option3: Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live
option4: Flee by night across the Jordan into the mountains of Moab
correct: Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live
explanation: Jeremiah urged unconditional political submission to Babylon: submitting to the yoke was the only divinely ordained path to preserve life and city. Jeremiah 27:12 (KJV) - "I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live."

question: What false promise were popular prophets proclaiming regarding the sacred vessels looted by Babylon in 597 BC in Jeremiah 27:16?
option1: The golden vessels have been miraculously hidden by angels in the rock of Mount Nebo
option2: Nebuchadnezzar hath converted to the God of Israel and will return the holy treasures
option3: The vessels shall remain in Babylon for a single week and then return with songs of joy
option4: Behold, the vessels of the LORD's house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon
correct: Behold, the vessels of the LORD's house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon
explanation: Court prophets spread patriotic lies claiming the looted temple vessels would be repatriated almost immediately ('now shortly'). Jeremiah 27:16 (KJV) - "Also I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Thus saith the LORD; Hearken not to the words of your prophets that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the LORD's house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you."

question: What genuine prophetic test does Jeremiah propose to the optimistic false prophets in Jeremiah 27:18?
option1: Let them now make intercession to the LORD of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the house of the LORD ... go not to Babylon
option2: Let them call down fire from heaven to consume the altar of burnt offering
option3: Let them predict the day when the Euphrates shall be dried up before our army
option4: Let them reveal the secret thoughts of King Nebuchadnezzar in his bedchamber
correct: Let them now make intercession to the LORD of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the house of the LORD ... go not to Babylon
explanation: Jeremiah challenged them: if they have genuine access to the heavenly council, let them pray to stop the remaining bronze temple furnishings from being deported to Babylon! Jeremiah 27:18 (KJV) - "But if they be prophets, and if the word of the LORD be with them, let them now make intercession to the LORD of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the house of the LORD, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem, go not to Babylon."

question: Which massive bronze temple furnishings remaining in Jerusalem are specifically prophesied to be carried off to Babylon in Jeremiah 27:19-22?
option1: The golden candlestick, the table of shewbread, and the altar of incense
option2: The pillars, and the sea, and the bases, and the residue of the vessels
option3: The Ark of the Covenant, the mercy seat, and the two cherubim
option4: The bronze altar of Solomon, the ten basins of brass, and the golden censers
correct: The pillars, and the sea, and the bases, and the residue of the vessels
explanation: Solomon's two colossal bronze pillars (Jachin and Boaz), the Molten Sea, and the mobile bronze water bases would all be broken up and transported to Babylon (fulfilled in Jeremiah 52:17). Jeremiah 27:19, 22 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that remain in this city ... They shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be until the day that I visit them, saith the LORD; then will I bring them up, and restore them to this place."

question: What three punishments are threatened against any rebellious nation refusing to submit its neck to Nebuchadnezzar's yoke in Jeremiah 27:8?
option1: The drought, the locust, and the earthquake
option2: The fire, the whirlwind, and the burning pitch
option3: The sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence
option4: The blind eyes, the iron fetters, and the dark dungeon
correct: The sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence
explanation: Any nation staging an insurrection against Nebuchadnezzar would be crushed by divine warfare, starvation, and plague. Jeremiah 27:8 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass, that the nation and kingdom which will not serve the same Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, and that will not put their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, that nation will I punish, saith the LORD, with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand."

question: What five categories of occult practitioners are citizens warned not to consult in Jeremiah 27:9?
option1: Your astrologers, your stargazers, your monthly prognosticators, your necromancers, and your soothsayers
option2: Your magicians, your Chaldeans, your wise men, your scribes, and your elders
option3: Your priests of Baal, your prophets of the grove, your witch doctors, your charmers, and your augurs
option4: Your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your enchanters, and your sorcerers
correct: Your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your enchanters, and your sorcerers
explanation: God commands the people to reject pagan occultists who peddled false hopes of national triumph against Babylon. Jeremiah 27:9 (KJV) - "Therefore hearken not ye to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters, nor to your sorcerers, which speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon:"

question: Which false prophet from Gibeon publicly confronted Jeremiah in the temple during the fourth year of Zedekiah in Jeremiah 28:1?
option1: Pashur the son of Immer
option2: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
option3: Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah
option4: Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon
correct: Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon
explanation: Hananiah ben Azur of Gibeon staged a sensational public challenge in the temple courtyards in 593 BC. Jeremiah 28:1 (KJV) - "And it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, and in the fifth month, that Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon, spake unto me in the house of the LORD, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,"

question: What optimistic timeline did Hananiah boldly proclaim for the return of temple vessels and exiled King Jeconiah in Jeremiah 28:2-4?
option1: Within two full years
option2: Within seventy days
option3: Within seven years
option4: Before the next new moon
correct: Within two full years
explanation: Hananiah promised that God would break Babylon's yoke and repatriate looted temple treasures and exiles within an optimistic two full years. Jeremiah 28:3-4 (KJV) - "Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the LORD's house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place, and carried them to Babylon: And I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, that went into Babylon, saith the LORD: for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon."

question: What magnanimous, honest response did Jeremiah initially voice regarding Hananiah's optimistic prediction in Jeremiah 28:6?
option1: Thou art a liar and a deceiver, and the wrath of God shall consume thee
option2: Amen: the LORD do so: the LORD perform thy words which thou hast prophesied
option3: Behold, the Lord hath not spoken by thy mouth, for thou speakest vanity
option4: Shall a man believe a dream of peace when the sword of the Chaldeans is drawn?
correct: Amen: the LORD do so: the LORD perform thy words which thou hast prophesied
explanation: Jeremiah sincerely wished that Hananiah's words of peace were true ('Amen! Would that the Lord do so!'), demonstrating that he took no personal pleasure in preaching disaster. Jeremiah 28:6 (KJV) - "Even the prophet Jeremiah said, Amen: the LORD do so: the LORD perform thy words which thou hast prophesied, to bring again the vessels of the LORD's house, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon into this place."

question: According to ancient prophetic tradition, what is the biblical test of an authentic prophet of peace in Jeremiah 28:8-9?
option1: When he showeth a sign in the sun or moon, then shall he be believed
option2: When the high priest anointeth him with the holy oil of the sanctuary
option3: The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the LORD hath truly sent him
option4: When all the elders and princes of the people confirm his vision in the gate
correct: The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the LORD hath truly sent him
explanation: While ancient true prophets historically preached war and judgment against sin, anyone prophesying unconditional peace bears the burden of strict empirical fulfillment (Deuteronomy 18:22). Jeremiah 28:8-9 (KJV) - "The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence. The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the LORD hath truly sent him."

question: What dramatic violent act did Hananiah execute against Jeremiah in the presence of all the people in Jeremiah 28:10?
option1: Hananiah smote Jeremiah on the cheek and cast his prophetic mantle into the fire
option2: Hananiah pulled off Jeremiah's shoes and threw dust into his eyes
option3: Hananiah tore Jeremiah's scroll in pieces and trampled it before the priests
option4: Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah's neck, and brake it
correct: Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah's neck, and brake it
explanation: In a brazen public display, Hananiah seized the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck and smashed it to pieces, claiming God had broken Babylon's power. Jeremiah 28:10 (KJV) - "Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah's neck, and brake it."

question: How did Jeremiah react immediately following Hananiah's dramatic smashing of the yoke in Jeremiah 28:11?
option1: And the prophet Jeremiah went his way
option2: Jeremiah fell upon his face and wept bitterly in the court
option3: Jeremiah called down fire from heaven to consume Hananiah
option4: Jeremiah rebuked him with a loud voice and shook the dust from his feet
correct: And the prophet Jeremiah went his way
explanation: Showing magnificent poise and restraint, Jeremiah did not engage in undignified shouting: he quietly turned and walked away, waiting for Yahweh to speak. Jeremiah 28:11 (KJV) - "And Hananiah spake in the presence of all the people, saying, Thus saith the LORD; Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within the space of two full years. And the prophet Jeremiah went his way."

question: What inescapable substitute did God command to replace the broken wooden yoke in Jeremiah 28:13-14?
option1: Thou hast broken the cedar yoke; but I will forge bonds of bronze
option2: Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron
option3: Thou hast cast off the light harness; but I will put heavy chains upon their feet
option4: Thou hast despised the yoke of a servant; but I will make thee a slave under the whip
correct: Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron
explanation: Human rebellion only intensified servitude: breaking a wooden yoke resulted in an unbreakable yoke of iron upon all nations under Nebuchadnezzar. Jeremiah 28:13-14 (KJV) - "Go and tell Hananiah, saying, Thus saith the LORD; Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron. For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and they shall serve him: and I have given him the beasts of the field also."

question: What fatal judicial sentence did Jeremiah pronounce upon Hananiah in Jeremiah 28:16?
option1: Thou shalt be struck with leprosy, and thy tongue shall cleave to the roof of thy mouth
option2: Thou shalt be carried away in chains to Babylon, and die in the dungeon of the Chaldeans
option3: Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the LORD
option4: Thou shalt be stoned to death outside the gate of Benjamin before the next feast
correct: Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the LORD
explanation: Because Hananiah preached spiritual rebellion against God under the guise of prophecy, he was sentenced to capital punishment within that calendar year. Jeremiah 28:16 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the LORD."

question: When did Hananiah die, precisely fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy in Jeremiah 28:17?
option1: The following year in the first month
option2: Within two full years
option3: On the Day of Atonement in the third year
option4: The same year in the seventh month
correct: The same year in the seventh month
explanation: Just two months after his confrontation with Jeremiah in the fifth month, Hananiah died in the seventh month (Tishri) of 593 BC. Jeremiah 28:17 (KJV) - "So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month."

question: What specific indictment did Jeremiah level against Hananiah before pronouncing his doom in Jeremiah 28:15?
option1: The LORD hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie
option2: Thou hast taken bribes of silver from the princes of Egypt
option3: Thou hast profaned the holy vessels of the house of the LORD
option4: Thou hast consulted familiar spirits in the valley of Hinnom
correct: The LORD hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie
explanation: Hananiah committed the mortal sin of deceiving a vulnerable nation: 'The LORD hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie'. Jeremiah 28:15 (KJV) - "Then said the prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the prophet, Hear now, Hananiah; The LORD hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie."

question: Which two royal couriers carried Jeremiah's pastoral letter from Jerusalem to the exiles in Babylon in Jeremiah 29:3?
option1: Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah
option2: Baruch the son of Neriah, and Seraiah the son of Neriah
option3: Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
option4: Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah
correct: Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah
explanation: King Zedekiah sent an official diplomatic delegation to Nebuchadnezzar consisting of Elasah ben Shaphan and Gemariah ben Hilkiah, who carried Jeremiah's prophetic letter to the Jewish exiles. Jeremiah 29:3 (KJV) - "By the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, (whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent unto Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon) saying,"

question: What settle-down instructions did Jeremiah give to the Jewish exiles in Babylon in Jeremiah 29:5-6?
option1: Remain in tents as nomads, eat no wine, and prepare daily to march back to Zion
option2: Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters ... that ye may be increased there, and not diminished
option3: Refuse to learn the language of the Chaldeans, and hold solemn fasts in the streets
option4: Buy no land and plant no vines, for the captivity shall end within two full years
correct: Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters ... that ye may be increased there, and not diminished
explanation: Jeremiah instructed exiles to embrace long-term residency: build permanent houses, cultivate orchards, marry, raise families, and preserve demography. Jeremiah 29:5-6 (KJV) - "Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished."

question: What revolutionary pastoral principle regarding the pagan empire did Jeremiah command the exiles in Jeremiah 29:7?
option1: Curse the city of Babylon day and night, and pray for the Medes to overthrow her walls
option2: Separate yourselves from the heathen, and have no fellowship with their magistrates
option3: And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace
option4: Subvert their government secretly, and send intelligence to Pharaoh king of Egypt
correct: And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace
explanation: Exiles were commanded to contribute constructively to Babylonian civic welfare and pray for their pagan captors, because the shalom of the exile community was inextricably linked to the shalom of the city. Jeremiah 29:7 (KJV) - "And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace."

question: What celebrated promise of divine providence and gracious future does God unveil for the exiles in Jeremiah 29:11?
option1: For my covenant with your fathers cannot be broken, thoughts of victory and not of shame, to crown you with glory
option2: Behold, I will make you rulers over the provinces of the east, thoughts of wealth and not of poverty
option3: I have loved thee with an everlasting love, thoughts of deliverance and not of destruction
option4: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end
correct: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end
explanation: God reassures the displaced exiles that His sovereign designs for them are benevolent ('thoughts of shalom'), purposed to grant them a future and a hope ('an expected end' / acharit vetiqvah). Jeremiah 29:11 (KJV) - "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end."

question: What condition guarantees that seekers will successfully find God in Jeremiah 29:13?
option1: And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart
option2: When ye bring unblemished bullocks to the ruins of the altar in Jerusalem
option3: When ye fast forty days in the wilderness and put on sackcloth
option4: When ye swear allegiance to the righteous Branch of David
correct: And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart
explanation: God promises personal accessibility and relational discovery to those who seek Him wholeheartedly without divided allegiance. Jeremiah 29:13 (KJV) - "And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart."

question: Which two false prophets in Babylon did Jeremiah denounce for sexual immorality and lying prophecies, foretelling that Nebuchadnezzar would roast them in fire in Jeremiah 29:21-23?
option1: Hananiah the son of Azur, and Shemaiah the Nehelamite
option2: Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah
option3: Pashur the son of Immer, and Zephaniah the priest
option4: Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the scribe
correct: Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah
explanation: Ahab ben Kolaiah and Zedekiah ben Maaseiah preached seditious lies and seduced their neighbors' wives in Babylon; Nebuchadnezzar executed them by burning them alive in a furnace (roasting in fire). Jeremiah 29:21-22 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes; And of them shall be taken up a curse by all the captivity of Judah which are in Babylon, saying, The LORD make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire;"

question: What derogatory term did Shemaiah the Nehelamite use to describe Jeremiah in his subversive letter to the temple authorities in Jeremiah 29:26-27?
option1: A traitor of the covenant and a companion of the Chaldeans
option2: A false diviner who deceiveth the simple with visions of the night
option3: Every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks ... Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet
option4: A blasphemer of the temple and an enemy of the king of Judah
correct: Every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks ... Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet
explanation: Shemaiah wrote from Babylon demanding that Zephaniah lock up Jeremiah as a raving lunatic ('madman' / meshugga) masquerading as a prophet. Jeremiah 29:26-27 (KJV) - "The LORD hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the LORD, for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks. Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?"

question: How did Zephaniah the priest respond when he received Shemaiah's threatening letter from Babylon in Jeremiah 29:29?
option1: Zephaniah immediately put Jeremiah in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin
option2: Zephaniah burned the letter in the brazier of the king's winter house
option3: Zephaniah delivered Jeremiah into the hands of the princes to be executed
option4: And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet
correct: And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet
explanation: Rather than arresting Jeremiah, Priest Zephaniah acted with professional respect, reading Shemaiah's hostile letter aloud to Jeremiah so he was informed. Jeremiah 29:29 (KJV) - "And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet."

question: What divine punishment was pronounced upon Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his posterity in Jeremiah 29:32?
option1: He shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people
option2: He shall be roasted in the fire with Ahab and Zedekiah before the king of Babylon
option3: He shall be struck blind and wander as a beggar through the streets of Babylon
option4: His wife and sons shall be slain by the sword of the Chaldeans in the gate
correct: He shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people
explanation: Shemaiah's line would suffer dynastic extinction: none of his descendants would survive to see the joyful return of the exiles. Jeremiah 29:32 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: he shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, saith the LORD; because he hath taught rebellion against the LORD."

question: What agricultural metaphor from Chapter 24 is repeated in Chapter 29 to describe the fate of those remaining in Jerusalem under Zedekiah in Jeremiah 29:17?
option1: Like withered vines fit only for the fire
option2: Like vile figs, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil
option3: Like rotten pomegranates trampled in the dust
option4: Like bitter olives fallen before the harvest
correct: Like vile figs, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil
explanation: God reiterates the vision of the rotten, putrid figs: those who remained in Jerusalem under Zedekiah were doomed to sword, famine, and pestilence. Jeremiah 29:17 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will send upon them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make them like vile figs, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil."

question: What command initiates the celebrated 'Book of Consolation' (Chapters 30-33) in Jeremiah 30:2?
option1: Proclaim these words on the walls of Zion with a loud voice
option2: Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book
option3: Send this scroll unto all the synagogues of the dispersion
option4: Inscribe these promises on pillars of bronze before the temple
correct: Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book
explanation: God commanded Jeremiah to commit his comprehensive restoration prophecies to a permanent scroll ('in a book' / el-sefer) for future generations. Jeremiah 30:2 (KJV) - "Thus speaketh the LORD God of Israel, saying, Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book."

question: What vivid physiological image depicts the extreme terror of grown men in Jeremiah 30:6?
option1: Every warrior hath cast down his shield, and his knees smite together like water
option2: The mighty men have fainted in the streets, and their breath is gone from them
option3: Ask ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?
option4: Their bones shake like reeds in the wind, and their tongues cleave to their gums
correct: Ask ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?
explanation: Mighty warriors are gripped by such unendurable agony that they clutch their stomachs like women undergoing labor contractions, their faces drained pale. Jeremiah 30:6 (KJV) - "Ask ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?"

question: What monumental eschatological period of unprecedented tribulation is identified in Jeremiah 30:7?
option1: The day of the fierce anger of the LORD upon all nations
option2: The hour of temptation that shall come upon the whole earth
option3: The valley of Jehoshaphat where the heathen are judged
option4: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it
correct: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it
explanation: 'The time of Jacob's trouble' denotes an incomparable climactic period of intense covenant distress, crowned with the absolute guarantee of divine deliverance ('he shall be saved out of it'). Jeremiah 30:7 (KJV) - "Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it."

question: Whom will the redeemed nation serve when the foreign yoke is shattered from their neck in Jeremiah 30:9?
option1: They shall serve the LORD their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them
option2: The high priest of the sanctuary and the seventy elders of Zion
option3: The princes of Judah and the governors of the provinces
option4: The angel of his presence who led their fathers out of Egypt
correct: They shall serve the LORD their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them
explanation: Liberated Israel will serve Yahweh their God and the Davidic Messiah-King ('David their king'), raised up in resurrection power. Jeremiah 30:9 (KJV) - "But they shall serve the LORD their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them."

question: What principle of measured discipline preserves Israel while pagan superpowers perish in Jeremiah 30:11?
option1: Because of the blood of the paschal lamb, no plague shall touch the seed of Jacob
option2: Though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure
option3: The mountains shall depart and the hills be removed, but my kindness shall not depart
option4: I have sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David or forsake his seed
correct: Though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure
explanation: Ancient superpowers that oppressed Israel (Assyria, Babylon) suffered complete extinction ('a full end'); but Israel receives measured corrective discipline ('in measure' / lamishpat), guaranteeing perpetual survival. Jeremiah 30:11 (KJV) - "For I am with thee, saith the LORD, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished."

question: What medical hopelessness characterizes Zion's condition before divine intervention in Jeremiah 30:12-13?
option1: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores
option2: The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint; the balm of Gilead hath failed
option3: Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines
option4: Thy leprosy is deep-seated in the walls of thy house, and thou art unclean
correct: Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines
explanation: Humanly speaking, Zion's moral and political wound was fatal and incurable: no physician or medication existed to heal her. Jeremiah 30:12-13 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD, Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines."

question: What miraculous promise of supernatural surgery reverses Zion's incurable plight in Jeremiah 30:17?
option1: I will send the balm of Gilead and anoint thy head with holy oil of gladness
option2: I will wash away thy filth with the blood of the righteous Branch of David
option3: I will open fountains in the midst of the valleys to cleanse all thy bruises
option4: For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the LORD; because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after
correct: For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the LORD; because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after
explanation: Where human medicine fails, Yahweh Himself intervenes as Great Physician to heal the despised 'Outcast' whom no nation cared for. Jeremiah 30:17 (KJV) - "For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the LORD; because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after."

question: What architectural and urban rebirth is foretold for the ruined city in Jeremiah 30:18?
option1: The city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof
option2: The walls shall be rebuilt with stones of sapphire and the gates of carbuncles
option3: The city shall be extended from the tower of Hananeel unto the corner gate
option4: The temple shall be established on the top of the mountains above all hills
correct: The city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof
explanation: Jerusalem will rise directly from her own archaeological ruin mound ('tel' / heap), and the royal palace will be re-inhabited in former grandeur. Jeremiah 30:18 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob's tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof."

question: What distinctive priest-king privilege will characterize the native ruler raised up from among their own people in Jeremiah 30:21?
option1: He shall sit upon the golden throne of Solomon and judge the twelve tribes of Israel
option2: Their governor shall proceed from the midst of them; and I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me: for who is this that engaged his heart to approach unto me?
option3: He shall wear the royal diadem of David and wield an iron sceptre over the Gentiles
option4: He shall conquer all the kingdoms of the north and bring tribute of silver into Zion
correct: Their governor shall proceed from the midst of them; and I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me: for who is this that engaged his heart to approach unto me?
explanation: The coming Ruler will not be a foreign puppet, but an indigenous Leader endowed with priestly access to approach God's presence directly - a unique Messianic attribute. Jeremiah 30:21 (KJV) - "And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them; and I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me: for who is this that engaged his heart to approach unto me? saith the LORD."

question: What classic covenant formula seals the restoration promise in Jeremiah 30:22?
option1: I have sworn by myself that my covenant with thee shall never fail
option2: Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified
option3: And ye shall be my people, and I will be your God
option4: The LORD shall reign over them in Mount Zion from henceforth, even forever
correct: And ye shall be my people, and I will be your God
explanation: The fundamental goal of redemptive history is reaffirmed: full, unbroken mutual belonging between Yahweh and His people. Jeremiah 30:22 (KJV) - "And ye shall be my people, and I will be your God."

question: What sublime declaration of eternal divine affection opens God's words to Israel in Jeremiah 31:3?
option1: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands: thy walls are continually before me
option2: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?
option3: Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee
option4: I will betroth thee unto me forever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness
correct: Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee
explanation: God grounds Israel's restoration in unconditional, primordial grace: an 'everlasting love' (ahavat olam) that persistently draws her with covenant loyalty (chesed). Jeremiah 31:3 (KJV) - "The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee."

question: Which ancestral matriarch is depicted weeping inconsolably for her exiled children in Ramah in Jeremiah 31:15?
option1: Sarah weeping in the cave of Machpelah for the dispersion of Isaac's seed
option2: Rebekah mourning from the borders of Bethel for Jacob's wandering sons
option3: Leah lamenting in the gates of Shiloh for the captivity of Judah
option4: Rachel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not
correct: Rachel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not
explanation: Rachel - mother of Joseph and Benjamin, buried near Ramah - is personified as weeping from the grave as exiles are marched past in chains (quoted in Matthew 2:18 regarding Herod's slaughter of the innocents). Jeremiah 31:15 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD; A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rahel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not."

question: What animal metaphor does Ephraim use to describe his past wild rebellion and need for divine conversion in Jeremiah 31:18?
option1: Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I shall be turned; for thou art the LORD my God
option2: I was as a wild ass snuffing up the wind in the desert: tame me, O Lord
option3: I was as a wandering sheep that forsook the fold: seek thy servant, O Shepherd
option4: I was as a roaring lion seeking prey in the forest: break my teeth, O God
correct: Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I shall be turned; for thou art the LORD my God
explanation: Ephraim confesses that he acted like an unbroken, undisciplined young bull flailing against the plow-yoke, praying: 'Turn thou me, and I shall be turned'. Jeremiah 31:18 (KJV) - "I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself thus; Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I shall be turned; for thou art the LORD my God."

question: What mysterious 'new thing' created in the earth is announced in Jeremiah 31:22?
option1: A virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel
option2: The LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man
option3: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock
option4: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy
correct: The LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man
explanation: Denoting a miraculous reversal of vulnerability, weak Israel ('a woman') will surround, shelter, or turn to Yahweh ('a man') in sovereign restoration. Jeremiah 31:22 (KJV) - "How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man."

question: What popular fatalistic proverb of intergenerational guilt will be permanently abolished in Jeremiah 31:29-30?
option1: The parents have sown iniquity, and the sons have reaped the whirlwind
option2: The kings have made alliances with Egypt, and the poor are delivered to Babylon
option3: The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge
option4: The elders have built altars on the high hills, and the infants perish in Tophet
correct: The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge
explanation: The cynical proverb blaming ancestors for present suffering is replaced by strict individual moral accountability: every person shall die for their own iniquity. Jeremiah 31:29-30 (KJV) - "In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge. But every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge."

question: With whom does God promise to inaugurate the monumental New Covenant in Jeremiah 31:31?
option1: With the seed of David and the sons of Aaron exclusively
option2: With all the Gentile nations of the ends of the earth
option3: With the faithful remnant of the Rechabites and the prophets
option4: With the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah
correct: With the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah
explanation: The New Covenant (Berit Chadashah) is formally established with the reunited twelve tribes: both the northern kingdom (house of Israel) and southern kingdom (house of Judah). Jeremiah 31:31 (KJV) - "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:"

question: How does the internal medium of the New Covenant contrast with the external Sinaitic Covenant in Jeremiah 31:33?
option1: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people
option2: I will carve my commandments upon tablets of polished gold and deposit them in the Ark
option3: I will send angels to proclaim my statutes with a trumpet from the summit of Mount Zion
option4: I will establish twelve schools of the prophets throughout all the cities of Judah
correct: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people
explanation: Rather than being inscribed externally on stone tablets that could be broken, God's Torah in the New Covenant is supernaturally internalized and engraved directly upon the human heart by the Holy Spirit. Jeremiah 31:33 (KJV) - "But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people."

question: What universal personal knowledge of God will characterize all members of the New Covenant in Jeremiah 31:34?
option1: All people shall speak with new tongues and understand the mystery of the seraphim
option2: And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them
option3: Every child shall be endowed with the wisdom of Solomon and the discernment of Daniel
option4: No man shall need a scribe or a priest, for the glory of the temple shall fill their houses
correct: And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them
explanation: Under the New Covenant, direct, unmediated experiential knowledge of Yahweh is democratized to every believer, from the humblest to the greatest. Jeremiah 31:34 (KJV) - "And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the LORD: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more."

question: What ultimate redemptive foundation secures all the blessings of the New Covenant in Jeremiah 31:34?
option1: For I will multiply their seed as the stars of heaven and give them the gate of their enemies
option2: For I have accepted the burnt offerings of rams and the blood of unblemished bullocks
option3: For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more
option4: For my servant David shall rule over them with an iron sceptre in righteousness
correct: For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more
explanation: The crowning pinnacle of the New Covenant is absolute, irreversible pardon: total vicarious atonement where God permanently blots out sins from divine remembrance (Hebrews 8:12; 10:17). Jeremiah 31:34 (KJV) - " ... for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more."

question: What cosmic celestial ordinances guarantee the eternal national preservation of Israel before God in Jeremiah 31:35-36?
option1: The foundations of the mountains set in the deep: if the rocks be dissolved, then shall Israel fail
option2: The sandy bounds of the sea by a perpetual decree: if the waves prevail, then shall Israel be blotted out
option3: The snow of Lebanon and the cold flowing streams: if they dry up, then shall my covenant be broken
option4: The sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night: if those ordinances depart, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation
correct: The sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night: if those ordinances depart, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation
explanation: Israel's national survival is as indestructible as the physical laws governing the solar and planetary system: only if the celestial universe collapses can Israel cease to exist as a nation before God. Jeremiah 31:35-36 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever."

question: Where was Jeremiah confined when the word of the LORD came to him during Nebuchadnezzar's final siege in the tenth year of Zedekiah in Jeremiah 32:1-2?
option1: Cast into the dungeon of Malchiah in the mire
option2: Incarcerated in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin
option3: Bound in chains in the chamber of Elishama the scribe
option4: Shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah's house
correct: Shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah's house
explanation: King Zedekiah had placed Jeremiah under protective house arrest in the palace guardhouse ('court of the prison' / chatser hammattarah) because of his defeatist prophecies. Jeremiah 32:2 (KJV) - "For then the king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah's house."

question: Who visited Jeremiah in prison to exercise the familial right of redemption (go'el) over ancestral land in Jeremiah 32:7-8?
option1: Hanameel the son of Shallum his uncle
option2: Baruch the son of Neriah his scribe
option3: Ahikam the son of Shaphan his friend
option4: Gedaliah the son of Pashur the prince
correct: Hanameel the son of Shallum his uncle
explanation: In fulfillment of Leviticus 25:25, Jeremiah's first cousin Hanameel ben Shallum offered him the redemption rights to purchase ancestral family land in Anathoth. Jeremiah 32:7-8 (KJV) - "Behold, Hanameel the son of Shallum thine uncle shall come unto thee, saying, Buy thee my field that is in Anathoth: for the right of redemption is thine to buy it. So Hanameel mine uncle's son came to me in the court of the prison according to the word of the LORD, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth ... for the right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine; buy it for thyself. Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD."

question: What exact purchase price did Jeremiah weigh out to buy the field in Anathoth in Jeremiah 32:9?
option1: Thirty pieces of silver
option2: Seventeen shekels of silver
option3: Fifty shekels of gold
option4: Ten talents of silver
correct: Seventeen shekels of silver
explanation: Jeremiah weighed out seventeen silver shekels on commercial balance scales in the presence of legal witnesses. Jeremiah 32:9 (KJV) - "And I bought the field of Hanameel my uncle's son, that was in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, even seventeen shekels of silver."

question: What legal deeds were executed, and to whom did Jeremiah entrust them in Jeremiah 32:10-12?
option1: Two tablets of clay sealed with the king's signet, entrusted unto Zephaniah the priest
option2: A roll of parchment inscribed with iron ink, entrusted unto Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
option3: The evidence of the purchase, both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open, entrusted unto Baruch the son of Neriah
option4: A brass deed signed by seventy elders, entrusted unto Gemariah the son of Shaphan
correct: The evidence of the purchase, both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open, entrusted unto Baruch the son of Neriah
explanation: Under ancient legal practice, dual deed scrolls were produced - a sealed copy for archival security and an unsealed copy for public inspection - entrusted to his scribe Baruch. Jeremiah 32:11-12 (KJV) - "So I took the evidence of the purchase, both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open: And I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the sight of Hanameel mine uncle's son, and in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison."

question: Where was Baruch instructed to store the legal deeds, and for what purpose in Jeremiah 32:14?
option1: Bury them beneath the altar of burnt offering in the temple
option2: Hide them in a secret chamber of the palace of Solomon
option3: Carry them to Babylon and deposit them in the house of the exiles
option4: Put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days
correct: Put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days
explanation: Storing parchment in sealed earthenware jars (identical to the preservation technique used for the Dead Sea Scrolls at Qumran) preserved the legal title deeds through decades of war and exile. Jeremiah 32:14 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Take these evidences, this evidence of the purchase, both which is sealed, and this evidence which is open; and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days."

question: What prophetic hope and commercial reality was affirmed by the purchase of this field in enemy-occupied territory in Jeremiah 32:15?
option1: Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land
option2: The temple shall be rebuilt with gold of Ophir within seventy weeks
option3: The king of Babylon shall surrender his crown to the princes of Judah
option4: The land of Benjamin shall be divided among the sons of the priests forever
correct: Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land
explanation: Investing money in real estate while the Babylonian siege engines pounded the walls was an astonishing act of faith: proving that Jewish life, property ownership, and agriculture would definitively be restored. Jeremiah 32:15 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land."

question: What famous affirmation of divine omnipotence opens Jeremiah's prayer of perplexity in Jeremiah 32:17?
option1: O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen?
option2: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee
option3: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable
option4: The LORD our God is one LORD: and blessed be his glorious name forever
correct: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee
explanation: Jeremiah addresses Creator God: 'there is nothing too hard for thee' (lo-yipale mimkha kol-davar). Jeremiah 32:17 (KJV) - "Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:"

question: How does God echo and confirm Jeremiah's theological confession in Jeremiah 32:27?
option1: Fear not, Jeremiah: for as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways
option2: Can a man question his Maker, or the clay say to the potter, What makest thou?
option3: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?
option4: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord
correct: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?
explanation: God takes Jeremiah's prayer statement and turns it into an omnipotent rhetorical question: 'is there any thing too hard for me?' Jeremiah 32:27 (KJV) - "Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?"

question: What two inward gifts will God grant His gathered people in the Everlasting Covenant in Jeremiah 32:39-40?
option1: A golden crown, and an iron sceptre, that they may rule over the heathen
option2: A tongue of fire, and an unshakeable spirit, that they may prophesy to all nations
option3: Ten thousand chariots, and horses from Egypt, that they may defend Zion
option4: One heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever ... I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me
correct: One heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever ... I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me
explanation: God guarantees eternal covenant stability by transforming human hearts: imparting 'one heart and one way' and infusing holy reverential fear so they never backslide again. Jeremiah 32:39-40 (KJV) - "And I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for the good of them, and of their children after them: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from them, to do them good; but I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me."

question: With what extraordinary depth of divine emotion does God promise to re-plant His people in the promised land in Jeremiah 32:41?
option1: Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul
option2: I will plant them according to the oath sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
option3: I will establish them with the arm of my power and with the breath of my mouth
option4: I will watch over them with the host of my holy angels night and day
correct: Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul
explanation: In an anthropomorphism of breathtaking tenderness, God declares He will plant them back into the land with His 'whole heart and with my whole soul'. Jeremiah 32:41 (KJV) - "Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul."

question: What famous invitation to prayer and revelatory promise is delivered to Jeremiah while confined in prison in Jeremiah 33:3?
option1: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not
option2: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession
option3: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near
option4: Pray without ceasing, and I will deliver this city from the hand of the king of Babylon
correct: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not
explanation: Known as 'God's telephone number' (Jeremiah 33:3), God invites His confined prophet to pray, promising to unveil inaccessible, hidden mysteries ('mighty/fenced-in things' / betsorot). Jeremiah 33:3 (KJV) - "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not."

question: What liturgical hymn of temple praise will resound again in the desolate streets of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 33:11?
option1: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory
option2: Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD
option3: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God
option4: The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad thereof
correct: Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD
explanation: Jerusalem's silent, burned ruins will once again reverberate with temple thanksgiving choirs singing the classic liturgical refrain: 'Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever' (Hodu le-Yahweh Tseva'ot ki-tov Yahweh ki-le'olam chasdo). Jeremiah 33:11 (KJV) - "The voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say, Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD. For I will cause to return the captivity of the land, as at the first, saith the LORD."

question: What pastoral accounting metaphor describes the peaceful return of thriving flocks in Jeremiah 33:13?
option1: The sheep shall graze upon the hills without fear of wolves
option2: The shepherds shall lead them beside the still waters of Siloam
option3: The flocks pass again under the hands of him that telleth them
option4: The lambs shall be gathered in the shepherd's bosom
correct: The flocks pass again under the hands of him that telleth them
explanation: Flocks will safely pass one by one under the shepherd's counting rod ('him that telleth / counteth them') across Judean hills and villages. Jeremiah 33:13 (KJV) - "In the cities of the mountains, in the cities of the vale, and in the cities of the south, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shall the flocks pass again under the hands of him that telleth them, saith the LORD."

question: What Messianic title and royal function is reiterated in Jeremiah 33:15?
option1: A King of peace shall arise from Bethlehem, and with an iron rod shall he rule all nations
option2: A Star shall come out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel to smite the corners of Moab
option3: A faithful Priest shall build an enduring house, and walk before mine Anointed forever
option4: In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land
correct: In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land
explanation: God re-affirms the prophecy of Jeremiah 23:5: raising up 'the Branch of righteousness' (Tsemach Tsedaqah) from David's line. Jeremiah 33:15 (KJV) - "In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land."

question: What name is applied to restored Jerusalem in Jeremiah 33:16, reflecting the character of her Messianic King?
option1: The LORD our righteousness
option2: The City of Peace
option3: The Lord is There (Yahweh Shammah)
option4: The Throne of Glory
correct: The LORD our righteousness
explanation: Remarkably, the very title given to the Messiah in Jeremiah 23:6 ('YAHWEH TSIDQENU' - The LORD our righteousness) is here bestowed upon redeemed Jerusalem herself, reflecting her total transformation into His likeness. Jeremiah 33:16 (KJV) - "In those days shall Judah be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell safely: and this is the name wherewith she shall be called, The LORD our righteousness."

question: What perpetual royal promise to the house of David is reaffirmed in Jeremiah 33:17?
option1: David's lineage shall defeat all the kingdoms of the north with the sword
option2: David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel
option3: David's house shall dwell in palaces of cedar until the end of the world
option4: David's descendants shall wear the golden crown in the temple of Solomon
correct: David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel
explanation: The Davidic Covenant (2 Samuel 7) is perpetual: an eternal King from David's line will reign unbroken (ultimately fulfilled in Christ, Luke 1:32-33). Jeremiah 33:17 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD; David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel;"

question: What parallel perpetual promise is granted to the Levitical priests in Jeremiah 33:18?
option1: The Levites shall inherit the finest vineyards of Samaria and the pastures of Bashan
option2: The high priest shall wear the Urim and Thummim throughout all generations
option3: Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually
option4: The sons of Zadok shall be made princes over all the governors of Judah
correct: Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually
explanation: Alongside the Davidic monarchy, God guarantees that legitimate Levitical ministry will never perish from His presence. Jeremiah 33:18 (KJV) - "Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually."

question: What cosmic comparison proves the absolute impossibility of breaking God's covenant with David and the Levites in Jeremiah 33:20-21?
option1: If the sand of the seashore can be measured by human hands, then can my covenant fail
option2: If the snow of Mount Hermon can be melted in a single hour, then shall my oath be forgotten
option3: If the stars of heaven can fall into the depths of the sea, then shall the throne of David be overthrown
option4: If ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, and that there should not be day and night in their season; Then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant
correct: If ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, and that there should not be day and night in their season; Then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant
explanation: The alternation of day and night is established by an inviolable cosmic treaty; only if day and night cease their appointed cycles can God's covenant with David be broken. Jeremiah 33:20-21 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD; If ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, and that there should not be day and night in their season; Then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant, that he should not have a son to reign upon his throne; and with the Levites the priests, my ministers."

question: What two chosen families did cynical skeptics claim God had permanently cast off in Jeremiah 33:24?
option1: The two families which the LORD hath chosen, he hath even cast them off (Israel and Judah / David and Levi)
option2: The family of Aaron and the family of Moses
option3: The house of Joseph and the house of Benjamin
option4: The clan of Caleb and the clan of Joshua
correct: The two families which the LORD hath chosen, he hath even cast them off (Israel and Judah / David and Levi)
explanation: Pessimists mockingly asserted that God had discarded the two chosen families (the royal house of David and the priestly house of Levi, or the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah). Jeremiah 33:24 (KJV) - "Considerest thou not what this people have spoken, saying, The two families which the LORD hath chosen, he hath even cast them off? thus they have despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them."

question: To what astronomical and geological vastness does God compare the multiplication of David's seed and the Levites in Jeremiah 33:22?
option1: As the drops of morning dew upon the grass of the field
option2: As the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites
option3: As the grains of wheat in the royal storehouses of Solomon
option4: As the leaves of the forest of Lebanon in summer
correct: As the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites
explanation: Reiterating the Abrahamic promise (Genesis 15:5; 22:17), God guarantees unmeasurable numerical expansion to the seed of David and His ministers. Jeremiah 33:22 (KJV) - "As the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites that minister unto me."

question: What personal fate did Jeremiah foretell to King Zedekiah concerning his confrontation with Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 34:3?
option1: Thou shalt be slain with the edge of the sword before the Water Gate
option2: Thine eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth, and thou shalt go to Babylon
option3: Thou shalt escape across the Jordan and be protected by the king of Moab
option4: Thou shalt be cast into the pit of Tophet and denied royal burial
correct: Thine eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth, and thou shalt go to Babylon
explanation: Zedekiah would suffer face-to-face interrogation by Nebuchadnezzar (at Riblah) before being deported to Babylon. Jeremiah 34:3 (KJV) - "And thou shalt not escape out of his hand, but shalt surely be taken, and delivered into his hand; and thine eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth, and thou shalt go to Babylon."

question: What comforting caveat was granted to King Zedekiah regarding his manner of death in Jeremiah 34:4-5?
option1: Thou shalt return to Jerusalem in thy old age and be buried in the sepulchre of David
option2: Thou shalt reign twenty years as a tributary king in the province of Babylon
option3: Thou shalt not die by the sword: But thou shalt die in peace: and with the burnings of thy fathers ... so shall they burn odours for thee; and they will lament thee, saying, Ah lord!
option4: Thou shalt die with thy sons around thee in a palace of cedar
correct: Thou shalt not die by the sword: But thou shalt die in peace: and with the burnings of thy fathers ... so shall they burn odours for thee; and they will lament thee, saying, Ah lord!
explanation: Though blinded, Zedekiah would not be executed by the sword; he would die a natural death in captivity, honored with traditional royal funeral incense burnings. Jeremiah 34:4-5 (KJV) - "Yet hear the word of the LORD, O Zedekiah king of Judah; Thus saith the LORD of thee, Thou shalt not die by the sword: But thou shalt die in peace: and with the burnings of thy fathers, the former kings which were before thee, so shall they burn odours for thee; and they will lament thee, saying, Ah lord! for I have pronounced the word, saith the LORD."

question: Which two fortified provincial outposts were the only remaining fortified cities in Judah holding out against the Babylonians alongside Jerusalem in Jeremiah 34:7?
option1: Hebron and Beersheba
option2: Bethlehem and Tekoa
option3: Gibeon and Mizpah
