option4: Lachish and Azekah
correct: Lachish and Azekah
explanation: Lachish and Azekah - strategic southwestern fortress cities guarding the Shephelah passes - were the last two fortified strongholds resisting Nebuchadnezzar (corroborated by the famous archaeological Lachish Ostraca). Jeremiah 34:7 (KJV) - "When the king of Babylon's army fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish, and against Azekah: for these defenced cities remained of the cities of Judah."

question: What covenant of social emancipation did King Zedekiah and the Judean princes enact during the siege crisis in Jeremiah 34:8-9?
option1: To proclaim liberty unto them; That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free
option2: To forgive all debts of silver and restore all mortgaged lands to the poor
option3: To distribute all royal grain storehouses freely to every family in Jerusalem
option4: To consecrate all firstborn sons to minister as Levites at the bronze altar
correct: To proclaim liberty unto them; That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free
explanation: Pressured by the desperate siege, Zedekiah led the aristocracy in a solemn covenant to obey the Sabbatical Torah law (Exodus 21:2; Deuteronomy 15:12) releasing all enslaved Hebrew brethren. Jeremiah 34:8-9 (KJV) - "This is the word that came unto Jeremiah from the LORD, after that the king Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people which were at Jerusalem, to proclaim liberty unto them; That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother."

question: What hypocritical treachery did the slaveowners commit as soon as the Babylonian army temporarily withdrew to engage Pharaoh's army in Jeremiah 34:11?
option1: They drove the freed slaves out of the city gates into the hands of the Chaldeans
option2: They turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection for servants and for handmaids
option3: They forced the freed servants to pay seventy shekels of silver for their redemption
option4: They murdered the elders who had witnessed the signing of the covenant
correct: They turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection for servants and for handmaids
explanation: The moment the immediate military threat evaporated, the greedy masters reneged on their sacred oath, re-enslaving their freed brethren and profaning God's name. Jeremiah 34:11 (KJV) - "But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection for servants and for handmaids."

question: What ironic, retaliatory 'liberty' does God proclaim against the treacherous slaveowners in Jeremiah 34:17?
option1: I proclaim a liberty for your enemies to plunder all your gold and silver
option2: I proclaim a liberty for the fire to consume your cedar palaces without quenching
option3: Behold, I proclaim a liberty for you, saith the LORD, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine; and I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth
option4: I proclaim a liberty for wild beasts to devour your children in the streets
correct: Behold, I proclaim a liberty for you, saith the LORD, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine; and I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth
explanation: With terrifying irony, God declares: since they refused to grant liberty to their brothers, He grants them 'liberty' to be slaughtered by the sword, plague, and starvation. Jeremiah 34:17 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD; Ye have not hearkened unto me, in proclaiming liberty, every one to his brother, and every man to his neighbour: behold, I proclaim a liberty for you, saith the LORD, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine; and I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth."

question: What ancient ritual ceremony of self-malediction had the princes and priests performed when ratifying the covenant in the temple in Jeremiah 34:18?
option1: They sprinkled blood on the horns of the altar and drank wine from silver bowls
option2: They broke an earthen jar and cast the pieces into the brook Kidron
option3: They burned a ram on the altar and swore by the life of King Zedekiah
option4: They cut the calf in twain, and passed between the parts thereof
correct: They cut the calf in twain, and passed between the parts thereof
explanation: Drawing on the ancient covenant ritual (Genesis 15:10, 17), participants sliced a sacrificial calf in two and walked between the severed halves, invoking: 'May God do so to me and cut me in two if I break this oath!' Jeremiah 34:18 (KJV) - "And I will give the men that have transgressed my covenant, which have not performed the words of the covenant which they had made before me, when they cut the calf in twain, and passed between the parts thereof,"

question: Who specifically participated in this covenant ritual of passing between the severed parts of the calf in Jeremiah 34:19?
option1: The princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, and the priests, and all the people of the land
option2: The king alone and his royal sons before the high priest
option3: The seventy elders and the captains of the host of Benjamin
option4: The scribes and the Levites who ministered at the doors
correct: The princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, and the priests, and all the people of the land
explanation: Every echelon of leadership - civil nobility, palace court eunuchs, priesthood, and common citizens - participated in the solemn oath. Jeremiah 34:19 (KJV) - "The princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, and the priests, and all the people of the land, which passed between the parts of the calf;"

question: What divine command guarantees the return of the departed Babylonian army in Jeremiah 34:22?
option1: I will send an east wind to scatter Pharaoh's chariots, and Babylon shall return in wrath
option2: Behold, I will command, saith the LORD, and cause them to return to this city; and they shall fight against it, and take it, and burn it with fire
option3: I will kindle a fire in the borders of Egypt, and Nebuchadnezzar shall march through Zion
option4: I will whistle for the Chaldean eagle from the north to swoop down upon the carcass
correct: Behold, I will command, saith the LORD, and cause them to return to this city; and they shall fight against it, and take it, and burn it with fire
explanation: The temporary lifting of the siege was illusory: God would summon Nebuchadnezzar's legions back to storm, capture, and burn Jerusalem to the ground. Jeremiah 34:22 (KJV) - "Behold, I will command, saith the LORD, and cause them to return to this city; and they shall fight against it, and take it, and burn it with fire: and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without an inhabitant."

question: According to the Mosaic Torah cited in Jeremiah 34:14, after how many years of service must a Hebrew slave be granted unconditional freedom?
option1: At the end of forty-nine years, in the year of Jubilee
option2: At the end of three years of labor
option3: At the end of seven years ... when he hath served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free
option4: At the death of the master of the house
correct: At the end of seven years ... when he hath served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free
explanation: Exodus 21:2 and Deuteronomy 15:12 mandate that Hebrew slaves serve a maximum of six years, receiving complete release at the start of the seventh Sabbatical year. Jeremiah 34:14 (KJV) - "At the end of seven years let ye go every man his brother an Hebrew, which hath been sold unto thee; and when he hath served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free from thee: but your fathers hearkened not unto me, neither inclined their ear."

question: Which nomadic clan was Jeremiah commanded to bring into one of the temple chambers to offer them wine in Jeremiah 35:2?
option1: The sons of the Kenites
option2: The house of the Gibeonites
option3: The house of the Rechabites
option4: The clan of the Korahites
correct: The house of the Rechabites
explanation: Jeremiah was instructed to invite the Rechabites - a conservative nomadic clan descended from the Kenites - into a temple hall to test their obedience. Jeremiah 35:2 (KJV) - "Go unto the house of the Rechabites, and speak unto them, and bring them into the house of the LORD, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink."

question: Who was the leader of the Rechabites whom Jeremiah escorted into the temple in Jeremiah 35:3?
option1: Jonadab the son of Rechab
option2: Malkijah the son of Rechab
option3: Shelemiah the son of Abdeel
option4: Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah
correct: Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah
explanation: Jeremiah gathered clan chief Jaazaniah ben Jeremiah ben Habaziniah along with his brothers, sons, and the entire Rechabite community. Jeremiah 35:3 (KJV) - "Then I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah, and his brethren, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;"

question: Into whose temple chamber were the Rechabites brought when wine was set before them in Jeremiah 35:4?
option1: The chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God
option2: The chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe
option3: The chamber of Elishama the royal scribe
option4: The chamber of Pashur the chief governor
correct: The chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God
explanation: They were brought into the spacious upper temple room belonging to the disciples of Hanan ben Igdaliah, revered as a 'man of God'. Jeremiah 35:4 (KJV) - "And I brought them into the house of the LORD, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was by the chamber of the princes, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the door:"

question: What ancestor had commanded the Rechabites never to drink wine or cultivate land, and how long had they obeyed his charge in Jeremiah 35:6-8?
option1: Jethro the priest of Midian (during the Exodus)
option2: Jonadab the son of Rechab our father (approximately 250 years earlier)
option3: Heber the Kenite (in the days of Deborah)
option4: Phinehas the son of Eleazar (in the plains of Moab)
correct: Jonadab the son of Rechab our father (approximately 250 years earlier)
explanation: Jonadab (Jehonadab) ben Rechab - who joined Jehu in eradicating Baal worship around 841 BC (2 Kings 10:15-23) - commanded ascetic vows faithfully kept for two and a half centuries. Jeremiah 35:6 (KJV) - "But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever:"

question: What three lifestyle restrictions did Jonadab impose upon his descendants to preserve their nomadic simplicity in Jeremiah 35:7?
option1: Eat no leavened bread, wear no linen garments, and shave not your heads
option2: Drink no strong drink, marry no foreign wives, and enter no walled cities
option3: Neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents
option4: Possess no gold or silver, ride no horses, and sacrifice no sheep
correct: Neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents
explanation: Jonadab prohibited permanent architecture (houses), agriculture (sowing seed), and viticulture (vineyards), commanding perpetual tent dwelling to resist Canaanite agrarian decadence. Jeremiah 35:7 (KJV) - "Neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents; that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers."

question: Why had the nomadic Rechabites temporarily moved inside the walled city of Jerusalem contrary to their normal custom in Jeremiah 35:11?
option1: To attend the solemn feast of Tabernacles in the house of the LORD
option2: To sell their wool and herds to the merchants of Egypt
option3: Because a severe drought dried up the pasturelands in the desert of Judah
option4: For fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians
correct: For fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians
explanation: Invading Babylonian and Aramean raiding forces sweeping across the countryside forced them to take emergency military refuge inside Jerusalem's walls. Jeremiah 35:11 (KJV) - "But it came to pass, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up into the land, that we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians: so we dwell at Jerusalem."

question: What humiliating contrast did God draw between the Rechabites and the citizens of Judah in Jeremiah 35:14-16?
option1: The sons of Jonadab obeyed their fallible human father's commandment for generations without breaking it, whereas Judah refused to obey their living Creator though He spoke persistently, rising early and speaking
option2: The Rechabites offered sacrifices with pure hands, while the priests of Zion profaned the altar with strange fire
option3: The Rechabites kept the sabbaths in the desert, while Jerusalem traded in the gates on holy days
option4: The Rechabites loved the poor, while the house of David oppressed the fatherless and widow
correct: The sons of Jonadab obeyed their fallible human father's commandment for generations without breaking it, whereas Judah refused to obey their living Creator though He spoke persistently, rising early and speaking
explanation: The Rechabites demonstrated unwavering loyalty to an ancient mortal ancestor's ascetic rules, while Judah flagrantly defied the repeated commandments of their eternal Creator God. Jeremiah 35:14, 16 (KJV) - "The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me ... Because the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of their father, which he commanded them; but this people hath not hearkened unto me:"

question: What perpetual covenant blessing did God pronounce upon the house of the Rechabites for their faithful obedience in Jeremiah 35:19?
option1: They shall inherit the fertile terraces of Carmel and the springs of Jericho
option2: Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever
option3: Their sons shall be made governors in the provinces of Babylon
option4: They shall be anointed high priests in the temple of Zion forever
correct: Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever
explanation: The phrase 'to stand before me' (la'amod lefanay) denotes priestly and covenantal service in God's presence, guaranteeing perpetual lineage survival and divine favor. Jeremiah 35:19 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever."

question: During which king's reign did the prophetic test of the Rechabites take place in Jeremiah 35:1?
option1: In the days of Zedekiah the son of Josiah
option2: In the days of Jehoiachin the son of Jehoiakim
option3: In the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah
option4: In the days of Josiah the son of Amon
correct: In the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah
explanation: This event occurred during the turbulent reign of King Jehoiakim (circa 601-598 BC) when Babylonian raiding bands invaded Judah. Jeremiah 35:1 (KJV) - "The word which came unto Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,"

question: What did Jeremiah set before the Rechabites in the temple chamber in Jeremiah 35:5?
option1: Golden flagons of sweet wine and loaves of shewbread
option2: Bowls of spiced wine and roasted flesh of sheep
option3: Flagons of strong drink and censers of frankincense
option4: Pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine
correct: Pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine
explanation: Jeremiah placed large flagons/pitchers of wine and individual cups before them, issuing the formal invitation: 'Drink ye wine'. Jeremiah 35:5 (KJV) - "And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine."

question: In which regnal year of Jehoiakim was Jeremiah commanded to compile all his spoken prophecies into a formal scroll in Jeremiah 36:1-2?
option1: The fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month
option2: The first year of Zedekiah king of Judah
option3: The eleventh year of Jehoiakim, before his death
option4: The fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah
correct: The fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah
explanation: In 605 BC (the fourth year of Jehoiakim, following the Battle of Carchemish), God ordered the permanent written compilation of 23 years of prophetic oracles. Jeremiah 36:1-2 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that this word came unto Jeremiah from the LORD, saying, Take thee a roll of a book, and write therein all the words that I have spoken unto thee against Israel, and against Judah, and against all the nations, from the day I spake unto thee, from the days of Josiah, even unto this day."

question: Who was Jeremiah's personal scribe who penned the prophetic scroll from Jeremiah's dictation in Jeremiah 36:4?
option1: Baruch the son of Neriah
option2: Seraiah the son of Neriah
option3: Shaphan the royal scribe
option4: Elishama the prince's scribe
correct: Baruch the son of Neriah
explanation: Baruch ben Neriah - a scholar of noble lineage whose brother Seraiah was Zedekiah's quartermaster - served as Jeremiah's faithful amanuensis. Jeremiah 36:4 (KJV) - "Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah: and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD, which he had spoken unto him, upon a roll of a book."

question: Why could Jeremiah not enter the temple himself to read the scroll, requiring Baruch to go as his proxy in Jeremiah 36:5-6?
option1: He was stricken with a grievous fever and could not walk
option2: I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the LORD
option3: He was ceremonially defiled by touching a dead body
option4: He was hiding in the desert of Engedi from King Jehoiakim
correct: I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the LORD
explanation: Jeremiah was officially restricted or barred ('shut up' / atsur) from entering the temple precincts due to temple police bans. Jeremiah 36:5-6 (KJV) - "And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the LORD: Therefore go thou, and read in the roll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the LORD in the ears of the people in the LORD's house upon the fasting day:"

question: On what special occasion and in whose temple chamber did Baruch read the prophetic scroll aloud to the public in Jeremiah 36:9-10?
option1: During the Feast of Tabernacles, in the chamber of Pashur the priest
option2: On the Day of Atonement, in the court of the priests before the altar
option3: Upon a proclaimed fasting day in the fifth year, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe
option4: At the new moon celebration, in the royal chamber of Elishama
correct: Upon a proclaimed fasting day in the fifth year, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe
explanation: In December 604 BC (the ninth month of Jehoiakim's fifth year, following the Babylonian sack of Ashkelon), a national fast was called; Baruch read the scroll from Gemariah ben Shaphan's upper room overlooking the New Gate. Jeremiah 36:9-10 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before the LORD ... Then read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the LORD's house, in the ears of all the people."

question: Who heard Baruch's reading and immediately reported the alarming prophecies to the assembled royal cabinet in the scribe's chamber in Jeremiah 36:11-13?
option1: Jehudi the son of Nethaniah
option2: Delaiah the son of Shemaiah
option3: Elnathan the son of Achbor
option4: Michaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan
correct: Michaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan
explanation: Young nobleman Michaiah ben Gemariah hurried down to the palace scribe's room to alert the ministers of state. Jeremiah 36:11-13 (KJV) - "When Michaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, had heard out of the book all the words of the LORD, Then he went down into the king's house, into the scribe's chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there ... Then Michaiah declared unto them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people."

question: Which official with royal Cushite ancestry was dispatched by the princes to summon Baruch with the scroll in Jeremiah 36:14?
option1: Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi
option2: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
option3: Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech
option4: Seraiah the son of Azriel
correct: Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi
explanation: The cabinet dispatched Jehudi ben Nethaniah ben Shelemiah ben Cushi (bearing ancestral lineage from Cush) to fetch Baruch and the manuscript. Jeremiah 36:14 (KJV) - "Therefore all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, unto Baruch, saying, Take in thine hand the roll wherein thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch the son of Neriah took the roll in his hand, and came unto them."

question: What protective advice did the alarmed princes give to Baruch after hearing the scroll read in Jeremiah 36:19?
option1: Take the scroll and flee across the Jordan into the land of Moab
option2: Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where ye be
option3: Present thyself boldly before King Jehoiakim in his winterhouse
option4: Deposit the scroll in the secret vaults beneath the Holy of Holies
correct: Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where ye be
explanation: Knowing King Jehoiakim's tyrannical and violent temper, the sympathetic princes urged Baruch and Jeremiah to go into deep underground hiding immediately. Jeremiah 36:19 (KJV) - "Then said the princes unto Baruch, Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where ye be."

question: Where was King Jehoiakim sitting, and how did he desecrate and destroy the scroll as Jehudi read it in Jeremiah 36:22-23?
option1: Sitting on his ivory throne: he tore the parchment with his hands and stamped it into the mire
option2: Standing by the altar: he poured oil upon the scroll and burned it with strange fire
option3: Sitting in the winterhouse with a fire on the hearth: as Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut it with a scribe's penknife and cast it into the fire until completely consumed
option4: Riding in his chariot: he pierced the scroll with a spear and threw it into the valley of Hinnom
correct: Sitting in the winterhouse with a fire on the hearth: as Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut it with a scribe's penknife and cast it into the fire until completely consumed
explanation: In an act of supreme defiance, King Jehoiakim sat warming himself before a charcoal brazier in his winter quarters, taking a scribe's knife (ta'ar hassofer) to slice off columns (leaves) section by section and feeding them into the flames. Jeremiah 36:22-23 (KJV) - "Now the king sat in the winterhouse in the ninth month: and there was a fire on the hearth burning before him. And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth."

question: Which three courtiers pleaded with King Jehoiakim not to burn the holy scroll, though he refused to listen in Jeremiah 36:25?
option1: Pashur, Zephaniah, and Hananiah
option2: Ahikam, Shaphan, and Hilkiah
option3: Baruch, Seraiah, and Jehudi
option4: Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah
correct: Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah
explanation: Elnathan ben Achbor, Delaiah ben Shemaiah, and Gemariah ben Shaphan courageously begged the king not to commit the sacrilege of burning God's word. Jeremiah 36:25 (KJV) - "Nevertheless Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the roll: but he would not hear them."

question: What divine intervention frustrated the arrest warrant sent by Jehoiakim, and what was the ultimate fate of the burned scroll in Jeremiah 36:26, 32?
option1: The LORD hid them: Jeremiah took another roll, and Baruch rewrote all the burned words from his mouth, adding many like words besides
option2: An angel blinded the royal guards: and the original scroll was miraculously preserved from the ashes
option3: They escaped to Babylon: and Daniel transcribed the words in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar
option4: The princes resisted the king's officers: and the scroll was buried until the return from exile
correct: The LORD hid them: Jeremiah took another roll, and Baruch rewrote all the burned words from his mouth, adding many like words besides
explanation: God supernaturally shielded Jeremiah and Baruch ('the LORD hid them'), commanding the production of an expanded second edition: human fire cannot incinerate the indestructible word of God! Jeremiah 36:26, 32 (KJV) - " ... but the LORD hid them ... Then took Jeremiah another roll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah; who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire: and there were added besides unto them many like words."

question: What temporary military event prompted the Babylonian army to withdraw their siege of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 37:5?
option1: Pharaoh's army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans ... heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem
option2: A sudden plague of pestilence struck the camp of Nebuchadnezzar at night
option3: An insurrection in the eastern provinces of Elam forced the king of Babylon to march home
option4: King Zedekiah sent a tribute of thirty talents of gold from the temple treasury
correct: Pharaoh's army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans ... heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem
explanation: Pharaoh Hophra's Egyptian expeditionary force marched north, temporarily diverting the Babylonian siege engines away from Jerusalem. Jeremiah 37:5 (KJV) - "Then Pharaoh's army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem."

question: What warning did God give concerning the retreating Egyptian army in Jeremiah 37:7-8?
option1: Pharaoh's cavalry shall conquer the king of Babylon at Carchemish and deliver Zion
option2: Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land. And the Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire
option3: The Egyptians shall be drowned in the Red Sea as in the days of Moses
option4: Pharaoh shall take Zedekiah captive and demand heavy tribute of silver from Jerusalem
correct: Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land. And the Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire
explanation: Jeremiah warned against false optimism: Egypt's relief column would beat a hasty retreat, and the Babylonians would return to conquer and incinerate Jerusalem. Jeremiah 37:7-8 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel; Thus shall ye say to the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to enquire of me; Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land. And the Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire."

question: What extreme hypothetical scenario highlights the absolute inevitability of Babylonian victory in Jeremiah 37:10?
option1: Though the walls of Zion reached unto heaven and her gates were of solid bronze
option2: Though twelve legions of angels encamped upon the Mount of Olives to defend the temple
option3: Though ye had smitten the whole army of the Chaldeans ... and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should they rise up every man in his tent, and burn this city with fire
option4: Though Pharaoh brought ten thousand chariots of iron and archers from Cush
correct: Though ye had smitten the whole army of the Chaldeans ... and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should they rise up every man in his tent, and burn this city with fire
explanation: Divine judgment was irrevocable: even if Judah miraculously slaughtered the entire Babylonian army leaving only maimed, wounded soldiers in tents, those wounded men would still rise up and burn Jerusalem. Jeremiah 37:10 (KJV) - "For though ye had smitten the whole army of the Chaldeans that fight against you, and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should they rise up every man in his tent, and burn this city with fire."

question: Why did Jeremiah attempt to leave Jerusalem during the temporary siege respite in Jeremiah 37:12?
option1: To flee to the court of Pharaoh in Egypt for political sanctuary
option2: To hide the sacred vessels of the temple in the caves of Engedi
option3: To offer sacrifices upon the high place of Gibeon with the Rechabites
option4: To go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people
correct: To go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people
explanation: Taking advantage of the lifted siege, Jeremiah sought to travel to his hometown of Anathoth in Benjamin to inspect or settle his property rights among his relatives. Jeremiah 37:12 (KJV) - "Then Jeremiah went forth out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people."

question: Which sentry officer arrested Jeremiah at the Gate of Benjamin on false charges of desertion in Jeremiah 37:13?
option1: Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah
option2: Pashur the son of Immer
option3: Jehucal the son of Shelemiah
option4: Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech
correct: Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah
explanation: Captain Irijah ben Shelemiah - grandson of false prophet Hananiah whom Jeremiah had confronted in Chapter 28 - falsely accused Jeremiah of defecting to the Chaldeans. Jeremiah 37:13 (KJV) - "And when he was in the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the ward was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he took Jeremiah the prophet, saying, Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans."

question: Where did the enraged princes incarcerate and beat Jeremiah in Jeremiah 37:15?
option1: In the cistern of Malchiah in the court of the prison
option2: In prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison
option3: In the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin by the temple
option4: In the underground vaults beneath the royal palace of David
correct: In prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison
explanation: The princes converted the private residence of Jonathan the royal scribe into a harsh subterranean detention facility ('the dungeon, and into the cabins'). Jeremiah 37:15 (KJV) - "Wherefore the princes were wroth with Jeremiah, and smote him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison."

question: What blunt, uncompromising answer did Jeremiah give when King Zedekiah secretly asked him 'Is there any word from the LORD?' in Jeremiah 37:17?
option1: There is: Pharaoh shall come with a mighty host to break the siege of the Chaldeans
option2: There is not: for the heavens are brass and the Lord will not answer thy prayer
option3: There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
option4: There is: if thou wilt fast seven days in sackcloth, the angel of death shall smite the enemy
correct: There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
explanation: Despite brutal imprisonment, Jeremiah refused to flatter the king: he delivered the unvarnished divine truth that Zedekiah would be surrendered into Nebuchadnezzar's hands. Jeremiah 37:17 (KJV) - "Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took him out: and the king asked him secretly in his house, and said, Is there any word from the LORD? And Jeremiah said, There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon."

question: What personal plea did Jeremiah make to King Zedekiah regarding his incarceration in Jeremiah 37:20?
option1: Grant me unconditional freedom to return to my house in Anathoth
option2: Allow Baruch my scribe to bring my books and parchment to comfort my soul
option3: Send me as an ambassador to Nebuchadnezzar to negotiate peace for Jerusalem
option4: Cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there
correct: Cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there
explanation: Conditions in Jonathan's subterranean dungeon were so lethal that Jeremiah pleaded not to be sent back there to perish. Jeremiah 37:20 (KJV) - "Therefore hear now, I pray thee, O my lord the king: let my supplication, I pray thee, be accepted before thee; that thou cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there."

question: Where did Zedekiah transfer Jeremiah, and what daily ration was ordered for his sustenance in Jeremiah 37:21?
option1: Into the court of the prison, and daily a piece of bread out of the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city were spent
option2: Into the upper chamber of the temple, with daily wine and parched corn from the royal storehouse
option3: Into the palace guardroom, with a measure of barley and oil from the King's Dale
option4: Into the house of Ahikam at Mizpah, with dried figs and raisins from the vineyards
correct: Into the court of the prison, and daily a piece of bread out of the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city were spent
explanation: Zedekiah transferred him to the palace guardhouse ('court of the prison') and assigned him a daily loaf of bread from Baker's Street until the city's food supply was exhausted. Jeremiah 37:21 (KJV) - "Then Zedekiah the king commanded that they should commit Jeremiah into the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread out of the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city were spent. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison."

question: What challenging question did Jeremiah pose to Zedekiah exposing the failure of popular court diviners in Jeremiah 37:19?
option1: Have your astrologers delivered the city from the sword of the Chaldeans?
option2: Where are now your prophets which prophesied unto you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land?
option3: Did not Hananiah promise that within two years the temple vessels would return?
option4: Why do your princes seek help from Egypt when the Lord hath forbidden it?
correct: Where are now your prophets which prophesied unto you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land?
explanation: Jeremiah challenged Zedekiah to examine reality: where were the loud-mouthed false prophets who had guaranteed Babylon would never invade? Jeremiah 37:19 (KJV) - "Where are now your prophets which prophesied unto you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land?"

question: Which four hostile Judean princes demanded Jeremiah's execution for demoralizing the defenders in Jeremiah 38:1-4?
option1: Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Elnathan the son of Achbor, Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, and Baruch
option2: Shephatiah the son of Mattan, Gedaliah the son of Pashur, Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah
option3: Seraiah the son of Neriah, Ebed-melech, Zephaniah the priest, and Jonathan the scribe
option4: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan the son of Kareah, Jaazaniah, and Shaphan
correct: Shephatiah the son of Mattan, Gedaliah the son of Pashur, Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah
explanation: Four militant princes accused Jeremiah of treason, claiming his prophecies of surrender 'weakeneth the hands of the men of war'. Jeremiah 38:1, 4 (KJV) - "Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken ... Therefore the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words unto them: for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt."

question: What pathetic confession of political impotence did King Zedekiah utter when pressured by his belligerent princes in Jeremiah 38:5?
option1: Take him and do with him as seemeth good in your eyes, but shed not innocent blood
option2: The law of David forbids me to execute a prophet of the Lord without trial
option3: Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you
option4: I have washed my hands of this man's blood; see ye to it in the gate
correct: Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you
explanation: Weak and spineless, Zedekiah completely abdicated royal authority, surrendering the prophet to the ruthless princes. Jeremiah 38:5 (KJV) - "Then Zedekiah the king said, Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you."

question: Where did the princes cast Jeremiah to suffer a slow, suffocating death in Jeremiah 38:6?
option1: The pit of Tophet in the valley of the son of Hinnom
option2: The royal quarry beneath the north wall of Jerusalem
option3: The dry cistern of King Asa at Mizpah
option4: The dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire
correct: The dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire
explanation: They lowered Jeremiah with ropes into Prince Malchiah's deep underground cistern, whose water had run dry, leaving thick, foul mud where the prophet sank. Jeremiah 38:6 (KJV) - "Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire."

question: Who was the royal Ethiopian eunuch who courageously intervened before the king to rescue Jeremiah from the muddy cistern in Jeremiah 38:7-9?
option1: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house
option2: Baruch the son of Neriah
option3: Jehudi the son of Nethaniah
option4: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
correct: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house
explanation: Ebed-melech (literally 'Servant of the King'), an Ethiopian court official, boldly approached Zedekiah sitting in the Gate of Benjamin to denounce the princes' murderous cruelty. Jeremiah 38:7-9 (KJV) - "Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon; the king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin; Ebedmelech went forth out of the king's house, and spake to the king, saying, My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the dungeon; and he is like to die for hunger in the place where he is: for there is no more bread in the city."

question: How many men was Ebed-melech commanded to take with him to hoist Jeremiah out of the cistern in Jeremiah 38:10?
option1: Ten men
option2: Thirty men
option3: Twelve men
option4: Seventy men
correct: Thirty men
explanation: Zedekiah assigned Ebed-melech a security detachment of 30 men to overcome any potential armed resistance from the princes. Jeremiah 38:10 (KJV) - "Then the king commanded Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die."

question: What tender, ingenious padding did Ebed-melech procure from under the royal treasury to protect Jeremiah's armpits from rope burn in Jeremiah 38:11-12?
option1: Pillows of fine wool and sheepskins from the royal stables
option2: Swaddling cloths of linen and cushions of down
option3: Old cast clouts and old rotten rags, to put under his armholes under the cords
option4: Soft leather tunics and strips of purple cloth
correct: Old cast clouts and old rotten rags, to put under his armholes under the cords
explanation: Showing magnificent gentleness and compassion, Ebed-melech gathered discarded, soft rags ('old cast clouts') to cushion the biting ropes under Jeremiah's armpits as they hauled him out of the suctioning mud. Jeremiah 38:11-12 (KJV) - "So Ebedmelech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah. And Ebedmelech the Ethiopian said unto Jeremiah, Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. And Jeremiah did so."

question: Where did King Zedekiah conduct his final secret interview with Jeremiah in Jeremiah 38:14?
option1: In the chamber of the princes by the Water Gate
option2: In the inner court of the king's winterhouse
option3: Beside the pool of Siloam in the King's Garden
option4: Into the third entry that is in the house of the LORD
correct: Into the third entry that is in the house of the LORD
explanation: Zedekiah summoned Jeremiah to a secluded passageway ('the third entry' / mevo hashlishi) connecting the royal palace to the temple complex. Jeremiah 38:14 (KJV) - "Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet unto him into the third entry that is in the house of the LORD: and the king said unto Jeremiah, I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me."

question: What secret oath did King Zedekiah swear to guarantee Jeremiah's physical safety during their private consultation in Jeremiah 38:16?
option1: As the LORD liveth, that made us this soul, I will not put thee to death, neither will I give thee into the hand of these men that seek thy life
option2: By the temple of Solomon and by the altar of the LORD, no hair of thy head shall perish
option3: As God liveth, who delivered David from the hand of Saul, I will defend thee from the princes
option4: I swear by the covenant of Abraham that thou shalt dwell in safety all the days of my reign
correct: As the LORD liveth, that made us this soul, I will not put thee to death, neither will I give thee into the hand of these men that seek thy life
explanation: Zedekiah swore by the living Creator ('As the LORD liveth, that made us this soul') that he would neither execute Jeremiah nor surrender him to the murderous princes. Jeremiah 38:16 (KJV) - "So Zedekiah the king sware secretly unto Jeremiah, saying, As the LORD liveth, that made us this soul, I will not put thee to death, neither will I give thee into the hand of these men that seek thy life."

question: What paralyzing fear prevented Zedekiah from surrendering to Nebuchadnezzar as Jeremiah commanded in Jeremiah 38:19?
option1: I fear that Nebuchadnezzar will immediately slay me and my sons with the sword
option2: I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me
option3: I fear that Pharaoh will invade Judah from the south and burn my royal palace
option4: I fear that the princes will assassinate me before I can reach the gates
correct: I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me
explanation: Pathetically driven by cowardice and fear of human ridicule, Zedekiah dreaded being mocked and abused by fellow Jewish deserters who had already surrendered to Babylon. Jeremiah 38:19 (KJV) - "And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me."

question: What mocking dirge will the captured women of Zedekiah's royal harem sing as they are marched into Babylonian captivity in Jeremiah 38:22?
option1: How is the mighty king fallen, and the crown of David trodden in the dust!
option2: Thou hast trusted in cedar palaces and Egyptian chariots, but they have failed thee
option3: Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back
option4: Woe unto our children, for the king hath delivered Zion to the fire of the north
correct: Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back
explanation: Zedekiah's own concubines and royal women will taunt him: his pro-Egyptian advisers pushed him into rebellion until his feet were trapped in political mud, while they abandoned him. Jeremiah 38:22 (KJV) - "And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah's house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylon's princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back."

question: In which regnal year, month, and day of King Zedekiah was the wall of Jerusalem finally breached by the Babylonians in Jeremiah 39:2?
option1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah, in the tenth month, the tenth day of the month
option2: In the twelfth year of Zedekiah, in the fifth month, the seventh day of the month
option3: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month
option4: In the tenth year of Zedekiah, in the first month, the fourteenth day of the month
correct: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month
explanation: On July 18, 586 BC (the 9th of Tammuz in Zedekiah's 11th year), the city walls gave way after an excruciating eighteen-month siege. Jeremiah 39:2 (KJV) - "And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, the city was broken up."

question: Where did the conquering Babylonian generals assemble their formal command post inside breached Jerusalem in Jeremiah 39:3?
option1: At the Water Gate
option2: At the Horse Gate
option3: In the High Gate of Benjamin
option4: In the middle gate
correct: In the middle gate
explanation: Babylonian military commanders - including Nergal-sharezer and Sarsechim - established their judicial headquarters in the Middle Gate dividing the upper and lower city. Jeremiah 39:3 (KJV) - "And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even Nergalsharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon."

question: By what nocturnal escape route did King Zedekiah and his soldiers attempt to flee from Jerusalem in Jeremiah 39:4?
option1: By night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain
option2: Through the secret water conduit leading into the brook Kidron
option3: Through the northern gate toward Mount Ephraim and Bethel
option4: Across the western wall toward the coastal road of the Philistines
correct: By night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain
explanation: Zedekiah slipped out through the southern exit between the dual fortifications near the King's Garden, fleeing eastward down through the Jordan Valley ('the plain' / the Arabah). Jeremiah 39:4 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain."

question: Where was fleeing King Zedekiah intercepted and captured by the pursuing Chaldean cavalry in Jeremiah 39:5?
option1: At the fords of the Jordan near Gilgal
option2: In the plains of Jericho
option3: In the wilderness of Engedi
option4: In the mountains of Beth-el
correct: In the plains of Jericho
explanation: Babylonian cavalry units overtook Zedekiah's fleeing entourage in the open plains of Jericho. Jeremiah 39:5 (KJV) - "But the Chaldeans' army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him."

question: To which northern Syrian headquarters was captured Zedekiah brought for imperial trial before Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 39:5?
option1: Carchemish on the Euphrates
option2: Damascus in Syria
option3: Riblah in the land of Hamath
option4: Tadmor in the wilderness
correct: Riblah in the land of Hamath
explanation: Riblah on the Orontes River served as Nebuchadnezzar's operational military headquarters during the campaign. Jeremiah 39:5 (KJV) - " ... they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him."

question: What horrific sequential punishment was inflicted upon King Zedekiah at Riblah in Jeremiah 39:6-7?
option1: He was forced to walk between the severed parts of his princes, and then beheaded
option2: He was stripped naked, branded on the forehead with the mark of a slave, and forced to row in the fleet
option3: He was thrown into a lion's den before all the kings of Syria and Hamath
option4: The king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah ... before his eyes ... Moreover he put out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon
correct: The king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah ... before his eyes ... Moreover he put out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar executed Zedekiah's royal sons before his very eyes - ensuring that the slaughter of his children was the final visual image stamped into his memory - before gouging out his eyes and binding him in bronze fetters. Jeremiah 39:6-7 (KJV) - "Then the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes: also the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah. Moreover he put out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon."

question: What socio-economic policy did Babylonian commander Nebuzaradan execute concerning the destitute poor remaining in Judah in Jeremiah 39:10?
option1: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time
option2: He sold them as tributary slaves unto the merchants of Tyre and Sidon
option3: He enrolled them into the auxiliary infantry of the Chaldean empire
option4: He forced them to pay annual agricultural tribute of half their olive oil
correct: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time
explanation: In an extraordinary agrarian reallocation, Nebuzaradan deeded confiscated aristocratic estates, vineyards, and agricultural fields to the landless peasant class. Jeremiah 39:10 (KJV) - "But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time."

question: What personal protective orders did Emperor Nebuchadnezzar issue regarding Jeremiah in Jeremiah 39:11-12?
option1: Bring him in chains to Babylon that he may serve as a royal astrologer in my palace
option2: Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do unto him even as he shall say unto thee
option3: Give him ten talents of gold and a royal chariot to return to Anathoth
option4: Appoint him high priest over the temple ruins in Jerusalem
correct: Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do unto him even as he shall say unto thee
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar had heard of Jeremiah's consistent prophecies counseling surrender; he ordered Nebuzaradan to guarantee the prophet's personal safety and grant any request he made. Jeremiah 39:11-12 (KJV) - "Now Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, saying, Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do unto him even as he shall say unto thee."

question: To whose custody was Jeremiah initially committed upon being released from the prison court in Jeremiah 39:14?
option1: Baruch the son of Neriah
option2: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
option3: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan
option4: Jonathan the scribe
correct: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan
explanation: Jeremiah was entrusted to Gedaliah ben Ahikam - a trusted pro-Babylonian nobleman from the righteous family of Shaphan - to dwell freely among the surviving populace. Jeremiah 39:14 (KJV) - "Even they sent, and took Jeremiah out of the court of the prison, and committed him unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him home: so he dwelt among the people."

question: What personal divine oracle of preservation was promised to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian in Jeremiah 39:17-18?
option1: Thou shalt be made a royal counselor in the court of the king of Babylon
option2: Thou shalt inherit the fields of Malchiah in the territory of Benjamin
option3: Thou shalt live to see the return of the exiles from Babylon after seventy years
option4: I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me
correct: I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me
explanation: Because of his courageous faith and selfless rescue of Jeremiah, God specifically rewarded Ebed-melech with total immunity from the sword: his life was granted to him 'for a prey'. Jeremiah 39:17-18 (KJV) - "But I will deliver thee in that day, saith the LORD: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid. For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the LORD."

question: At which transit staging depot near Jerusalem was Jeremiah found bound in chains before Nebuzaradan formally liberated him in Jeremiah 40:1?
option1: Gibeon
option2: Mizpah
option3: Anathoth
option4: Ramah
correct: Ramah
explanation: Jeremiah had been accidentally rounded up in manacles alongside exiles at Ramah (the staging assembly point five miles north of Jerusalem) before Nebuzaradan identified and released him. Jeremiah 40:1 (KJV) - "The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all that were carried away captive of Jerusalem and Judah, which were carried away captive unto Babylon."

question: What remarkable theological confession did the pagan general Nebuzaradan utter to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 40:2-3?
option1: The LORD thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place. Now the LORD hath brought it ... because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you
option2: Marduk the great god of Babylon hath delivered Zion into our hands because your king broke his oath
option3: The gods of the mountains are stronger than the gods of the valleys, therefore ye are overthrown
option4: Great is Nebuchadnezzar our master, whom no god of the nations can resist
correct: The LORD thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place. Now the LORD hath brought it ... because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you
explanation: Astonishingly, a pagan Babylonian field commander preached accurate Deuteronomic theology to the prophet, recognizing that Jerusalem fell because of Israel's covenant disobedience to Yahweh. Jeremiah 40:2-3 (KJV) - "And the captain of the guard took Jeremiah, and said unto him, The LORD thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place. Now the LORD hath brought it, and done according as he hath said: because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you."

question: What generous options did Nebuzaradan present to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 40:4?
option1: Thou must either go into exile with King Zedekiah or be sold as a slave to the merchants of Tyre
option2: If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee ... forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go
option3: Thou shalt either dwell in the court of the palace in Babylon or be executed at Riblah
option4: Thou shalt either serve as governor over the cities of Judah or depart into Egypt
correct: If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee ... forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go
explanation: Nebuzaradan granted Jeremiah absolute freedom of movement: an honored VIP pension in Babylon or unfettered liberty to reside anywhere in Judah. Jeremiah 40:4 (KJV) - "And now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which were upon thine hand. If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee to come with me into Babylon, forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go."

question: What supplies did Nebuzaradan bestow upon Jeremiah when the prophet chose to remain in the land in Jeremiah 40:5?
option1: A silver flagon and two mules
option2: A royal mantle and a signet ring
option3: Victuals and a reward
option4: Ten talents of bronze and an armed guard
correct: Victuals and a reward
explanation: Nebuzaradan generously provided Jeremiah with food rations ('victuals') and a financial gift ('reward' / mas'et). Jeremiah 40:5 (KJV) - " ... So the captain of the guard gave him victuals and a reward, and let him go."

question: Where did newly appointed governor Gedaliah establish the administrative capital of Judah, and where did Jeremiah go to live with him in Jeremiah 40:6?
option1: Hebron
option2: Bethlehem
option3: Gibeon
option4: Mizpah
correct: Mizpah
explanation: Because Jerusalem was a smoldering ruin, Gedaliah set up his provisional provincial capital at Mizpah (in Benjamin), where Jeremiah joined him. Jeremiah 40:6 (KJV) - "Then went Jeremiah unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and dwelt with him among the people that were left in the land."

question: What practical counsel did Governor Gedaliah swear to the guerrilla captains and scattered Jewish refugees in Jeremiah 40:9-10?
option1: Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you ... gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels
option2: Prepare your swords and chariots secretly, for within two years we shall rebel against Babylon
option3: Flee across the Jordan into the land of Ammon before the Chaldean tax collectors arrive
option4: Offer daily sacrifices upon the ruins of the altar in Jerusalem to avert the wrath of God
correct: Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you ... gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels
explanation: Gedaliah established a peaceful agrarian recovery policy: submit loyally to Babylonian authority, harvest the summer crops (grapes, olives, summer figs), and rebuild civilian communities. Jeremiah 40:9-10 (KJV) - "And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan sware unto them and to their men, saying, Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you. As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah, to serve the Chaldeans, which will come unto us: but ye, gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that ye have taken."

question: From which three neighboring countries did scattered Jewish refugees return when they heard Gedaliah was governor in Jeremiah 40:11-12?
option1: Egypt, Philistia, and Syria
option2: Moab, the Ammonites, and Edom
option3: Tyre, Sidon, and Damascus
option4: Assyria, Media, and Elam
correct: Moab, the Ammonites, and Edom
explanation: Displaced refugees who had escaped across the Jordan returned from Moab, Ammon, and Edom, enjoying an abundant harvest under Gedaliah's benevolent leadership. Jeremiah 40:11-12 (KJV) - "Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan; Even all the Jews returned out of all places whither they were driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, unto Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruits very much."

question: Which foreign monarch was unmasked as the mastermind behind the assassination plot against Governor Gedaliah in Jeremiah 40:14?
option1: Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt
option2: Hadad king of Edom
option3: Baalis the king of the Ammonites
option4: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
correct: Baalis the king of the Ammonites
explanation: King Baalis of Ammon sponsored an assassination conspiracy to destabilize the fragile Babylonian province of Judah. Jeremiah 40:14 (KJV) - "And said unto him, Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites hath sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee? But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not."

question: Which patriotic military captain warned Gedaliah of the plot and offered to assassinate Ishmael secretly to protect the remnant in Jeremiah 40:13-15?
option1: Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth
option2: Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite
option3: Elnathan the son of Achbor
option4: Johanan the son of Kareah
correct: Johanan the son of Kareah
explanation: Johanan ben Kareah correctly identified the imminent danger and secretly volunteered to eliminate Ishmael preemptively to prevent the destruction of the Jewish remnant. Jeremiah 40:15 (KJV) - "Then Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?"

question: How did Governor Gedaliah tragically respond to Johanan's urgent warning in Jeremiah 40:16?
option1: Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael
option2: Put Ishmael in prison until the matter be examined before the elders
option3: Send an armed escort to guard the palace at Mizpah night and day
option4: Flee with me into the wilderness of Engedi until the conspiracy be broken
correct: Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael
explanation: Possessing noble but fatal naivete, Gedaliah dismissed the warning as malicious slander, refusing to take defensive measures. Jeremiah 40:16 (KJV) - "But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael."

question: Who led the treacherous assassination of Governor Gedaliah during a fellowship banquet at Mizpah in Jeremiah 41:1-2?
option1: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, with ten men
option2: Johanan the son of Kareah, with forty warriors
option3: Baalis the king of the Ammonites, with a company of archers
option4: Pashur the son of Malchiah, with the princes of Zedekiah
correct: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, with ten men
explanation: Ishmael ben Nethaniah - a bitter member of the displaced royal family of David sponsored by Ammon - violated sacred hospitality laws by murdering his host Gedaliah during a shared meal. Jeremiah 41:1-2 (KJV) - "Now it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and the princes of the king, even ten men with him, came unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah. Then arose Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men that were with him, and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land."

question: Whom else did Ishmael and his assassins slaughter at Mizpah alongside Gedaliah in Jeremiah 41:3?
option1: The prophet Jeremiah and Baruch his scribe
option2: All the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war
option3: The daughters of King Zedekiah and the royal eunuchs
option4: The priests of Shiloh and the elders of Benjamin
correct: All the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war
explanation: To prevent news of the coup from leaking, Ishmael massacred Gedaliah's Jewish civilian staff and the small Babylonian military garrison stationed at Mizpah. Jeremiah 41:3 (KJV) - "Ishmael also slew all the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war."

question: From which three northern cities did eighty grieving pilgrims arrive on their way to bring offerings to the ruined temple in Jeremiah 41:5?
option1: Dan, Bethel, and Megiddo
option2: Nazareth, Capernaum, and Tiberias
option3: Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria
option4: Hazor, Ramah, and Gilgal
correct: Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria
explanation: Eighty devout northern pilgrims with shaven beards, torn garments, and mourning gashes traveled south carrying grain offerings and incense toward the temple site in Jerusalem. Jeremiah 41:5 (KJV) - "That there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the LORD."

question: What diabolical deception did Ishmael practice to lure the eighty pilgrims into his trap at Mizpah in Jeremiah 41:6?
option1: He blew the trumpet and invited them to anoint a new king over Israel
option2: He offered them bread and wine in the name of the king of Babylon
option3: He claimed that the temple of Solomon had been miraculously restored by angels
option4: Ishmael ... went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and ... said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
correct: Ishmael ... went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and ... said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
explanation: Feigning deep pious grief, Ishmael walked out weeping crocodile tears, pretending to be a fellow mourner and inviting them inside to meet the already-murdered governor. Jeremiah 41:6 (KJV) - "And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam."

question: Where did Ishmael dump the slaughtered corpses of seventy of these pilgrims in Jeremiah 41:7, 9?
option1: Into the midst of the pit which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel
option2: Into the brook Kidron by the entry of the Water Gate
option3: Into the valley of Tophet in the valley of the son of Hinnom
option4: Into the cistern of Malchiah in the court of the prison
correct: Into the midst of the pit which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel
explanation: Ishmael butchered 70 pilgrims in cold blood, tossing their bodies into King Asa's massive historic cistern (constructed 300 years earlier during war with Baasha of Israel, 1 Kings 15:22). Jeremiah 41:7, 9 (KJV) - "And it was so, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him ... Now the pit wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain."

question: What bribe secured the survival of ten of the eighty pilgrims in Jeremiah 41:8?
option1: Slay us not: for we have thirty shekels of silver hidden in our girdles
option2: Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey
option3: Slay us not: for we are skilled carpenters and smiths who can forge weapons
option4: Slay us not: for our fathers are princes in the court of the king of Ammon
correct: Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey
explanation: Ten men bought their lives by revealing hidden underground agricultural caches ('treasures in the field') of grain, olive oil, and honey. Jeremiah 41:8 (KJV) - "But ten men were found among them that said unto Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he forbare, and slew them not among their brethren."

question: Whom did Ishmael take hostage as captives when fleeing toward Ammon in Jeremiah 41:10?
option1: The high priest and the seventy elders of the sanctuary
option2: The scribes of Shaphan and the servants of Jonathan
option3: All the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king's daughters, and all the people that remained
option4: The remaining Chaldean soldiers and their horses
correct: All the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king's daughters, and all the people that remained
explanation: Ishmael abducted the royal princesses ('king's daughters') and surviving civilians at Mizpah to sell or deliver them to King Baalis of Ammon. Jeremiah 41:10 (KJV) - "Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king's daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites."

question: Where did Johanan and his forces intercept Ishmael and liberate the captives in Jeremiah 41:11-12?
option1: At the fords of the Jordan near Jericho
option2: Beside the pool of Siloam
option3: In the plains of Moab
option4: By the great waters that are in Gibeon
correct: By the great waters that are in Gibeon
explanation: Johanan mobilized loyal troops and intercepted the terrorist band at the famous Pool of Gibeon ('great waters that are in Gibeon', 2 Samuel 2:13). Jeremiah 41:11-12 (KJV) - "But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done, Then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great waters that are in Gibeon."

question: What became of Ishmael when Johanan's forces arrived in Jeremiah 41:13-15?
option1: All the captives deserted Ishmael and returned to Johanan, but Ishmael escaped with eight men and fled to the Ammonites
option2: Ishmael was slain by the sword of Johanan and cast into the pool of Gibeon
option3: Ishmael was captured, bound in chains, and delivered to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah
option4: Ishmael committed suicide by falling upon his sword before the men of Judah
correct: All the captives deserted Ishmael and returned to Johanan, but Ishmael escaped with eight men and fled to the Ammonites
explanation: The captives rejoiced and defected to Johanan, while Ishmael and eight surviving henchmen slipped away into Transjordanian Ammon. Jeremiah 41:14-15 (KJV) - "So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah cast about and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites."

question: Where did Johanan and the recovered remnant encamp near Bethlehem as they prepared to flee into Egypt in Jeremiah 41:17-18?
option1: In the cave of Adullam
option2: In the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem
option3: At the threshing floor of Araunah
option4: Beside the well of Bethlehem
correct: In the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem
explanation: Terrified that Nebuchadnezzar would execute collective reprisals for the assassination of Governor Gedaliah and his garrison, Johanan camped at the caravanserai of Chimham (Geruth Chimham, David's gift to Barzillai's son, 2 Samuel 19:37-40) to plan an escape to Egypt. Jeremiah 41:17-18 (KJV) - "And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem, to go to enter into Egypt, Because of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land."

question: What solemn delegation approached Jeremiah at Chimham requesting divine guidance in Jeremiah 42:1-2?
option1: The elders of Anathoth and the priests of Shiloh
option2: All the captains of the forces, Johanan the son of Kareah, Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest
option3: The royal princesses and the eunuchs of Zedekiah's palace
option4: The scribes of Baruch and the messengers of the king of Ammon
correct: All the captains of the forces, Johanan the son of Kareah, Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest
explanation: The entire surviving remnant - military officers and civilians - approached Jeremiah to ask for divine direction. Jeremiah 42:1-2 (KJV) - "Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest, came near, And said unto Jeremiah the prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us unto the LORD thy God, even for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes do behold us:)"

question: What unconditional pledge of absolute obedience did the people swear to God through Jeremiah in Jeremiah 42:5-6?
option1: If the Lord command us to rebuild Jerusalem, we will labor day and night without wages
option2: If the Lord forbid us to enter Egypt, we will surrender ourselves to the Chaldeans at Riblah
option3: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us
option4: We swear by the life of our souls that we will walk in all the statutes of Moses
correct: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us
explanation: They invoked Yahweh as a 'true and faithful witness', swearing absolute, unconditional obedience to whatever message God returned ('whether pleasing or painful'). Jeremiah 42:5-6 (KJV) - "Then they said to Jeremiah, The LORD be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not even according to all things for the which the LORD thy God shall send thee to us. Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."

question: How long did Jeremiah wait in prayer before the divine answer was revealed to him in Jeremiah 42:7?
option1: After three days
option2: After seven days
option3: On the following morning
option4: After ten days
correct: After ten days
explanation: Jeremiah was no vending machine of false prophecy: he waited ten full days in earnest prayer until the genuine word of the Lord came. Jeremiah 42:7 (KJV) - "And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah."

question: What divine promise did God give the remnant if they chose to remain peacefully in Judah in Jeremiah 42:10?
option1: If ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up
option2: I will give you ten thousand talents of silver from the treasury of Babylon
option3: I will restore King Jehoiachin to sit upon David's throne within two years
option4: I will cause rivers of water to break forth in the desert of Tekoa
correct: If ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up
explanation: God reaffirmed the covenant construction verbs: He would protect, build, and plant them securely in Judah, relenting of further calamity. Jeremiah 42:10 (KJV) - "If ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up: for I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you."

question: What reassuring command did God give concerning their paralyzing terror of Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 42:11-12?
option1: Nebuchadnezzar shall be slain by his own servants and his empire divided among the Medes
option2: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon ... for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand. And I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you
option3: An angel of the Lord shall stand between you and the Chaldean host at the Jordan
