option4: The king of Babylon shall send gifts of peace and appoint Johanan governor over Judah
correct: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon ... for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand. And I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you
explanation: God commanded them not to fear Nebuchadnezzar: Yahweh would sovereignly incline the Babylonian emperor's heart to show them mercy. Jeremiah 42:11-12 (KJV) - "Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom ye are afraid; be not afraid of him, saith the LORD: for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand. And I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you, and cause you to return to your own land."

question: What false security did the rebellious remnant imagine they would find in Egypt in Jeremiah 42:14?
option1: Where we can worship the God of our fathers without fear of the Chaldeans
option2: Where we shall buy fertile fields along the Nile and become rich merchants
option3: Where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell
option4: Where Pharaoh's armies will protect our children from foreign kings
correct: Where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell
explanation: They chased a mirage of peace, food security, and immunity from military conflict in Egypt. Jeremiah 42:14 (KJV) - "Saying, No; but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell:"

question: What terrifying poetic justice would overtake them in Egypt if they migrated there in Jeremiah 42:16?
option1: Pharaoh shall seize your sons for charioteers and sell your daughters as handmaids
option2: The Nile shall turn to blood and plagues of frogs and locusts shall consume your houses
option3: The king of Ammon shall invade Egypt and slay you by the waters of Sihor
option4: The sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die
correct: The sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die
explanation: Fleeing God's appointed place was fatal: the very sword (Nebuchadnezzar's later invasion of Egypt in 568 BC) and famine they sought to avoid would hunt them down and exterminate them in Egypt. Jeremiah 42:16 (KJV) - "Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die."

question: What four bywords of international shame will characterize the refugees who migrate into Egypt in Jeremiah 42:18?
option1: An execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach
option2: A proverb, and a byword, an abomination, and a sorrow
option3: A mockery, and a desolation, a warning, and a lamentation
option4: A shame, and a tragedy, a hissing, and a ruin
correct: An execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach
explanation: Just as Jerusalem suffered God's fury, the disobedient refugees in Egypt would become an object of horror and universal cursing ('an execration' / alah). Jeremiah 42:18 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured forth upon you, when ye shall enter into Egypt: and ye shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and ye shall see this place no more."

question: What clear, categorical command did God deliver regarding Egypt in Jeremiah 42:19?
option1: Depart from Chimham and march unto the fortress of Lachish
option2: The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day
option3: Send an embassy to Pharaoh but dwell ye in the caves of the desert
option4: Surrender yourselves unto the captain of the guard at Babylon
correct: The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day
explanation: God issued an unambiguous, non-negotiable negative imperative: 'Go ye not into Egypt!' Jeremiah 42:19 (KJV) - "The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day."

question: What internal duplicity and spiritual hypocrisy does Jeremiah unmask among the leaders in Jeremiah 42:20?
option1: For ye had already sent messengers to Pharaoh to prepare houses in Tahapanes
option2: For ye loved the idols of Egypt more than the living God of Israel
option3: For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us ... and we will do it
option4: For ye took bribes of silver from the captains of the Ammonites
correct: For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us ... and we will do it
explanation: Jeremiah exposes their religious fraud: they had already resolved to flee to Egypt before asking for prayer, deceitfully seeking divine rubber-stamping ('ye dissembled in your hearts' / hit'eitem benafshotekhem). Jeremiah 42:20 (KJV) - "For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us unto the LORD our God; and according unto all that the LORD our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it."

question: In Jeremiah 43:2, which leaders insolently accused Jeremiah of speaking falsely when he forbade the remnant from going down into Egypt?
option1: Pashur the son of Malchiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah
option2: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and Baalis the king of the Ammonites
option3: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah and Johanan the son of Kareah, along with all the proud men
option4: Seraiah the son of Neriah and Gemariah the son of Shaphan
correct: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah and Johanan the son of Kareah, along with all the proud men
explanation: Jeremiah 43:2 (KJV) - "Then spake Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men, saying unto Jeremiah, Thou speakest falsely: the LORD our God hath not sent thee to say, Go not into Egypt to sojourn there:"

question: Whom did the arrogant leaders accuse of inciting Jeremiah against them to deliver them into the hands of the Chaldeans in Jeremiah 43:3?
option1: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
option2: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
option3: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
option4: Baruch the son of Neriah
correct: Baruch the son of Neriah
explanation: Jeremiah 43:3 (KJV) - "But Baruch the son of Neriah setteth thee on against us, for to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us to death, and carry us away captives into Babylon."

question: To which Egyptian frontier city did Johanan and the captains bring the remnant of Judah, Jeremiah, and Baruch, in disobedience to the Lord's voice?
option1: Tahpanhes
option2: Migdol
option3: Noph
option4: Pathros
correct: Tahpanhes
explanation: Jeremiah 43:7 (KJV) - "So they came into the land of Egypt: for they obeyed not the voice of the LORD: thus came they even to Tahpanhes."

question: What prophetic symbolic action was Jeremiah commanded to perform at the entry of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes according to Jeremiah 43:9?
option1: Break an earthen bottle of clay before the governors of Egypt at the river Nile
option2: Take great stones in his hand and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln in the sight of the men of Judah
option3: Pour blood and ashes upon the threshold of the royal palace
option4: Erect twelve wooden pillars inscribed with the names of the tribes of Israel
correct: Take great stones in his hand and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln in the sight of the men of Judah
explanation: Jeremiah 43:9 (KJV) - "Take great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln, which is at the entry of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;"

question: What did the Lord declare would be set upon the hidden stones at the entry of Pharaoh's palace in Jeremiah 43:10?
option1: An altar of sacrifice dedicated to the God of Israel
option2: The standard of the king of Persia
option3: The throne and royal pavilion of Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, God's servant
option4: A pillar of salt and brimstone testifying against Egypt
correct: The throne and royal pavilion of Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, God's servant
explanation: Jeremiah 43:10 (KJV) - "And say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid; and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them."

question: According to Jeremiah 43:11, what three fates will Nebuchadrezzar deliver to the land of Egypt when he smites it?
option1: Such as are for pestilence to pestilence, famine to famine, and exile to exile
option2: Such as are for burning to burning, drowning to drowning, and plunder to plunder
option3: Such as are for bondage to bondage, tribute to tribute, and desolation to desolation
option4: Such as are for death to death, such as are for captivity to captivity, and such as are for the sword to the sword
correct: Such as are for death to death, such as are for captivity to captivity, and such as are for the sword to the sword
explanation: Jeremiah 43:11 (KJV) - "And when he cometh, he shall smite the land of Egypt, and deliver such as are for death to death; and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword."

question: With what metaphor does Jeremiah 43:12 describe Nebuchadrezzar taking possession of and clearing the land of Egypt without resistance?
option1: As a shepherd putteth on his garment
option2: As a reaper gathereth sheaves into his bosom
option3: As a merchant weigheth out fine silver
option4: As an eagle sweepeth down upon its prey
correct: As a shepherd putteth on his garment
explanation: Jeremiah 43:12 (KJV) - "And I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt; and he shall burn them, and carry them away captives: and he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd putteth on his garment; and he shall go forth from thence in peace."

question: Which specific Egyptian religious cult center and its sacred obelisks/images did Jeremiah prophesy Nebuchadrezzar would shatter in Jeremiah 43:13?
option1: The temple of Karnak in Thebes
option2: Beth-shemesh (the House of the Sun / Heliopolis)
option3: The pyramid monuments of Giza
option4: The sanctuary of Apis at Memphis
correct: Beth-shemesh (the House of the Sun / Heliopolis)
explanation: Jeremiah 43:13 (KJV) - "He shall break also the images of Beth-shemesh, that is in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of the Egyptians shall he burn with fire."

question: Who were among the people specifically enumerated in Jeremiah 43:6 that Johanan took down to Egypt against divine counsel?
option1: Only the chief priests and military officers of Judah
option2: The royal guard and the surviving nobles of Jerusalem exclusively
option3: Men, women, children, the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzar-adan had left with Gedaliah
option4: Foreign mercenaries and merchant caravans from Tyre
correct: Men, women, children, the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzar-adan had left with Gedaliah
explanation: Jeremiah 43:6 (KJV) - "Even men, and women, and children, and the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah."

question: What primary divine purpose is underscored by God commanding Jeremiah to hide the stones in the brick pavement in the sight of the Jewish refugees?
option1: To establish a secret boundary marker for returning exiles seventy years later
option2: To desecrate the ceremonial entrance of Pharaoh's palace according to Levitical law
option3: To conceal sacred temple treasures brought out of Jerusalem
option4: To serve as an undeniable visible sign that their geographical relocation could not avert Nebuchadnezzar's divinely appointed judgment
correct: To serve as an undeniable visible sign that their geographical relocation could not avert Nebuchadnezzar's divinely appointed judgment
explanation: Jeremiah 43:9-10 (KJV) - "Take great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln ... in the sight of the men of Judah; And say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid ... "

question: In Jeremiah 44:1, which four Egyptian geographic locations are specified where Jewish refugees were dwelling when the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah?
option1: Alexandria, Goshen, Pelusium, and Aswan
option2: Thebes, Heliopolis, Tanis, and Sais
option3: Sin, No-Amon, Beth-shemesh, and Rameses
option4: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph (Memphis), and the country of Pathros (Upper Egypt)
correct: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph (Memphis), and the country of Pathros (Upper Egypt)
explanation: Jeremiah 44:1 (KJV) - "The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews which dwell in the land of Egypt, which dwell at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros, saying,"

question: How did the Lord describe His tireless efforts to turn Judah from idolatry before Jerusalem's destruction in Jeremiah 44:4?
option1: Rising early and sending them all my servants the prophets, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate
option2: Speaking in dreams and visions of the night to the elders of Israel
option3: Writing His statutes on pillars of brass in the temple courts
option4: Striking them with severe plagues of hail and locusts in the days of their youth
correct: Rising early and sending them all my servants the prophets, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate
explanation: Jeremiah 44:4 (KJV) - "Howbeit I sent unto you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate."

question: In their brazen refusal to heed Jeremiah's prophecy in Jeremiah 44:17, what deity did the people resolutely declare they would continue to burn incense and pour drink offerings to?
option1: Baal-peor
option2: The queen of heaven
option3: Molech the abomination of Ammon
option4: Dagon of the Philistines
correct: The queen of heaven
explanation: Jeremiah 44:17 (KJV) - "But we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings, and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem: for then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil."

question: What erroneous historical correlation did the idolaters argue in Jeremiah 44:18 to justify their continuing worship of the queen of heaven?
option1: That their ancestors had prospered under Solomon only when honoring the deities of Tyre and Sidon
option2: That the temple of Jerusalem was burned because Josiah destroyed the high places of Pharaoh
option3: That since they ceased burning incense to the queen of heaven, they had lacked all things and been consumed by sword and famine
option4: That Egypt was richer than Babylon due to the sun god Ra's superior protection
correct: That since they ceased burning incense to the queen of heaven, they had lacked all things and been consumed by sword and famine
explanation: Jeremiah 44:18 (KJV) - "But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine."

question: What specific ritual pastry did the women of Judah confess to baking for the queen of heaven in Jeremiah 44:19?
option1: Wafers dipped in honey and pomegranate wine
option2: Unleavened barley loaves sprinkled with frankincense
option3: Fig cakes kneaded with blood of white heifers
option4: Cakes to worship her (bearing her image)
correct: Cakes to worship her (bearing her image)
explanation: Jeremiah 44:19 (KJV) - "And when we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured out drink offerings unto her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her, without our men?"

question: In Jeremiah 44:26, what solemn oath did the Lord swear concerning His holy name among the Jewish refugees in Egypt?
option1: His name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord GOD liveth
option2: His name would be erased from the ark of the covenant forever
option3: His name would be proclaimed only in the tongue of the Chaldeans
option4: His name would be blasphemed among the Gentiles for seven generations
correct: His name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord GOD liveth
explanation: Jeremiah 44:26 (KJV) - "Therefore hear ye the word of the LORD, all Judah that dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, saith the LORD, that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord GOD liveth."

question: According to Jeremiah 44:27, how will the Lord watch over the remnant of Judah in the land of Egypt?
option1: With mercy and long-suffering
option2: For evil, and not for good
option3: As a father pitieth his rebellious children
option4: In silence until the year of jubilee
correct: For evil, and not for good
explanation: Jeremiah 44:27 (KJV) - "Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them."

question: What sign did the Lord give to the Jews in Egypt to prove that His words of doom would surely stand against them (Jeremiah 44:29-30)?
option1: The river Nile would turn into blood for seven days
option2: The temple of On would collapse during a solar eclipse
option3: Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt would be given into the hand of his enemies who seek his life
option4: A miraculous pillar of cloud would lead a small remnant across the Red Sea
correct: Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt would be given into the hand of his enemies who seek his life
explanation: Jeremiah 44:29-30 (KJV) - "And this shall be a sign unto you, saith the LORD ... Behold, I will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life."

question: According to Jeremiah 44:28, what proportion of the Judean refugees who entered Egypt would escape the sword and return to Judah?
option1: Two-thirds of all the families that fled to Tahpanhes
option2: None whatsoever, for total annihilation was decreed without exception
option3: All the women and children who did not burn incense
option4: A small number that shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah
correct: A small number that shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah
explanation: Jeremiah 44:28 (KJV) - "Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs."

question: What foundational theological indictment does Jeremiah deliver in Jeremiah 44:23 against the refugees' interpretation of their history?
option1: That their present calamities resulted not from abandoning the queen of heaven, but because they sinned against the Lord and disobeyed His law
option2: That they failed to offer adequate animal sacrifices along with their drink offerings
option3: That they had built altars of brick instead of unhewn stone in Pathros
option4: That their kings had made an unholy commercial treaty with Tyre
correct: That their present calamities resulted not from abandoning the queen of heaven, but because they sinned against the Lord and disobeyed His law
explanation: Jeremiah 44:23 (KJV) - "Because ye have burned incense, and because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies; therefore this evil is happened unto you, as at this day."

question: In what specific historical regnal year was the personal oracle in Jeremiah 45 delivered to Baruch the son of Neriah?
option1: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah
option2: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah king of Judah
option3: In the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
option4: In the fourteenth year of Josiah king of Judah
correct: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah
explanation: Jeremiah 45:1 (KJV) - "The word that Jeremiah the prophet spake unto Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,"

question: What lament did Baruch utter in his personal anguish recorded in Jeremiah 45:3?
option1: My heart is wounded within me, and my days are consumed like smoke
option2: Woe is me now! for the LORD hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest
option3: O that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears
option4: Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed?
correct: Woe is me now! for the LORD hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest
explanation: Jeremiah 45:3 (KJV) - "Thou didst say, Woe is me now! for the LORD hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest."

question: In Jeremiah 45:4, how does the Lord frame His sweeping cosmic dismantling of Judah to correct Baruch's self-centered perspective?
option1: I will cause the sun to go down at noon and darken the earth in the clear day
option2: The heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment
option3: Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land
option4: I will shake the nations and fill this house with glory
correct: Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land
explanation: Jeremiah 45:4 (KJV) - "Thus shalt thou say unto him, The LORD saith thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land."

question: What penetrating question and explicit prohibition did God deliver to Baruch in Jeremiah 45:5?
option1: Wilt thou contend with the Almighty? answer thou it
option2: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? boast not
option3: Canst thou draw out leviathan with a hook? fear greatly
option4: And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not
correct: And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not
explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (KJV) - "And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest."

question: What divine promise of personal preservation was granted to Baruch amid impending universal catastrophe in Jeremiah 45:5?
option1: Thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest
option2: Thou shalt inherit the vineyard of thy fathers in peace
option3: Thou shalt be appointed chief governor of Jerusalem under Babylon
option4: No plague shall come nigh thy dwelling neither shall any weapon prosper against thee
correct: Thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest
explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (KJV) - "And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest."

question: What activity was Baruch engaged in when this divine communication came to him, according to Jeremiah 45:1?
option1: Fasting and weeping in the inner court of the temple
option2: Writing these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah
option3: Carrying an official scroll of state to the king of Babylon
option4: Purchasing a parcel of land in his ancestral territory
correct: Writing these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah
explanation: Jeremiah 45:1 (KJV) - "The word that Jeremiah the prophet spake unto Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,"

question: What phrase in Jeremiah 45:5 indicates the universal scope of judgment that God was about to unleash?
option1: I will blot out man from the face of the earth
option2: The whole earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy
option3: I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD
option4: The foundations of the mountains shall melt like wax
correct: I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD
explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (KJV) - "And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest."

question: What does the expression 'thy life will I give unto thee for a prey' idiomatically signify in Jeremiah 45:5?
option1: Becoming food and game hunted down by wild beasts of the desert
option2: Receiving a large share of the plundered riches of the Babylonians
option3: Being rewarded with sacrificial animals dedicated at the sanctuary
option4: Escaping with one's bare life as the only spoil of war rescued from devastating ruin
correct: Escaping with one's bare life as the only spoil of war rescued from devastating ruin
explanation: Jeremiah 45:5 (KJV) - " ... but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest." This idiom (also given to Ebed-melech in Jer 39:18) means Baruch would survive the universal devastation with his life intact as his prize.

question: How does the agricultural and building imagery of Jeremiah 45:4 ('built will I break down ... planted I will pluck up') connect back to Jeremiah's original commission in Jeremiah 1:10?
option1: It reaffirms that God's sovereign authority overthrows nations just as Jeremiah was ordained to root out and pull down
option2: It indicates that physical farming and carpentry were banned in Judah
option3: It proves that Solomon's temple was built contrary to divine will
option4: It cancels Jeremiah's initial calling to build and plant the house of Israel
correct: It reaffirms that God's sovereign authority overthrows nations just as Jeremiah was ordained to root out and pull down
explanation: Jeremiah 45:4 (KJV) - "The LORD saith thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land." This directly echoes Jeremiah 1:10 ("to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant").

question: What pastoral and theological purpose is served by placing this brief oracle to Baruch directly before the prophecies against foreign nations in Chapters 46 to 51?
option1: It reveals that Baruch was secretly scheming to usurp Jehoiakim's royal throne
option2: It provides a profound personal anchor reminding God's faithful servant of divine sovereignty and gracious preservation prior to global judgments
option3: It marks the end of Jeremiah's prophetic career and transfers office to Baruch
option4: It serves as an official legal disclaimer exonerating Baruch from Babylonian treason
correct: It provides a profound personal anchor reminding God's faithful servant of divine sovereignty and gracious preservation prior to global judgments
explanation: Jeremiah 45:4-5 (KJV) - "The LORD saith thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land. And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest."

question: In Jeremiah 46:2, against which Egyptian army and Pharaoh was the opening oracle directed, referencing their decisive defeat by the Euphrates river at Carchemish?
option1: The army of Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt
option2: The army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt
option3: The army of Shishak king of Egypt
option4: The army of So king of Egypt
correct: The army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt
explanation: Jeremiah 46:2 (KJV) - "Against Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah."

question: In Jeremiah 46:7-8, to what natural phenomenon is Egypt's proud military mobilization compared?
option1: A raging whirlwind sweeping across the desert of Sin
option2: A consuming forest fire devouring the cedars of Lebanon
option3: A flood whose waters are moved as the rivers (like the rising Nile)
option4: A swarming cloud of locusts blotting out the midday sun
correct: A flood whose waters are moved as the rivers (like the rising Nile)
explanation: Jeremiah 46:7-8 (KJV) - "Who is this that cometh up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers? Egypt riseth up like a flood, and his waters are moved like the rivers; and he saith, I will go up, and will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and the inhabitants thereof."

question: Which three African allied nations and their specialized weaponry are summoned to Egypt's battle array in Jeremiah 46:9?
option1: Midianites, Amalekites, and Kenites that handle the javelin
option2: Philistines, Edomites, and Moabites that wield two-edged iron swords
option3: Tyrians, Sidonians, and Arvadites that steer fighting galleys
option4: Ethiopians and Libyans (Cush and Put) that handle the shield, and the Lydians (Ludim) that handle and bend the bow
correct: Ethiopians and Libyans (Cush and Put) that handle the shield, and the Lydians (Ludim) that handle and bend the bow
explanation: Jeremiah 46:9 (KJV) - "Come up, ye horses; and rage, ye chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; the Ethiopians and the Libyans, that handle the shield; and the Lydians, that handle and bend the bow."

question: How does Jeremiah 46:10 designate the battle of Carchemish from the perspective of divine judgment?
option1: The day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries
option2: The day of the great eclipse over the kingdoms of Ham
option3: The year of Babylonian plunder and worldwide tribute
option4: The feast of Moloch celebrated in the valley of Tophet
correct: The day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries
explanation: Jeremiah 46:10 (KJV) - "For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord GOD of hosts hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates."

question: What futile remedy is prescribed ironically to the 'virgin, the daughter of Egypt' in Jeremiah 46:11?
option1: Wash seven times in the waters of the Nile at dawn
option2: Go up into Gilead, and take balm; in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured
option3: Sprinkle the dust of the pyramids upon thine open wounds
option4: Consult the magicians and astrologers of On for healing incantations
correct: Go up into Gilead, and take balm; in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured
explanation: Jeremiah 46:11 (KJV) - "Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, the daughter of Egypt: in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured."

question: What scornful nickname did the fleeing mercenaries give to Pharaoh king of Egypt in Jeremiah 46:17?
option1: A broken reed that pierceth the hand of whoever leaneth on it
option2: A painted crocodile dried up in the mud of the delta
option3: Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath passed the time appointed
option4: The boasting shadow that fleeth from the sunrise
correct: Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath passed the time appointed
explanation: Jeremiah 46:17 (KJV) - "They did cry there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath passed the time appointed."

question: To which two towering landmarks does the Lord liken the imposing certainty of Nebuchadrezzar's coming in Jeremiah 46:18?
option1: As Mount Hermon in the north, and as Mount Sinai in the desert
option2: As Mount Zion in Judah, and as Mount Gerizim in Ephraim
option3: As the cedars of Lebanon, and as the oaks of Bashan
option4: As Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea
correct: As Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea
explanation: Jeremiah 46:18 (KJV) - "As I live, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts, Surely as Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come."

question: In Jeremiah 46:20-21, what animal metaphors are used to contrast Egypt and her lavishly paid foreign mercenaries?
option1: Egypt is like a very fair heifer, and her hired men are like fatted bullocks
option2: Egypt is like a graceful gazelle, and her soldiers are like ravenous wolves
option3: Egypt is like a nesting eagle, and her captains are like swift leopards
option4: Egypt is like an untamed wild ass, and her allies are like charging warhorses
correct: Egypt is like a very fair heifer, and her hired men are like fatted bullocks
explanation: Jeremiah 46:20-21 (KJV) - "Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction cometh; it cometh out of the north. Also her hired men are in the midst of her like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together: they did not stand, because the day of their calamity was come upon them, and the time of their visitation."

question: Which supreme deity of Thebes and his associated rulers does the Lord specifically promise to punish in Jeremiah 46:25?
option1: Osiris the lord of the underworld and Ptah of Memphis
option2: The multitude of No (Amon of No / Thebes), and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings
option3: Anubis the guardian of tombs and Horus the son of Isis
option4: Ra the god of Heliopolis and Apis the sacred bull
correct: The multitude of No (Amon of No / Thebes), and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings
explanation: Jeremiah 46:25 (KJV) - "The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saith; Behold, I will punish the multitude of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all them that trust in him:"

question: What tender promise of ultimate restoration and disciplined correction does the Lord grant to His covenant people at the conclusion of Chapter 46 (Jeremiah 46:27-28)?
option1: Thy borders shall extend from the Nile unto the Euphrates without tribute
option2: I will deliver Egypt into thy hands to be thy bondservants forever
option3: Fear not, O Jacob my servant ... for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure
option4: Thou shalt build up the waste places of Egypt and dwell in their fortified cities
correct: Fear not, O Jacob my servant ... for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure
explanation: Jeremiah 46:27-28 (KJV) - "Fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off ... for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished."

question: According to Jeremiah 47:1, what specific historical event provided the chronological anchor for the prophecy against the Philistines?
option1: In the year that king Ahaz died
option2: When Nebuchadrezzar burned the walls of Tyre
option3: Before that Pharaoh smote Gaza
option4: After the battle of Megiddo where Josiah fell
correct: Before that Pharaoh smote Gaza
explanation: Jeremiah 47:1 (KJV) - "The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza."

question: In Jeremiah 47:2, from what compass direction does the overwhelming judgment on Philistia arise, likened to an overflowing flood?
option1: Out of the south
option2: Across the western sea
option3: From the eastern desert
option4: Out of the north
correct: Out of the north
explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD; Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein: then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl."

question: What striking physical symptom of overwhelming terror among parents is described in Jeremiah 47:3 during the thunderous cavalry assault?
option1: The fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands
option2: Mothers shall abandon their newborn babes in the open streets
option3: The elders shall cover their faces with dust and refuse to weep
option4: Their knees shall smite together like reeds shaken in the water
correct: The fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands
explanation: Jeremiah 47:3 (KJV) - "At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, and at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands;"

question: Which two Phoenician island maritime cities would be severed from Philistine alliance and aid according to Jeremiah 47:4?
option1: Arvad and Gebal
option2: Tyrus and Zidon
option3: Berytus and Byblos
option4: Carthage and Utica
correct: Tyrus and Zidon
explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 (KJV) - "Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor."

question: From what ancestral Mediterranean origin does Jeremiah 47:4 identify the Philistines as being the remnant?
option1: The coasts of Chittim
option2: The islands of Elishah
option3: The country of Caphtor (Crete)
option4: The highlands of Seir
correct: The country of Caphtor (Crete)
explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 (KJV) - " ... for the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor."

question: What sign of extreme grief and mourning is declared to have come upon Gaza in Jeremiah 47:5?
option1: Gaza is covered with sackcloth and ashes
option2: Gaza hath put bitter wormwood upon her lips
option3: The gates of Gaza are stained with black tar
option4: Baldness is come upon Gaza
correct: Baldness is come upon Gaza
explanation: Jeremiah 47:5 (KJV) - "Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?"

question: What pagan mourning ritual practiced in the valley of Ashkelon is rebuked with the question 'how long wilt thou cut thyself?' in Jeremiah 47:5?
option1: Ritual self-laceration and cutting of flesh in grieving
option2: Walking barefoot through fields of burning thorns
option3: Burying hair shaven from the forehead under threshold stones
option4: Pouring libations of human blood before Dagon
correct: Ritual self-laceration and cutting of flesh in grieving
explanation: Jeremiah 47:5 (KJV) - "Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?"

question: What dramatic personification and desperate plea does the prophet address to God's instrument of judgment in Jeremiah 47:6?
option1: O consuming fire of Yahweh, quench thy flames and spare the weeping remnant
option2: O thou sword of the LORD, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still
option3: O arrow of the Almighty, turn aside thy flight from the innocent sucklings
option4: O great rod of anger, fall no more upon the wounded shoulders of the earth
correct: O thou sword of the LORD, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still
explanation: Jeremiah 47:6 (KJV) - "O thou sword of the LORD, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still."

question: How does the prophet himself answer why the sword of the Lord cannot be quieted in Jeremiah 47:7?
option1: Because the blood of Naboth the Jezreelite still crieth out from the soil
option2: Because the princes of Philistia have refused to pay tribute to the temple
option3: How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it
option4: Because the stars in their courses fight against the cities of the plain
correct: How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it
explanation: Jeremiah 47:7 (KJV) - "How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it."

question: What coastal geographic region is specifically designated as the target of the Lord's irrevocable charge in Jeremiah 47:7?
option1: Against Mount Carmel and the harbor of Joppa
option2: Against the plain of Sharon and the brook of Egypt
option3: Against the gulf of Aqaba and the port of Ezion-geber
option4: Against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore
correct: Against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore
explanation: Jeremiah 47:7 (KJV) - "How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it."

question: Which national god of Moab is prophesied to go into captivity along with his priests and princes in Jeremiah 48:7?
option1: Milcom
option2: Baal-zebub
option3: Nisroch
option4: Chemosh
correct: Chemosh
explanation: Jeremiah 48:7 (KJV) - "For because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together."

question: What famous curse is pronounced in Jeremiah 48:10 against anyone who fails to execute the Lord's judgment vigorously?
option1: Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood
option2: Cursed be he that removeth his neighbor's landmark in the valley of Moab
option3: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man and maketh flesh his arm
option4: Cursed be he that blesseth Chemosh in the secret chamber
correct: Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood
explanation: Jeremiah 48:10 (KJV) - "Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood."

question: In Jeremiah 48:11, what winemaking metaphor describes Moab's uninterrupted ease, complacency, and stagnant pride?
option1: Moab is as sweet must trodden under foot by the laborers in the winepress
option2: Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel
option3: Moab is like sour grapes that set the children's teeth on edge
option4: Moab is as new wine poured into old bottles that burst in pieces
correct: Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel
explanation: Jeremiah 48:11 (KJV) - "Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed."

question: To what idol shrine and false confidence of the Northern Kingdom is Moab's impending shame over Chemosh compared in Jeremiah 48:13?
option1: As Samaria was ashamed of the golden calf in Dan
option2: As Ahab was ashamed of the high places in Jezreel
option3: As the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth-el their confidence
option4: As Jeroboam was ashamed of the altar at Shechem
correct: As the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth-el their confidence
explanation: Jeremiah 48:13 (KJV) - "And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth-el their confidence."

question: What sorrowful exclamation over Moab's broken political authority and imperial splendor is uttered in Jeremiah 48:17?
option1: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
option2: How is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed!
option3: How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people!
option4: How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!
correct: How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!
explanation: Jeremiah 48:17 (KJV) - "All ye that are about him, bemoan him; and all ye that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!"

question: In Jeremiah 48:28, where are the inhabitants of Moab advised to dwell, and what nesting creature are they urged to emulate?
option1: Leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole's mouth
option2: Flee to the cedar forests and build nests like the storks in the fir trees
option3: Climb into the high cliffs and hide like the conies in the rocks
option4: Flee across the Jordan and shelter like sheep in sheepfolds
correct: Leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole's mouth
explanation: Jeremiah 48:28 (KJV) - "O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole's mouth."

question: What prominent national sin of Moab is repeatedly condemned in Jeremiah 48:29?
option1: His witchcraft and trade with the sorcerers of the east
option2: The pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart
option3: His deceitful weights and balances in merchant trade
option4: His shedding of innocent blood in the high places of Baal
correct: The pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart
explanation: Jeremiah 48:29 (KJV) - "We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart."

question: For what famous agricultural product of Moab does the prophet express deep mourning in Jeremiah 48:32?
option1: The olive orchards of Tekoa
option2: The wheat fields of Minnith
option3: The vine of Sibmah
option4: The pomegranates of Engedi
correct: The vine of Sibmah
explanation: Jeremiah 48:32 (KJV) - "O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for thee with the weeping of Jazer: thy plants are gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage."

question: What three inescapable traps await the fleeing inhabitants of Moab according to Jeremiah 48:43-44?
option1: The lion, the bear, and the serpent
option2: The sword, the famine, and the pestilence
option3: The drought, the hail, and the locust
option4: Fear, and the pit, and the snare
correct: Fear, and the pit, and the snare
explanation: Jeremiah 48:43-44 (KJV) - "Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith the LORD. He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the LORD."

question: What climactic eschatological promise concludes the judgment oracle of Moab in Jeremiah 48:47?
option1: Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the LORD
option2: Moab shall be as Sodom and her daughters as Gomorrah for all generations
option3: The name of Moab shall be blotted out from under heaven forever
option4: Moab shall be divided among the twelve tribes of Israel by lot
correct: Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the LORD
explanation: Jeremiah 48:47 (KJV) - "Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the LORD. Thus far is the judgment of Moab."

question: In Jeremiah 49:1, what indignant question did the Lord ask regarding the Ammonites occupying the ancestral territory of Gad?
option1: Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?
option2: Why have ye set up the image of Moloch in the holy borders of Benjamin?
option3: Who hath authorized Ammon to drink the wine of the vineyards of Gilead?
option4: Shall the children of Lot possess the covenant portion of Jacob forever?
correct: Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?
explanation: Jeremiah 49:1 (KJV) - "Concerning the Ammonites, thus saith the LORD; Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?"

question: What capital city of the Ammonites is prophesied to become a 'desolate heap' with her daughters burned with fire in Jeremiah 49:2?
option1: Heshbon
option2: Rabbah of the Ammonites
option3: Medeba
option4: Dibon
correct: Rabbah of the Ammonites
explanation: Jeremiah 49:2 (KJV) - "Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the LORD."

question: In the oracle against Edom, which region renowned for traditional wisdom is questioned with 'Is wisdom no more in Teman?' in Jeremiah 49:7?
option1: Dedan
option2: Bozrah
option3: Teman
option4: Sela
correct: Teman
explanation: Jeremiah 49:7 (KJV) - "Concerning Edom, thus saith the LORD of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?"

question: What tender promise of divine guardianship does the Lord insert for Edom's helpless survivors in Jeremiah 49:11?
option1: I will guide their steps across the wilderness to an oasis of palm trees
option2: Thy little ones shall be nourished by the daughters of Zion
option3: I will give them bread from heaven and water from the flinty crag
option4: Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me
correct: Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me
explanation: Jeremiah 49:11 (KJV) - "Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me."

question: In Jeremiah 49:16, how does God describe Edom's false security in its high, inaccessible mountain fortresses?
option1: O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence
option2: Thou that buildest towers upon iron crags, the fire shall consume thy lofty battlements
option3: Thy mountain peaks shall melt like wax before the scorching east wind
option4: Though thy gates be of bronze and thy walls of flint, the worm shall devour them
correct: O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence
explanation: Jeremiah 49:16 (KJV) - "Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the LORD."

question: Which ancient Syrian cities are dismayed by evil tidings as Damascus wanes and her palaces are consumed by fire in Jeremiah 49:23-27?
option1: Tyre and Sidon
option2: Hamath and Arpad
option3: Carchemish and Haran
option4: Gaza and Ekron
correct: Hamath and Arpad
explanation: Jeremiah 49:23 (KJV) - "Concerning Damascus. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad: for they have heard evil tidings: they are fainthearted; there is sorrow on the sea; it cannot be quiet."

question: Whose royal palaces in Damascus did the Lord declare would be consumed by fire in Jeremiah 49:27?
option1: The palaces of Hazael
option2: The palaces of Rezin
option3: The palaces of Ben-hadad
option4: The palaces of Hadadezer
correct: The palaces of Ben-hadad
explanation: Jeremiah 49:27 (KJV) - "And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben-hadad."

question: How are the nomadic Arabian kingdoms of Hazor characterized in Jeremiah 49:31 regarding their open, defenseless lifestyle?
option1: A people fortified behind earthen ramparts and deep trenches of water
option2: Tribes that dwell under tents of goat hair beneath the cedars of Lebanon
option3: Warriors who ride upon swift camels armed with two-edged swords
option4: A nation that dwelleth without care, which have neither gates nor bars, which dwell alone
correct: A nation that dwelleth without care, which have neither gates nor bars, which dwell alone
explanation: Jeremiah 49:31 (KJV) - "Arise, get you up unto the wealthy nation, that dwelleth without care, saith the LORD, which have neither gates nor bars, which dwell alone."

question: In Jeremiah 49:35, what primary weapon and source of military prowess did the Lord threaten to break concerning Elam?
option1: The bow of Elam, the chief of their might
option2: The bronze spears of the mountain archers
option3: The iron chariots of Susa
option4: The heavy cavalry of the eastern plains
correct: The bow of Elam, the chief of their might
explanation: Jeremiah 49:35 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might."

question: What eschatological promise of ultimate restoration concludes the oracle against Elam in Jeremiah 49:39?
option1: Elam shall build an altar unto the LORD by the river Ulai
option2: In the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the LORD
option3: The sons of Elam shall be cupbearers in the temple of Jerusalem
option4: Elam shall never be conquered by the kings of Media
correct: In the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the LORD
explanation: Jeremiah 49:39 (KJV) - "But it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the LORD."

question: Which chief Babylonian deities are declared confounded and broken in pieces at the fall of Babylon in Jeremiah 50:2?
option1: Nabu is confounded, Nergal is broken in pieces
option2: Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces
option3: Ishtar is confounded, Tammuz is broken in pieces
option4: Sin is confounded, Shamash is broken in pieces
correct: Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces
explanation: Jeremiah 50:2 (KJV) - "Declare ye among the nations, and publish, and set up a standard; publish, and conceal not: say, Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces; her idols are confounded, her images are broken in pieces."

question: In Jeremiah 50:4-5, how are the returning children of Israel and Judah described as they seek the Lord their God?
option1: Marching with trumpets and harps, rejoicing in the spoils of the Chaldeans
option2: Bearing the vessels of gold and silver with royal banners flying
option3: Going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the LORD their God. They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant
option4: Demanding vengeance upon the borders of Edom and Moab
correct: Going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the LORD their God. They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant
explanation: Jeremiah 50:4-5 (KJV) - "In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together, going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the LORD their God. They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten."

question: According to Jeremiah 50:6, what had caused the Lord's people to become 'lost sheep' who forgot their resting place?
option1: The fierce wolves of Assyria had driven them into desert pits
option2: A great drought had dried up all the pastures of Gilead
option3: They followed the false stars and sorceries of Egypt
option4: Their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains
correct: Their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains
explanation: Jeremiah 50:6 (KJV) - "My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace."

question: Which two successive imperial powers are identified in Jeremiah 50:17 as having ravaged and broken the bones of scattered Israel?
option1: First the king of Assyria devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones
option2: First Pharaoh-necho of Egypt, and last Cyrus the Persian
option3: First the princes of Syria, and last the governors of Ammon
option4: First the Philistines of Caphtor, and last the Edomites of Mount Seir
correct: First the king of Assyria devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones
explanation: Jeremiah 50:17 (KJV) - "Israel is a scattered sheep; the lions have driven him away: first the king of Assyria hath devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones."

question: What lush pastures will Israel feed upon when restored to his habitation according to Jeremiah 50:19?
option1: The plains of Sharon and the valley of Jezreel
option2: Carmel and Bashan, and Mount Ephraim and Gilead
option3: The hills of Hebron and the meadows of Jericho
option4: The banks of the Jordan and the heights of Hermon
correct: Carmel and Bashan, and Mount Ephraim and Gilead
explanation: Jeremiah 50:19 (KJV) - "And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead."

question: What remarkable promise of complete pardoning of sin is declared in Jeremiah 50:20?
option1: Their sins shall be cast into the depths of the Euphrates river
option2: A new sacrifice of bullocks and rams shall atone for them every morning
option3: The iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve
option4: Their transgressions shall be remembered only until the year of jubilee
correct: The iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve
explanation: Jeremiah 50:20 (KJV) - "In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve."

question: What symbolic military title is given to Babylon in Jeremiah 50:23 before it was cut asunder and broken?
option1: The iron shield of the nations
option2: The golden crown of the east
option3: The roaring lion of the desert
option4: The hammer of the whole earth
correct: The hammer of the whole earth
explanation: Jeremiah 50:23 (KJV) - "How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!"

question: How does Jeremiah 50:34 describe Israel's divine Redeemer in contrast to Babylonian oppression?
option1: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name: he shall throughly plead their cause
option2: Their Redeemer is a silent watchman waiting for the dawn
option3: Their Redeemer is as an archer shooting unseen arrows from the clouds
option4: Their Redeemer is a merciful king riding upon a white horse
correct: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name: he shall throughly plead their cause
explanation: Jeremiah 50:34 (KJV) - "Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name: he shall throughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the land, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon."

question: Why is a drought declared upon the waters of Babylon in Jeremiah 50:38?
option1: Because they diverted the sacred waters of the Gihon spring
option2: For it is the land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols
option3: Because their canals were contaminated with toxic bitumen
option4: Because they withheld water from thirsty Jewish captives
correct: For it is the land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols
explanation: Jeremiah 50:38 (KJV) - "A drought is upon her waters; and they shall be dried up: for it is the land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols."

question: To what legendary catastrophic divine judgment is Babylon's permanent desolation compared in Jeremiah 50:40?
option1: As the flood in the days of Noah that destroyed all flesh
option2: As the destruction of the tower of Babel on the plains of Shinar
option3: As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof
option4: As the plagues of hail and darkness that smote the land of Pharaoh
correct: As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof
explanation: Jeremiah 50:40 (KJV) - "As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the LORD; so shall no man abide there, neither shall any son of man dwell therein."

question: In Jeremiah 51:1-2, what will the Lord raise up against Babylon to winnow her and empty her land?
option1: A flaming fire, and hewers of wood that shall cut her down
option2: An overflowing river, and fishermen that shall cast nets
option3: A destroying wind, and fanners that shall fan her
option4: A swarm of locusts, and cankerworms that shall devour her vines
correct: A destroying wind, and fanners that shall fan her
explanation: Jeremiah 51:1-2 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against them that dwell in the midst of them that rise up against me, a destroying wind; And will send unto Babylon fanners, that shall fan her, and shall empty her land: for in the day of trouble they shall be against her round about."

question: In Jeremiah 51:7, what metallic vessel is Babylon compared to in the hand of the Lord that intoxicated the earth?
option1: A silver flagon filled with bitter gall and wormwood
option2: A brazen cauldron boiling with fury and blood
option3: An earthen jar broken into thirty pieces of pottery
option4: A golden cup in the LORD's hand, that made all the earth drunken
correct: A golden cup in the LORD's hand, that made all the earth drunken
explanation: Jeremiah 51:7 (KJV) - "Babylon hath been a golden cup in the LORD's hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad."

question: Whose spirit did the Lord raise up to execute His device to destroy Babylon, fulfilling 'the vengeance of his temple' (Jeremiah 51:11)?
option1: The spirit of the kings of the Medes
option2: The spirit of the princes of Greece
option3: The spirit of the governors of Ethiopia
option4: The spirit of the chieftains of Scythia
correct: The spirit of the kings of the Medes
explanation: Jeremiah 51:11 (KJV) - "Make bright the arrows; gather the shields: the LORD hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes: for his device is against Babylon, to destroy it; because it is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance of his temple."

question: What military instrument does God address in Jeremiah 51:20-23, using it to shatter nations, horses, chariots, and rulers?
option1: Thou art my two-edged sword of judgment
option2: Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war
option3: Thou art my mighty spear dipped in oil
option4: Thou art my iron rod of chastisement
correct: Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war
explanation: Jeremiah 51:20 (KJV) - "Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms;"

question: In Jeremiah 51:25, what geographic metaphor does the Lord apply to Babylon as He threatens to roll it down from the rocks?
option1: O cedar of Lebanon ... I will strip thy branches and cast thy trunk into the sea
option2: O deep abyss ... I will stop thy fountains and burn thy reeds
option3: O destroying mountain ... I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain
option4: O great wall of brass ... I will crumble thy mortar into fine dust
correct: O destroying mountain ... I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain
explanation: Jeremiah 51:25 (KJV) - "Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the LORD, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain."

question: How does Jerusalem describe Nebuchadrezzar's ravenous consumption of her in Jeremiah 51:34?
option1: He hath torn me like a lion of Bashan and left my bones in the field
option2: He hath trodden me like grapes in a winepress until my blood flowed to the horses' bridles
option3: He hath plucked my feathers like an eagle and delivered me to foreign fowlers
option4: He hath devoured me, he hath crushed me ... he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates
correct: He hath devoured me, he hath crushed me ... he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates
explanation: Jeremiah 51:34 (KJV) - "Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me, he hath crushed me, he hath made me an empty vessel, he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates, he hath cast me out."

question: What fate is prophesied for the massive architectural defenses of Babylon in Jeremiah 51:58?
option1: The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire
option2: Her hundred brass gates shall be carried away into the land of Elam
option3: Her hanging gardens shall be submerged beneath the sands of the wilderness
option4: Her ziggurat towers shall be toppled into the waters of the canal
correct: The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire
explanation: Jeremiah 51:58 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the people shall labour in vain, and the folk in the fire, and they shall be weary."

question: Whom did Jeremiah commission to carry the scroll of doom to Babylon when he traveled with King Zedekiah in his fourth year (Jeremiah 51:59)?
option1: Baruch the son of Neriah the scribe
option2: Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, a quiet prince
option3: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
option4: Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest
correct: Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, a quiet prince
explanation: Jeremiah 51:59 (KJV) - "The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And this Seraiah was a quiet prince."

question: What dramatic prophetic sign was Seraiah commanded to perform after reading the scroll in Babylon (Jeremiah 51:63-64)?
option1: Burn it with fire on an altar dedicated to the God of Abraham
option2: Bury it under the foundation brick of the palace of Nebuchadnezzar
option3: Bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates, saying, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise
option4: Tear it into twelve pieces and scatter them upon the four winds
correct: Bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates, saying, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise
explanation: Jeremiah 51:63-64 (KJV) - "And it shall be, when thou hast made an end of reading this book, that thou shalt bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates: And thou shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her: and they shall be weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah."

question: What exact editorial note marks the formal conclusion of Jeremiah's prophetic oracles at the end of Jeremiah 51:64?
option1: Amen and Amen: the vision is sealed
option2: Here endeth the prophecy of the weeping seer
option3: Written and completed by Baruch the scribe
option4: Thus far are the words of Jeremiah
correct: Thus far are the words of Jeremiah
explanation: Jeremiah 51:64 (KJV) - "And thou shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her: and they shall be weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah."

question: How old was Zedekiah when he began to reign in Jerusalem, and what was his mother's name according to Jeremiah 52:1?
option1: Eighteen years old; Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem
option2: Twenty-five years old; Zebudah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah
option3: Sixteen years old; Jecoliah of Jerusalem
option4: One and twenty years old; Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah
correct: One and twenty years old; Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah
explanation: Jeremiah 52:1 (KJV) - "Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah."

question: On what specific calendar date did Nebuchadrezzar begin his final siege of Jerusalem in Zedekiah's ninth year (Jeremiah 52:4)?
option1: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month
option2: In the fourth year of his reign, in the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month
option3: In the eleventh year of his reign, in the fifth month, in the seventh day of the month
option4: In the seventh year of his reign, in the third month, in the fifteenth day of the month
correct: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month
explanation: Jeremiah 52:4 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it, and built forts against it round about."

question: Where was Zedekiah overtaken by the Chaldean army after he fled the broken city by night (Jeremiah 52:8)?
option1: At the ford of the Jabbok
option2: In the plains of Jericho
option3: In the wilderness of Engedi
option4: Near the waters of Merom
correct: In the plains of Jericho
explanation: Jeremiah 52:8 (KJV) - "But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him."

question: What horrific judgments were inflicted upon Zedekiah at Riblah in the land of Hamath according to Jeremiah 52:10-11?
option1: He was stripped naked and forced to walk behind Nebuchadrezzar's chariot across the desert
option2: He was cast into a furnace of fire along with his chief royal counselors
option3: The king of Babylon slew his sons and all the princes of Judah before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon
option4: He was hanged on a gallows fifty cubits high in the sight of all the Chaldeans
correct: The king of Babylon slew his sons and all the princes of Judah before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon
explanation: Jeremiah 52:10-11 (KJV) - "And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah. Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death."

question: Which Babylonian commander burned the house of the Lord, the king's house, and broke down the walls of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 52:12-14?
option1: Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag
option2: Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim
option3: Nebushasban, Rab-saris
option4: Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard
correct: Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard
explanation: Jeremiah 52:12-14 (KJV) - "Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard, which served the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem, And burned the house of the LORD, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem ... And all the army of the Chaldeans ... brake down all the walls of Jerusalem round about."

question: According to Jeremiah 52:21-22, what were the physical dimensions and decorative details of the two bronze pillars (Jachin and Boaz)?
option1: The height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, a fillet of twelve cubits compassed it, the thickness was four fingers, hollow; and a chapiter of brass of five cubits with network and ninety-six pomegranates
option2: The height was thirty cubits, thirty cubits around, solid bronze with figures of cherubim and palm trees
option3: The height was twelve cubits, eight cubits around, two fingers thick with golden lily work
option4: The height was twenty-four cubits, sixteen cubits around, with carved wreaths of cedar wood
correct: The height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, a fillet of twelve cubits compassed it, the thickness was four fingers, hollow; and a chapiter of brass of five cubits with network and ninety-six pomegranates
explanation: Jeremiah 52:21-23 (KJV) - "And concerning the pillars, the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits; and a fillet of twelve cubits did compass it; and the thickness thereof was four fingers: it was hollow. And a chapiter of brass was upon it; and the height of one chapiter was five cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the chapiters round about ... And there were ninety and six pomegranates on a side; and all the pomegranates upon the network were an hundred round about."

question: Which chief religious leaders of the temple were captured and executed by the king of Babylon at Riblah according to Jeremiah 52:24-27?
option1: Pashur the chief governor of the house of the Lord and Hananiah the prophet
option2: Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door
option3: Hilkiah the high priest and Ahikam the scribe
option4: Azariah the high priest and Jonathan the royal recorder
correct: Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door
explanation: Jeremiah 52:24-27 (KJV) - "And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door ... And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land."

question: What total number of Jewish exiles carried captive to Babylon across three deportations is officially recorded in Jeremiah 52:28-30?
option1: Ten thousand men of valor
option2: Forty-two thousand three hundred and threescore
option3: Four thousand and six hundred persons
option4: Seven thousand seven hundred persons
correct: Four thousand and six hundred persons
explanation: Jeremiah 52:28-30 (KJV) - "This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons: In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzar-adan ... carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred."

question: In the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's captivity, which Babylonian king ascended the throne and graciously released him from prison (Jeremiah 52:31)?
option1: Belshazzar king of Babylon
option2: Neriglissar king of Babylon
option3: Labashi-marduk king of Babylon
option4: Evil-merodach king of Babylon
correct: Evil-merodach king of Babylon
explanation: Jeremiah 52:31 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison,"

question: What royal honors and provisions were bestowed upon exiled King Jehoiachin until the day of his death according to Jeremiah 52:32-34?
option1: Spake kindly unto him, set his throne above the kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, fed him continually at his table, and gave him a daily allowance all the days of his life
option2: Granted him an army to return and rebuild the destroyed temple walls in Jerusalem
option3: Appointed him satrap over the provinces of Syria and Phoenicia
option4: Restored the sacred gold vessels of Solomon to his personal custody
correct: Spake kindly unto him, set his throne above the kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, fed him continually at his table, and gave him a daily allowance all the days of his life
explanation: Jeremiah 52:32-34 (KJV) - "And spake kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon, And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life. And for his diet, there was a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life."
